intro:
Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Tether USDT is what arrives on Ethereum mainnet.

Base is chain 8453, an Ethereum L2, and the gas coin there is ETH. The USDC you send is Circle's contract 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan. Ethereum is chain 1, blocks are about 12 seconds, and the USDT you should see is Tether's contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Both tokens use 6 decimals on these chains, but the issuers differ. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native gas, and it is not either asset on this route.
description: Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on mainnet. Match both contracts on Basescan and Etherscan too.

sections.heading: Two issuers, one dollar word
sections.body: Circle issues the USDC that leaves Base. Tether issues the USDT that arrives on Ethereum. A shared price near one dollar is not a shared contract. If a lender, a payroll file, or a pool asked for Circle dollars on Ethereum, they mean 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, and this route will not credit it. Maker DAI is a third token, with 18 decimals and a different issuer. Read the quote symbol against the issuer you can redeem with.

sections.heading: What Basescan and Etherscan each show
sections.body: Approve USDC on Base only if the spender matches the router on the quote and the cap matches the size you intend. After you sign, the Base hash stays on Basescan. The USDT credit is a separate fact on Etherscan, sent to your wallet at Tether's contract. A bridge wait sits on top of those 12 second blocks, and nothing here promises how long that wait runs. The handoff itself is explained in [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work).

sections.heading: When this hop is the wrong job
sections.body: Stay on Base if the buyer of your dollars is already there. Crossing to Ethereum only to swap back pays gas twice and adds a second contract check. Skip this page if you need native ETH on Ethereum for fees, because USDT cannot pay gas. Skip it if the wallet is still on chain 8453 while you search Etherscan, since the balance will look empty until the network changes.

sections.heading: Two ETH balances, neither is the swap
sections.body: ETH on Base pays the approval and the send. ETH on Ethereum pays whatever you do with USDT afterward. Those balances do not merge just because the ticker is ETH. If the minimum on the quote is worse than you will accept, do not sign. When a quote expires, request another one. This page is not a price lock.

faqs.question: Is Ethereum USDT the same token as Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Tether's USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not Circle's USDC. If the other side of your trade named Circle, use a route that delivers Ethereum USDC instead. Maker DAI is different again. This page fits only when Tether's Ethereum token is the balance you meant to hold.

faqs.question: Do I approve USDC on Base before this swap?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the wallet asks. USDC on Base is an ERC-20, so the router needs an allowance before it can pull tokens. The native-gas placeholder is not the asset you spend here, so there is no gas-coin transfer in place of that approval. Read the spender and the allowance cap before you confirm.

faqs.question: Will the USDT I receive pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. USDT is an ERC-20 from Tether. Gas on chain 1 is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds. The ETH you hold on Base, chain 8453, does not pay mainnet fees. If Ethereum ETH is empty, you can see the USDT on Etherscan and still be unable to move it.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to DAI on Ethereum. You spend Circle USDC on Base and you take delivery of Maker DAI on Ethereum.

The token that leaves is Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Confirm it on Basescan. Base is chain 8453, and you pay ETH there because Base is an L2, not a separate gas coin. What arrives is Maker's DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain 1 and a block is about 12 seconds. DAI uses 18 decimals. USDC uses 6. The native-gas placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not DAI and not USDC.
description: Swap USDC from Base to DAI on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Base and Maker DAI arrives on mainnet. DAI has 18 decimals. USDC has 6. Check Etherscan now.

sections.heading: Maker's dollar, not Circle's
sections.body: DAI is minted through Maker's system. It is not a Circle IOU and it is not Tether's USDT. People treat it as a dollar because the peg is designed to hold, not because the contract is USDC with a new name. A desk that redeems at Circle cannot redeem this DAI at Circle. If your instructions said USDT, this page is the wrong asset even when the price on the screen is close.

sections.heading: Decimals change the figure you expect
sections.body: A balance of 100 USDC is 100000000 base units. A balance of 100 DAI is 100 followed by 18 zeros. Wallets usually hide that, and a raw explorer transfer may not. If you compare base units across this route, the numbers will look wildly different for the same dollar amount. Read the human amount on the quote, then match the token contract, not the integer width.

sections.heading: Wrong route, named plainly
sections.body: Do not use this page to wrap or unwrap ETH. Do not use it if you wanted Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Do not use it if you wanted to keep Circle USDC and only change chains. A local swap on Base, if the DAI you want is already listed there, avoids the bridge. Crossing chains is justified when the DAI balance has to sit on Ethereum.

sections.heading: How to follow the payment
sections.body: The steps for signing and tracking a hop are in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). You still verify the two contracts yourself: source on Basescan, DAI on Etherscan. Leave ETH on Base for gas. Leave ETH on Ethereum so the DAI is not stuck as a balance you cannot send. The bridge wait is separate from the 12 second block time, and it is not promised here.

faqs.question: Is DAI just USDC under another ticker?
faqs.answer: No. USDC is issued by Circle and uses 6 decimals. DAI is issued through Maker and uses 18 decimals. The Ethereum contract for this route is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. If a counterparty said Circle or Tether, this arrival token will not satisfy that instruction. Compare the contract on Etherscan before you mark the invoice paid.

faqs.question: Why does the raw amount look so much larger?
faqs.answer: DAI's 18 decimal places make the base-unit integer bigger than USDC's 6 decimal places for a similar dollar value. The wallet should show the human amount. If you are reading an event log on Etherscan, divide by 10 to the 18th for DAI and by 10 to the 6th for the USDC you sent from Base.

faqs.question: Can I send this DAI back by reversing the same transaction?
faqs.answer: A confirmed send is not reversed from this page. DAI, once credited on Ethereum, is a new balance at the Maker contract. Moving it back to Base is a separate quote, with its own gas in ETH on chain 1 and its own minimum. If that return quote is worse than you accept, do not sign it.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to ETH on Ethereum. What leaves is Circle USDC. What arrives is native ETH, the gas coin, on Ethereum.

You send Circle USDC from 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453, and you can inspect that contract on Basescan. You receive native ETH on Ethereum, chain 1. The address field for that native coin is the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is not an ERC-20 you open as a token page. Etherscan shows the ETH balance on the account itself. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. ETH here is not WETH.
description: Swap USDC from Base to ETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Base and native ETH, the gas coin, arrives on mainnet. It is not WETH. Confirm it on Etherscan.

sections.heading: Native ETH is the arrival, not a receipt token
sections.body: On Ethereum the gas coin and the asset you are buying are the same ETH. That is unusual next to stablecoin routes, where the arrival token cannot pay fees. You still should not empty the idea of gas: the ETH has to land, and a later transaction spends some of it. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a different asset. If a contract call demands that WETH address, this route has not finished the job.

sections.heading: The placeholder is not a contract to approve
sections.body: Interfaces write 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE when they mean the chain's native coin. On this route it marks Ethereum ETH, the thing that arrives. It does not mark the USDC you send. USDC still needs an ERC-20 approval on Base if the router must pull it. Do not paste the placeholder into a token search and expect a Circle or Tether page.

sections.heading: Use mainnet notes, not the L2 balance
sections.body: Chain details for the destination sit on [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum). Your Base ETH balance, which pays gas on chain 8453, is not the ETH this swap is buying. After arrival, look at the Ethereum account on Etherscan, not at the USDC token page. If you only wanted to sell USDC for ETH inside Base, you do not need this hop at all.

sections.heading: When to refuse the quote
sections.body: Refuse this route if you need Tether, Maker DAI, or Circle USDC to remain the dollar you hold. Refuse it if the wallet network is Arbitrum, Polygon, or Base while you are checking the result, because native ETH balances are per chain. Refuse it if the minimum received, after fees, is less ETH than you will accept. There is no promised clock on the bridge wait.

faqs.question: Does the ETH I receive count as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin, represented here by 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. WETH is the ERC-20 at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Pools that accept only WETH will not see this balance until you wrap it in a separate transaction. Wrapping is not part of this route. Check Etherscan for the account balance, not for a WETH token credit.

faqs.question: Where do I look on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Look at your address on Ethereum, chain 1, not at a token contract for the arrival. Native ETH is the account balance. The USDC you spent is the Circle contract on Basescan, 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. A Base transaction hash will not be the Ethereum receipt. Switch the wallet to chain 1 before you decide the funds are missing.

faqs.question: I still have USDC on Base. Did this route miss it?
faqs.answer: This route only spends the USDC you put in the quote. USDC left in the wallet stays on Base. If you never signed, nothing moved. If you signed and the Base send is confirmed, wait for the Ethereum ETH credit and do not send a second swap just because the L2 balance has not changed yet.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to WETH on Ethereum. Base sends Circle USDC away, and Ethereum credits canonical WETH rather than loose ETH.

Circle USDC on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Check it on Basescan before you approve. Base is chain 8453, an L2, and gas is ETH. Canonical WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Check that on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain 1, with blocks around 12 seconds. WETH is an ERC-20 claim on ETH. It is not the gas coin, and it is not the Base WETH predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006.
description: Swap USDC from Base to WETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Base and canonical WETH arrives on mainnet. WETH does not pay gas until you unwrap it there.

sections.heading: Why the WETH contract exists
sections.body: Ethereum applications often cannot hold native ETH inside the same interface they use for tokens, so they use WETH. Depositing ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 mints WETH. Withdrawing burns WETH and returns ETH. This route buys that wrapped token from a USDC sale on Base. It does not call deposit on Base, and it does not leave you with spendable gas on Ethereum by itself.

sections.heading: Base WETH is a different deployment
sections.body: On Base, wrapped ETH lives at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. That contract cannot satisfy an Ethereum mainnet pool. If your goal was only to wrap ETH you already hold on Base, do that wrap on Base and stop. If your goal was native ETH on Ethereum, the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the arrival you wanted, and this page is wrong.

sections.heading: Gas you still have to own
sections.body: You pay ETH on Base to approve USDC and to send the swap. You need ETH on Ethereum later to approve WETH or to unwrap it. WETH sitting at the canonical contract will not pay those fees. [Trade on Base](/chains/base) is the source chain, and the source gas never migrates with the token. The bridge does not publish a completion time.

sections.heading: A short refusal list
sections.body: Refuse the quote if the other side asked for Tether USDT or Maker DAI. Refuse it if they asked for Circle USDC on Ethereum. Refuse it if you confused WBTC with ETH: WBTC is a bitcoin receipt, not this asset, and it is not native bitcoin either. Refuse it if the minimum WETH is too small for the USDC you are spending.

faqs.question: Can I pay Ethereum gas with the WETH from this swap?
faqs.answer: Not directly. WETH is an ERC-20. Validators and wallets take native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, for gas on chain 1. You unwrap WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 only after you already have a little ETH to pay for that unwrap. Plan that ETH separately. A WETH balance alone does not broadcast the next transaction.

faqs.question: Is Base WETH at 0x4200...0006 the token I will receive?
faqs.answer: No. That address is wrapped ETH on Base, chain 8453. This route spends Base USDC and delivers Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, which you verify on Etherscan. Holding the Base WETH contract does not mean the mainnet position is open. Basescan and Etherscan are showing two different deployments of wrapped ether.

faqs.question: What if the app I am funding only accepts native ETH?
faqs.answer: Then this route stops one step early. You would still unwrap WETH on Ethereum, and that unwrap is a separate transaction with its own gas. If native ETH was the goal, choose the route that delivers the gas coin instead of the WETH contract. Unwrapping also needs a little native ETH already on chain 1.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Base, and Circle USDC is what arrives on Ethereum.

The asset you spend is native ETH on Base. Interfaces label it 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and that string is a stand-in for the gas coin, not a token contract on Basescan. Base is chain 8453, an L2. The USDC you receive is Circle's Ethereum contract 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain 1, and blocks take about 12 seconds. This USDC is 6 decimals. It is not Tether and not Maker DAI.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Base and Circle USDC arrives on mainnet. Confirm the USDC contract on Etherscan before signing.

sections.heading: You are spending the gas coin
sections.body: On Base, ETH pays fees and, on this route, ETH is also the asset being sold. If you spend the entire balance, the transaction cannot pay for itself. Leave enough ETH on chain 8453 for the network fee. There is no ERC-20 approval for native ETH. If the wallet asks you to approve WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, you are on a different route than this one.

sections.heading: Circle on Ethereum, specifically
sections.body: The arrival contract is the long-standing Circle USDC on mainnet. It is not a bridged IOU with a similar name, and it is not USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. A treasury that whitelists only that Circle address will reject other dollar tokens even when the price matches. Read 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan and compare it with the quote before you sign.

sections.heading: L2 ETH is not already mainnet ETH
sections.body: Holding ETH on Base does not mean you hold ETH on Ethereum. This swap sells the Base balance for dollars on mainnet. You do not arrive with native ETH on chain 1. You arrive with USDC, which cannot pay Ethereum gas. Fund a little mainnet ETH by some other means if you must move the USDC after it lands. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) describes the separation between the two receipts.

sections.heading: Skip this page when
sections.body: Skip it if you wanted to move ETH and keep ETH. Skip it if the dollar you need is Tether or DAI. Skip it if a Base application already pays you in USDC and you never needed mainnet. Skip it if the quote's minimum USDC is below your floor. The block interval is about 12 seconds. The bridge wait on top of that is not a number this page will invent.

faqs.question: Does native ETH on Base need an approval?
faqs.answer: No. The 0xEeee placeholder means the gas coin, and gas coins are sent, not approved. You do need to leave some ETH behind so the fee can be paid. If the only ETH you have is WETH, an ERC-20, this native route will not see that balance until you unwrap it on Base.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract should Etherscan show?
faqs.answer: Circle's Ethereum USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. A credit at any other dollar contract, including Tether or DAI, is a different trade. The source side is not a USDC transfer. It is native ETH leaving Base, chain 8453, which you trace on Basescan as a value transfer.

faqs.question: Will I have ETH for gas on Ethereum after this?
faqs.answer: Not from this route. You sold Base ETH and bought USDC. USDC does not pay gas on chain 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds once you do have ETH to spend. Bring a small ETH balance to Ethereum before you try to transfer the USDC out.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Ethereum. You sell native ETH on Base and you receive Tether USDT on Ethereum.

Native ETH on Base is written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That value is the gas coin on chain 8453, visible on Basescan as the account balance, not as an ERC-20 page. Tether USDT on Ethereum is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Open it on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain 1 and a block is about 12 seconds. USDT here has 6 decimals. It is not Circle USDC and it is not WETH.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on mainnet. USDT has 6 decimals and cannot pay Ethereum gas fees.

sections.heading: Selling the fee token on purpose
sections.body: This route only makes sense when you want Tether's dollar more than you want Base ETH. Because the thing you sell is also the fee token, size the send so the remainder still covers gas on Base. A wallet that shows zero ETH after you type the amount will fail before any bridge starts. WETH is not a substitute input. ETH and WETH are different balances even on the same chain.

sections.heading: Tether's contract, including its rough edges
sections.body: Ethereum USDT is an old token. Its transfer does not behave like a textbook ERC-20 in every tool, and Tether can freeze listed addresses. Neither fact makes a random USDT copy acceptable. The contract on the quote must be 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. If your counterparty freezes or rejects Tether, Circle USDC is the other major dollar, and this page does not deliver it.

sections.heading: What you will not hold at the end
sections.body: You will not hold native ETH on Ethereum merely because you started with ETH on Base. You will not hold Maker DAI. You will not hold WBTC, and WBTC would not have been native bitcoin anyway. You hold USDT, an ERC-20, on chain 1. Moving it requires ETH you did not buy in this swap.

sections.heading: Tracking without a shared hash
sections.body: Basescan records the ETH leaving chain 8453. Etherscan records USDT arriving on chain 1. Those are two pages. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through that split. Do not resend because the Ethereum token page is still quiet while the Base debit is already final. The extra wait is the bridge, and it has no promised length.

faqs.question: Is the USDT I receive able to pay mainnet fees?
faqs.answer: No. Fees on Ethereum are native ETH. USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is Tether's token, 6 decimals, and wallets cannot use it as gas. Your Base ETH was the input, so it is gone if you sold it. Keep a separate mainnet ETH balance before you try to transfer the USDT.

faqs.question: What if the wallet wants me to approve ETH?
faqs.answer: Native ETH is not approved. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stands for the gas coin on Base, chain 8453. An approval popup for a token means the selected input is an ERC-20 such as WETH or USDC, which is a different route. Recheck the asset line on the quote.

faqs.question: I wanted Circle dollars. Is this close enough?
faqs.answer: No. Circle's Ethereum USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Tether is a different company and a different contract. Price proximity is not acceptance by a whitelist. If the written instruction says USDC, leave this page. A whitelist that names Circle will reject Tether even when both prices sit near a dollar.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to DAI on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Base, and Maker DAI is the token that arrives on Ethereum.

You spend the Base gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain 8453. Basescan shows that as ETH leaving the account. You receive DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Etherscan is the explorer for that contract. Ethereum is chain 1, with roughly 12 second blocks. DAI is Maker's token and uses 18 decimals. It is not Circle USDC, not Tether USDT, and not WETH.
description: Swap ETH from Base to DAI on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Base and Maker DAI arrives on mainnet. DAI uses 18 decimals and is not Circle USDC or Tether.

sections.heading: What Maker changes about the dollar
sections.body: DAI is created in Maker's credit system and kept near a dollar by that system. Circle and Tether are companies that issue fiat-backed tokens. If your risk rule says only fiat-issued stables, DAI fails the rule even when the quote looks like a dollar sale. The contract check is simple: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, or you are looking at the wrong token.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals and a gas coin input
sections.body: The input has 18 decimals because ETH does. The output has 18 decimals because DAI does. That coincidence does not make them the same unit. One ETH is not one DAI. Read the quote in human amounts. Also leave ETH on Base. Selling the full gas balance strands the transaction before it is broadcast.

sections.heading: Wrong when the destination app disagrees
sections.body: A money market that lists USDC will not treat this DAI as a deposit of USDC. A contract that wants WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 will not treat DAI as wrapped ether. A request for native ETH on Ethereum is the opposite trade. And if you only needed DAI on Base, bridging to mainnet is an extra hop you can skip.

sections.heading: Settlement notes for this pair
sections.body: Chain 1 is the place the DAI will show, and [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) collects the mainnet context. The source debit is on Basescan. You will need ETH on Ethereum to move DAI later, because DAI is not gas. Block time is about 12 seconds. That figure is not a promise for when the bridge credits you.

faqs.question: Is DAI redeemable at Circle or Tether?
faqs.answer: No. DAI is Maker's token at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Circle redeems USDC. Tether redeems USDT. If your treasury policy names one of those companies, this route delivers the wrong instrument, even though the price is quoted near one dollar. Holding DAI means you accepted Maker's system, not a fiat redemption window at those two firms.

faqs.question: Why is the base-unit number so large on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals. A transfer of 250 DAI is 250 times 10 to the 18th in the event log. Compare that with the human amount in the wallet, not with the 6-decimal integer you may remember from USDC. The input side is native ETH on Base, which also uses 18 decimals, and the prices still differ.

faqs.question: Do I unwrap anything at the end?
faqs.answer: No unwrap is required to hold DAI. Unwrapping is a WETH action. This route never delivers WETH. It delivers Maker DAI on Ethereum. You only need a little native ETH on chain 1 afterward if you want to send that DAI somewhere else. If the app asked for WETH, you are on the wrong page.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to WETH on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Base, and canonical WETH arrives on Ethereum, which is not the same as wrapping in place.

The ETH you send is the gas coin on Base, chain 8453, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows the account, not a token contract. The WETH you receive is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain 1 and blocks are about 12 seconds. Wrapping on Base would have minted 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and stayed on Base. That is a different action.
description: Swap ETH from Base to WETH on Ethereum. Native Base ETH leaves and canonical WETH arrives on mainnet. Local wrapping on Base is a different action entirely.

sections.heading: This is not the wrap button
sections.body: A wrap on Base takes native ETH and gives you Base WETH at the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. You stay on chain 8453. You can unwrap there and get Base ETH back. This page does something else. It sells or bridges that value toward Ethereum and credits canonical WETH on mainnet. If you only needed a tokenized ETH balance for a Base app, stop and wrap locally.

sections.heading: Canonical WETH still cannot pay gas
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. Ethereum miners and validators are paid in native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, not in WETH. After this route you can hold a large WETH balance and still be unable to unwrap it if the Ethereum account has no ETH. Get a small gas balance onto chain 1 before you depend on the unwrap.

sections.heading: When the route mismatches the order
sections.body: It is the wrong route if the order says native ETH on Ethereum. It is wrong if the order says USDC, USDT, or DAI. It is wrong if someone said bitcoin: WBTC is not native bitcoin, and this route does not deliver WBTC either. It is wrong if your input balance is already Base WETH, because this page spends unwrapped ETH.

sections.heading: Read both explorers in order
sections.body: Start on Basescan and confirm ETH left the account on chain 8453. Then open Etherscan and look for WETH at the canonical contract, not for a rise in the native ETH line. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the short version of why those receipts differ. Do not treat 12 second blocks as a delivery promise.

faqs.question: If I wrap on Base, do I get this WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Wrapping on Base credits 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain 8453. This route credits 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum, which you check on Etherscan. The tickers match. The contracts and the chains do not. If the app you are funding lives on Base, the local wrap is the whole task.

faqs.question: Will the WETH that arrives pay the next Ethereum fee?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is not gas. Native ETH is gas, and the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is how interfaces refer to it. You need some of that native coin on chain 1 before you can unwrap or approve the WETH you just received. Until that gas coin is present, the WETH can sit on Etherscan and still be immovable.

faqs.question: I meant to keep ETH, not sell it into a wrapper on another chain. What now?
faqs.answer: Do not sign. A local wrap on Base keeps you on Base. A route that delivers native ETH on Ethereum keeps the gas coin as the gas coin. This page is only right when canonical mainnet WETH is the balance an application asked for. A local wrap leaves you on Base with a different contract.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Ethereum. Base WETH leaves chain 8453, and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum mainnet.

The input is wrapped ETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, an ERC-20 you can open on Basescan. Native ETH, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, is a different balance. If the wallet only holds the gas coin, this route has nothing to spend until you wrap. The output is Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain 1, and blocks are about 12 seconds. That USDC has 6 decimals. It is not Tether and it is not Maker DAI.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Ethereum. Base WETH leaves and Circle USDC arrives on mainnet. The input is an ERC-20, so the wallet will ask for an approval.

sections.heading: Allowance, then the hop
sections.body: WETH on Base cannot be pulled until you grant the router an allowance. Read the spender and the cap. An unlimited allowance is optional, not required by the route. If you reject that signature, the swap cannot start. Native gas transfers do not ask for this, which is how you can tell the input is the wrapper. The approval itself is paid in ETH on chain 8453. [Trade on Base](/chains/base) is the network the wallet must show while you sign.

sections.heading: Circle on mainnet, six decimals
sections.body: The arrival contract is the USDC address many desks already whitelist. Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 will not pass that check, and neither will DAI. One USDC is 1,000,000 base units because the token uses 6 decimals. If an event log shows an 18 decimal integer, you are looking at a different contract than the one on this quote.

sections.heading: When the WETH route is a mismatch
sections.body: Do not use this page if the Base balance is still native ETH. Do not use it to unwrap and keep ETH on Base. Do not use it for USDT or DAI. Do not use it if the USDC only needs to exist on Base for a local app. WBTC is not part of the trade, and WBTC would not be native bitcoin even if it were.

sections.heading: Ethereum fees are a separate coin
sections.body: USDC cannot pay fees on chain 1. ETH spent as gas on Base does not reappear on Ethereum. Put a little ETH on mainnet before you plan to forward the USDC. Etherscan shows the credit only after the bridge completes, and this page does not time that wait. If the minimum USDC is below your floor, leave the quote unsigned.

faqs.question: Does Base WETH need an approval on this route?
faqs.answer: Yes. The input 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is an ERC-20, so the router needs an allowance before it can take the tokens. Native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, is not the input and is not approved. You still spend a little of that gas coin to pay for the approval and the send on Base.

faqs.question: Is the USDC that arrives the 6 decimal Circle token?
faqs.answer: Yes. The destination is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, chain 1, which you check on Etherscan. It is Circle's USDC, 6 decimals, not Tether and not Maker DAI. A credit at any other dollar contract means you are looking at a different trade than this quote. Match the address before you treat the invoice as paid.

faqs.question: My Base balance is native ETH, not WETH. Can I use this page?
faqs.answer: Not until you wrap. This route only sees WETH at the Base predeploy. Native ETH stays the gas coin until a wrap mints the ERC-20. If you wanted to sell the gas coin itself for USDC, choose the native ETH route instead of approving a token you do not hold.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Ethereum. You send Base WETH and you receive Tether USDT on Ethereum mainnet.

Confirm the source on Basescan: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, chain 8453, an L2 where gas is still ETH. Confirm the destination on Etherscan: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, chain 1, about 12 seconds a block. That contract is Tether, 6 decimals. It is not Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and it is not canonical WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native gas, which you are not delivering.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Ethereum. Base WETH leaves and Tether USDT arrives on mainnet. USDT is 6 decimals and cannot pay gas fees on Ethereum too.

sections.heading: Tether is the point of the trade
sections.body: People pick this route when a venue, a market, or a payment rail settles in Tether rather than Circle. The price can look identical and the contract still be wrong. Tether also operates a freeze list. If an address is blocked, holding the right contract does not make the balance useful. That is a property of this token, not a reason to accept a lookalike USDT from a different deployer.

sections.heading: What the allowance is allowing
sections.body: You are allowing a router to move Base WETH, not to move Ethereum USDT in advance. The USDT does not exist in your wallet yet. After the hop, a later Ethereum app may ask for a second approval, and that one is paid with mainnet ETH. Mixing those two requests up is how people approve the wrong chain. This page does not ask you to approve USDT in order to receive it.

sections.heading: Wrong job, listed without decoration
sections.body: Wrong if you need Circle's redemption contract. Wrong if you need DAI from Maker, which has 18 decimals and a different issuer. Wrong if the input is native ETH and you have not wrapped. Wrong if you wanted Ethereum WETH so a pool can pair it. Wrong if both sides of the deal are already on Base. The bridge is justified when the Tether balance must sit on Ethereum.

sections.heading: Two explorers, no shared clock
sections.body: Basescan shows WETH leaving. Etherscan shows USDT arriving. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the reason those pages do not share a transaction hash. Block time on Ethereum is about 12 seconds. The bridge adds its own wait, and that wait is not stated as a duration here. Refresh the quote if it expires. Do not sign a minimum you would not accept.

faqs.question: Will this USDT be frozen just because it crossed from Base?
faqs.answer: Crossing does not by itself freeze a balance. Tether can still freeze addresses under its own rules, on the contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. If your address is already listed, do not expect this route to produce a spendable balance. Circle USDC is a different issuer and a different contract if your policy cannot use Tether.

faqs.question: Do I approve USDT on Ethereum before it arrives?
faqs.answer: No. You approve Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 so the router can take the input. USDT is the output. An approval of USDT would only matter later, if an Ethereum app needs to pull those tokens, and that signature would be on chain 1, paid in ETH.

faqs.question: Is Base WETH the same contract as Ethereum WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Base uses 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Ethereum canonical WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route spends the Base contract and does not deliver the Ethereum one. It delivers Tether USDT, which you verify on Etherscan. ETH and WETH remain different assets on both chains, and this quote buys neither of them on mainnet.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to DAI on Ethereum. Wrapped ETH leaves Base, and Maker DAI is what you receive on Ethereum.

Spend 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453, and check that token on Basescan. Receive 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum, chain 1, and check it on Etherscan. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. DAI is Maker's token and uses 18 decimals, the same width as WETH and a different price. USDC and USDT on Ethereum use 6 decimals, so a raw unit comparison with those dollars will mislead you. Native gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is not the token you are buying.
description: Swap WETH from Base to DAI on Ethereum. Base WETH leaves and Maker DAI arrives on mainnet. DAI has 18 decimals and is not a Circle or Tether token at all.

sections.heading: Same decimal width, different asset
sections.body: Both WETH and DAI use 18 decimals, so the integers in an event log can look cousin to each other. They are not. One wrapped ether is not one DAI. Read the human amounts on the quote. DAI holds a peg by Maker's system. It is not a claim you redeem at Circle, and it is not Tether. A policy that only allows fiat-issued stables should stop on this page.

sections.heading: The wrapper has to be spendable first
sections.body: If your ether on Base is still the gas coin, wrap it into 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 before this route can see it. After it is wrapped, the router needs an allowance. Rejecting the allowance stops the trade cleanly. There is no partial burn of WETH from a signature you declined.

sections.heading: Where this route wastes the hop
sections.body: It wastes the hop if the DAI market you want is already on Base. It is the wrong token if the counterparty wrote USDC or USDT. It is the wrong shape if they wrote native ETH or canonical WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. It is also the wrong mental model if someone called the destination bitcoin. WBTC is not native bitcoin, and this quote does not deliver WBTC.

sections.heading: Follow-through on mainnet
sections.body: The signing order is covered in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). Afterward you still need ETH on Ethereum to move DAI, because DAI is not gas. Basescan will not display the DAI credit. Etherscan will. Leave the quote if the minimum DAI, given the ETH price, is a discount you will not take. No fill time is offered here.

faqs.question: Why do WETH and DAI logs look numerically similar?
faqs.answer: Both tokens use 18 decimals, so a transfer of 1 unit is 10 to the 18th in base units for each. The prices are unrelated. One WETH is not one DAI. Read the wallet amount, then confirm the contract on Etherscan is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and not a 6 decimal stable by mistake.

faqs.question: Is DAI the same kind of dollar as USDC?
faqs.answer: No. USDC is Circle and uses 6 decimals. DAI is Maker and uses 18 decimals. Tether is a third issuer. If the instruction names Circle or Tether, this arrival will not match it. The source token is Base WETH, not Base USDC, so you are also selling ether exposure.

faqs.question: What pays gas after the DAI arrives?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum, chain 1. DAI cannot pay it, and the ETH you hold on Base, chain 8453, is a separate balance. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds once you have that gas coin. The bridge wait before the DAI shows on Etherscan is not the same figure and is not promised.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to ETH on Ethereum. Base WETH leaves, and native ETH on Ethereum mainnet is what arrives.

You are not unwrapping in place. Unwrapping on Base would return the gas coin on chain 8453 and never create a mainnet balance. This route takes WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, visible on Basescan, and delivers native ETH on Ethereum. Interfaces write that arrival as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Etherscan shows it as the account balance, not as a token contract. Ethereum is chain 1, with blocks around 12 seconds. Canonical WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a different result.
description: Swap WETH from Base to ETH on Ethereum. Base WETH leaves and native ETH arrives on mainnet. That is not an in-place unwrap, and it is not canonical WETH.

sections.heading: Local unwrap versus this hop
sections.body: A local unwrap burns Base WETH and credits Base ETH. You can pay Base fees with the result. This page sends the wrapped position toward Ethereum and credits the gas coin there. If a Base app needs ETH, the bridge is the long way around. If an Ethereum app needs the gas coin, the local unwrap never leaves chain 8453 and cannot help.

sections.heading: The arrival can pay fees, the input could not travel as gas
sections.body: WETH is an ERC-20 and needs an approval on Base. Native ETH on Ethereum is the fee token, so once it arrives it can pay for later mainnet transactions. Do not assume the amount that arrives is sized as spare gas. Fees vary, and the quote's minimum is the floor, not a promise that surplus remains after the next transfer.

sections.heading: Refuse it for these orders
sections.body: Refuse it if the order is canonical WETH on Ethereum. Refuse it if the order is USDC, USDT, or DAI. Refuse it if your Base balance is already native ETH, because this page cannot spend the gas coin. Refuse it if the wallet network is still Base while you look for the result on Etherscan. The balance is per chain.

sections.heading: Where to read the result
sections.body: Account pages on Etherscan, not the WETH token page, are the arrival record. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the chain context for what that ETH can do next. The debit is on Basescan. Twelve second blocks describe Ethereum's cadence. They do not describe how long the bridge takes. If the quote expires, take a new one instead of signing stale numbers.

faqs.question: Is receiving native ETH the same as receiving WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Etherscan shows it on the account. WETH is the ERC-20 at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. A pool that only accepts that contract will ignore the native balance until you wrap it on Ethereum. Wrapping is a separate step after the native coin arrives.

faqs.question: Can I just unwrap Base WETH and call that this swap?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 returns ETH on Base, chain 8453. This route delivers ETH on Ethereum, chain 1. The tickers match and the chains do not. Basescan and Etherscan will show different account histories for the two actions. A local unwrap never creates the Ethereum balance this page is about.

faqs.question: Does the ETH that arrives pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: It is the gas coin, so it can, once it is credited. Spend some of it on a later transaction and the rest is what you keep. The input side still needed its own ETH on Base to pay for the WETH approval and the send. Those two ETH balances are not one pool of funds.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Tether-pegged USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

The USDC you send is Circle's Base contract 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, 6 decimals, on Basescan. Base is chain 8453, an L2, and gas is ETH. The USDT you receive is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. BNB Chain is chain 56, blocks are about 3 seconds, and gas is BNB. That USDT is the 18 decimal Binance-pegged token, often called BSC-USD. It is not the 6 decimal Tether contract on Ethereum. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native gas, not this USDT.
description: Swap USDC from Base to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base and 18 decimal USDT arrives on chain 56. That USDT is not Ethereum's 6 decimal Tether.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals is the trap
sections.body: A holder who knows Ethereum USDT expects 6 decimals. This BNB Chain token uses 18. The wallet should show a similar dollar amount, but a script that divides by 1,000,000 will be wrong by a factor of a trillion. Read 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan and check the decimals field before you automate anything. The source USDC really is 6 decimals. The destination is not.

sections.heading: BNB is the new gas coin
sections.body: ETH on Base pays the send. It does not pay fees on chain 56. After USDT arrives you need BNB, the native coin, to transfer it. Arriving USDT does not include BNB. If the account on BNB Chain is empty of BNB, the dollars can sit visible on BscScan and still be stuck. Fund gas before you depend on a forward transfer.

sections.heading: Use a different route when
sections.body: Use a different route if you need Ethereum mainnet USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Use a different route if you need BNB itself, or the pegged ETH token, rather than a dollar. Use a different route if you meant to keep Circle USDC and only change chains. Stay on Base if the buyer of USDC is already there.

sections.heading: Chain 56 is its own book
sections.body: Notes for the destination are on [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc). Three second blocks are the chain cadence, not a bridge promise. Basescan records the USDC debit. BscScan records the USDT credit. Do not resubmit because those hashes differ. If the minimum received is poor, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is BNB Chain USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and uses 6 decimals. This route delivers 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain 56, which uses 18 decimals. Check it on BscScan. Treating them as one contract will break a payment or a script even when the ticker says USDT. Read the decimals field on BscScan before you automate the credit.

faqs.question: What do I need in the wallet after the swap?
faqs.answer: BNB, the gas coin on chain 56. USDT cannot pay those fees. The ETH you used on Base, chain 8453, does not transfer over as gas. The native-gas placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means BNB on this destination, and this route is not delivering that placeholder. It is delivering the USDT contract.

faqs.question: Should I approve USDC on Base?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the wallet asks. Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is an ERC-20, so the router needs an allowance. Review the spender and the cap. The approval is signed on Base and costs ETH. It does not approve anything on BNB Chain. You still need BNB on chain 56 later, because the USDT you receive cannot pay gas.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base, and pegged ETH arrives as a BEP-20 token, not as gas.

Send Circle USDC from 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453. Read it on Basescan. Receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain, chain 56. Read it on BscScan. That contract is Binance-pegged ETH. It is not native ETH, it is not WETH, and it does not pay fees. Fees on BNB Chain are BNB. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE would mean BNB on this chain, and this route does not deliver it.
description: Swap USDC from Base to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base and pegged ETH arrives as a BEP-20. It is not native ETH and it does not pay gas fees.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH is a token with a familiar ticker
sections.body: On Ethereum, ETH is the gas coin. On BNB Chain, the token named ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a pegged asset. You can trade it. You cannot pay a validator with it. WETH is yet another contract and is not what this quote buys. If a help page told you to get ETH for gas, it meant BNB, and this route will not solve that problem.

sections.heading: What you still spend on Base
sections.body: USDC is an ERC-20, so expect an approval, paid in ETH on chain 8453. Leave enough ETH for that fee. The USDC contract must match Circle's Base deployment before you trust the spender. A copied USDC with the same ticker is not this input.

sections.heading: The route is wrong in four common cases
sections.body: It is wrong if you wanted native ETH on Ethereum, chain 1. It is wrong if you wanted BNB so you can move tokens on chain 56. It is wrong if you wanted USDT or to keep USDC. It is wrong if you wanted WETH on Base at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Selling dollars for pegged ETH only makes sense when a BNB Chain app asked for that BEP-20.

sections.heading: How the receipt splits
sections.body: [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains why Basescan and BscScan do not share one hash. Look for the USDC debit on Base, then the pegged ETH credit on BscScan at the contract above. Three second blocks are not a delivery promise. Keep BNB on the destination account or the new ETH token cannot be transferred.

faqs.question: Can I pay BNB Chain fees with this ETH?
faqs.answer: No. The token at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is pegged ETH, a BEP-20. Gas on chain 56 is BNB, the native coin, which interfaces sometimes write as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You need that BNB separately. This route sells USDC for the pegged token and does not include the gas coin.

faqs.question: Is this the same ETH I would receive on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum ETH is the gas coin on chain 1, and you would see it as an account balance on Etherscan. This arrival is a token on BscScan. It is also not WETH. If the order says mainnet ETH or canonical WETH, leave this page.

faqs.question: Which contract do I check for the USDC I send?
faqs.answer: Circle's Base USDC, 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, on Basescan. Base is chain 8453 and the fee for the send is ETH. The destination check is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan, chain 56, where blocks are about 3 seconds. That token is pegged ETH, not the gas coin, so you still need BNB to move it.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base, and native BNB is the coin that arrives.

You spend Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453, an L2 with ETH gas. Basescan shows that contract. You receive native BNB on chain 56. The address field for that coin is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, a placeholder for the gas coin, not a BEP-20 page on BscScan. BscScan shows BNB on the account. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a different asset and is not the result.
description: Swap USDC from Base to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base and native BNB arrives on chain 56. BNB is the gas coin, not pegged ETH. Confirm it on BscScan.

sections.heading: You are buying the fee token
sections.body: On BNB Chain the useful fee balance is BNB. This route sells Base USDC and credits that native coin. That is different from buying USDT or pegged ETH, which then sit useless until BNB is added. Because the arrival is gas, later transfers can spend it. The amount is still whatever the quote delivers, not a calculated stipend for a month of fees.

sections.heading: The placeholder means BNB only on chain 56
sections.body: The same 0xEeee string on Base means ETH. On Ethereum it means ETH. On BNB Chain it means BNB. Pasting that string into a search will not open a token contract, because there is no ERC-20 behind it. If a form shows that placeholder as the output, you are buying the native coin of the selected chain. Confirm the chain id is 56 before you sign.

sections.heading: Skip the swap if the order disagrees
sections.body: Skip it if the order is pegged ETH. Skip it if the order is USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Skip it if you need Circle USDC to remain USDC. Skip it if you are on Ethereum and thought BNB was a token there. Also skip it if you would rather sell USDC for ETH and stay on Base.

sections.heading: Signing and checking
sections.body: The click path is in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains). You still match the USDC contract on Basescan yourself. Afterward, open the account on BscScan and read the BNB line, not a token dropdown. Leave ETH on Base so the approval and the send can be paid. The 3 second block time is not a promise for the bridge.

faqs.question: Does the 0xEeee address on this route mean ETH or BNB?
faqs.answer: On the destination it means BNB, the gas coin of chain 56. The same placeholder on Base means ETH, which is what you use to pay for the USDC approval. It is not a contract you open on BscScan. Pegged ETH, if that is what you wanted, is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 instead.

faqs.question: Will I receive a BEP-20 called BNB?
faqs.answer: You receive native BNB, which BscScan shows as the account balance. You do not receive the pegged ETH token, and you do not receive USDT. If a dapp asks for a token contract rather than the gas coin, this route has not given it that contract.

faqs.question: What if I have no ETH left on Base?
faqs.answer: Then you cannot pay the Base fee, chain 8453, and the swap will not broadcast. USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 cannot pay gas. Keep a little ETH beside the USDC you intend to sell. The BNB you are buying does not exist on Base to pay that fee.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDC on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Base, and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

The ETH you sell is the gas coin on Base, chain 8453, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows it on the account, not as a token. Leave some of it for the fee or the transaction cannot be sent. The USDC you receive is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. That is Binance-pegged USDC with 18 decimals, not Circle's 6 decimal USDC on Ethereum or Base. BNB Chain is chain 56, blocks about 3 seconds, and the gas coin there is BNB.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDC on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Base and 18 decimal pegged USDC arrives on chain 56. It is not Circle's 6 decimal USDC on BscScan.

sections.heading: Pegged USDC is not the Circle contract you may know
sections.body: Circle's Base USDC is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 and uses 6 decimals. Circle's Ethereum USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, also 6 decimals. The token this route credits uses 18 decimals and a Binance peg. A treasury whitelist copied from Ethereum will not recognize 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Check the decimals on BscScan before you report the balance to accounting.

sections.heading: You are selling the Base fee token
sections.body: There is no ERC-20 approval for native ETH. There is a requirement to keep enough ETH to pay the Base fee. If you type the entire balance, the wallet should warn you. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is not accepted by this page. Unwrap first if that is all you hold.

sections.heading: Four reasons to close the tab
sections.body: Close it if you need Circle's own USDC contract. Close it if you need Tether at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Close it if you need BNB for gas and thought USDC would cover fees. Close it if you meant to buy ETH on Ethereum rather than sell ETH from Base. A BNB Chain app that specifically wants this pegged dollar is the case that fits.

sections.heading: Destination gas is BNB
sections.body: USDT and USDC on chain 56 cannot pay fees, and neither can the ETH you no longer hold on Base. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the right place to remember that BNB is mandatory. BscScan is the explorer for the credit. Three second blocks are the chain, not the bridge. Do not sign a minimum you dislike.

faqs.question: Is this the same USDC Circle issues on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Base Circle USDC is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 and has 6 decimals. This route delivers 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, an 18 decimal pegged token, which you check on BscScan. A whitelist built for Circle's contract will miss it. Accounting that assumes 6 decimals will also misread the 18 decimal balance on BscScan.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH before selling it?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH on Base is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is sent rather than approved. You must leave enough to pay the fee on chain 8453. If the wallet asks you to approve WETH, the selected input is the wrapper, which is a different route.

faqs.question: Can the USDC I receive pay BNB Chain gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain 56 is BNB. Pegged USDC is a BEP-20. Blocks are about 3 seconds when you do have BNB to spend. Bring BNB to the account before you try to move the dollars. The ETH sold from Base does not become that BNB.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDT on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Base, and 18 decimal USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

The ETH you sell is the gas coin on Base, chain 8453, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows that as the account balance. Keep enough ETH to pay the fee. There is no token approval for native ETH. The USDT you receive is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan, chain 56, where blocks are about 3 seconds. It uses 18 decimals. Ethereum's Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, uses 6. Gas after arrival is BNB, not ETH and not USDT.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDT on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Base and 18 decimal USDT arrives on chain 56. It is not Ethereum's 6 decimal Tether contract.

sections.heading: You are spending the Base fee coin
sections.body: Type less than the full ETH balance. The remainder pays the chain 8453 fee. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 will not be picked up by this route. If that wrapper is what you hold, unwrap it or switch to the WETH page. Selling ETH here is deliberate: you give up Base gas in exchange for a dollar token on another chain.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimal USDT versus the one on Ethereum
sections.body: BscScan's decimals field on 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 should read 18. A payment script copied from Ethereum that assumes 6 decimals will mis-state the amount by twelve orders. The ticker can still say USDT. Tether's mainnet contract is a different deployment. Do not paste 0xdAC17 into a BNB Chain transfer and expect this balance to move.

sections.heading: BNB is still missing unless you add it
sections.body: USDT cannot pay fees on chain 56. The ETH you sold lived on Base and does not become BNB. Before you forward the dollars, the account needs native BNB. Interfaces write that gas coin as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE only when the selected network is BNB Chain. On Base the same string means ETH, which is what you are selling.

sections.heading: Close this page if the order says otherwise
sections.body: Close it for Circle USDC, including the 18 decimal peg at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d if that specific contract was required, and also for Circle's own 6 decimal contracts. Close it if you wanted pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Close it if you wanted to keep ETH. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the destination context. Three second blocks are not a bridge promise.

faqs.question: Is this the 6 decimal USDT from Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and has 6 decimals. This route delivers 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, chain 56, with 18 decimals. Check that on BscScan. A shared ticker does not make the contracts interchangeable for payments or for scripts. Open the decimals field before you copy an amount from a mainnet habit.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH on Base before this swap?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and you send it rather than approve it. You do have to leave enough on chain 8453 to pay the fee. An approval popup means the wallet thinks you are spending an ERC-20 such as WETH, which is a different route.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay fees once it arrives?
faqs.answer: No. Fees on BNB Chain are BNB. USDT is a BEP-20. Blocks are about 3 seconds when BNB is available to spend. The ETH you sold from Base does not refill that BNB balance. Fund BNB before you try to move the dollars off the account.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to BNB on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Base, and native BNB is what arrives on chain 56.

Both sides use the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and that string is not one asset. On Base, chain 8453, it means ETH, the L2 gas coin, which you can see on Basescan as the account balance. On BNB Chain, chain 56, it means BNB, which BscScan shows as the account balance. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. Pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a BEP-20 and is not what this quote buys. Leave some Base ETH for the fee.
description: Swap ETH from Base to BNB on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Base and native BNB arrives on chain 56. The shared 0xEeee label is a different coin on each chain.

sections.heading: One label, two coins
sections.body: Wallets reuse 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for whatever the chain uses as gas. If you copy that string into a token list you will not find a contract, because native coins are not ERC-20s. The chain id in the wallet is the real selector: 8453 sells ETH, 56 receives BNB. Signing while the wallet still shows Ethereum mainnet, chain 1, would be a different trade entirely.

sections.heading: Do not drain Base
sections.body: This route sells the same coin that pays the Base fee. A max click can fail before any bridge message is sent. There is no approval step for native ETH. If your balance is WETH, this page will not see it. Unwrap on Base first, or use the WETH-to-BNB route, which is an allowance plus a different quote.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH is the usual mix-up
sections.body: Someone asking for ETH on BNB Chain often means 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. That token cannot pay fees. Someone asking for ETH on Ethereum means the gas coin on chain 1, which this route does not deliver. Someone asking for USDT or USDC should not be on this page at all. WBTC is unrelated, and it is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: How to confirm you bought gas
sections.body: After the Base debit, open the account on BscScan and read the BNB line. A token transfer of pegged ETH means you used another route. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers why the hashes differ. Three second blocks describe chain 56, not the bridge wait. Reject the quote if the minimum BNB is too small.

faqs.question: Why do both tokens show the same address?
faqs.answer: Interfaces use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a stand-in for the native gas coin of whichever chain is selected. On Base that coin is ETH. On BNB Chain it is BNB. The string is not a contract on Basescan or BscScan. Chain ids 8453 and 56 keep the balances apart.

faqs.question: Is the BNB I receive able to pay fees?
faqs.answer: Yes. BNB is the gas coin on chain 56, and blocks there are about 3 seconds. The amount is whatever the quote delivers, not a reserved fee budget. You still had to keep some ETH on Base, chain 8453, to pay for the send. That Base remainder does not migrate.

faqs.question: I wanted the ETH token on BNB Chain, not BNB. Is this it?
faqs.answer: No. The BEP-20 named ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. It is pegged ETH, not WETH, and it cannot pay gas. This page delivers native BNB. If a dapp asked for that pegged contract, switch routes before you sign. Native BNB is the gas coin, and pegged ETH will not run a transaction on chain 56.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDC on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves, and 18 decimal pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

The input is the ERC-20 at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Confirm it on Basescan and expect an approval. Native ETH, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, is not this input. The output is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan, chain 56, about 3 second blocks. That USDC is Binance-pegged and uses 18 decimals. Circle's Base USDC, 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, uses 6 and is a different product. You will need BNB to move the result.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDC on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves and 18 decimal pegged USDC arrives on chain 56. It is not Circle's 6 decimal USDC on BscScan.

sections.heading: Approval on the wrapper only
sections.body: The router must be allowed to move Base WETH. Read the spender and set a cap you accept. That signature is mined on chain 8453 and costs ETH. It does not pre-approve the USDC on BNB Chain. If you decline it, nothing is bridged. If the wallet offers no WETH balance, you are holding native ETH and this page cannot spend it.

sections.heading: Decimals and the whitelist problem
sections.body: Eighteen decimal pegged USDC will not match a Circle whitelist copied from Ethereum or Base. Those Circle contracts use 6 decimals. Accounting exports that divide by 1,000,000 will inflate this balance. Read the decimals on BscScan for 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d before you book it. The word USDC on the quote is not a promise of Circle redemption.

sections.heading: When this WETH sale is the wrong job
sections.body: It is the wrong job if you hold native ETH and have not wrapped. It is wrong if you need Circle's 6 decimal USDC on Base at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 or on Ethereum at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. It is wrong if you need Tether, native BNB, or pegged ETH. It is wrong if a Base app already accepts WETH and you had no reason to leave chain 8453.

sections.heading: BNB after the dollars land
sections.body: Pegged USDC cannot pay chain 56 fees. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) shows the signing order, and you still check both contracts yourself. Basescan records the WETH debit. BscScan records the USDC credit. Three second blocks are the chain cadence, not a promised arrival. If the minimum on the quote is too low, do not sign.

faqs.question: Does this USDC match Circle's Base contract?
faqs.answer: No. Circle on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 and uses 6 decimals. This route delivers 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, an 18 decimal pegged token on BscScan. A whitelist or a script built for Circle will not treat them as the same coin, even though both use the USDC ticker. Check the decimals on BscScan before you book the credit.

faqs.question: What if my Base balance is native ETH?
faqs.answer: This page cannot spend it. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and the input here is WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Wrap first, then approve, or switch to the route that sells native ETH. The wrap stays on Base until you take that second step.

faqs.question: What pays fees on BNB Chain after USDC arrives?
faqs.answer: BNB, the native coin on chain 56. Pegged USDC cannot pay them. Blocks are about 3 seconds once BNB is in the account. ETH used as gas on Base does not convert into that BNB. Fund it separately or the dollars sit on BscScan without a way to move.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDT on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves, and 18 decimal USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

Approve and spend 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan is the explorer, and gas for that approval is ETH. Receive 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, chain 56. BscScan should show 18 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 has 6 decimals and is not this balance. Native gas is the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning ETH on Base and BNB on the destination. You are buying neither native coin.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDT on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves and 18 decimal USDT arrives on chain 56. That token is not the 6 decimal Tether contract on Ethereum.

sections.heading: Wrapper in, wide-unit dollar out
sections.body: WETH uses 18 decimals. This BNB Chain USDT also uses 18. The integers can look comparable in a log and still represent a price, not a one-for-one unit. Read the human amounts. The source is wrapped ether, so you are exiting ETH exposure. The destination is a pegged dollar. Treating the raw integers as equal is how a review misprices the fill.

sections.heading: An Ethereum USDT address will not see this credit
sections.body: Paste 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 into a mainnet watch list and the BNB Chain balance will stay invisible. The credit lives on chain 56, at the 18 decimal contract, on BscScan. If a counterparty sent you an Ethereum address and an Ethereum USDT contract, this route does not pay them. You would still need a separate hop to mainnet.

sections.heading: Wrong when the goal was simpler
sections.body: Wrong if you only wanted to unwrap WETH and keep ETH on Base. Wrong if the input is still native ETH. Wrong if you need Circle USDC, pegged or native. Wrong if you need BNB itself so you can pay fees. Wrong if you need pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. The fit is a BNB Chain venue that settles in this USDT contract.

sections.heading: Split receipts
sections.body: The Base side is an ERC-20 debit of WETH. The BNB Chain side is a BEP-20 credit of USDT. [Trade on Base](/chains/base) is the source network that must be selected while you approve. Blocks on chain 56 are about 3 seconds. That cadence is not the bridge's duration. Bring BNB before you try to forward the USDT. Decline a minimum you will not accept.

faqs.question: Do I approve WETH, USDT, or both?
faqs.answer: You approve Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 so the router can take the input. You do not approve USDT in order to receive it. A later BNB Chain app may ask for a USDT allowance, and that signature would be on chain 56, paid in BNB. Keep those two requests on their own chains.

faqs.question: Why does this USDT use 18 decimals?
faqs.answer: The contract 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain is an 18 decimal pegged token. Ethereum's Tether uses 6. Check the decimals field on BscScan instead of assuming the mainnet width. A script that scales by 1,000,000 will not report this balance correctly. The source token is Base WETH, which you approve on chain 8453, not on BNB Chain.

faqs.question: Can I start from native ETH on Base?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and pays gas on chain 8453. This route only spends WETH. Wrap on Base first if the wrapper is what you meant to sell, or choose the native ETH route if you want to sell the gas coin directly.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to ETH on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves, and pegged ETH arrives as a BEP-20 on BNB Chain.

Spend wrapped ETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. That contract is on Base, chain 8453, and Basescan is where you read the approval. Receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain 56. BscScan lists it as pegged ETH. It is not native ETH, it is not WETH, and it cannot pay fees. Native BNB is the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on this destination, and this quote does not deliver that placeholder. Blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds.
description: Swap WETH from Base to ETH on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves and pegged ETH arrives as a BEP-20. It cannot pay gas. Native BNB is a different gas coin entirely.

sections.heading: The ETH you receive cannot run a transaction
sections.body: On Ethereum, ETH pays gas. On Base, ETH pays gas. On BNB Chain, the token people call ETH is a peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Moving it costs BNB. If the reason you wanted ETH was to pay fees, you bought the wrong asset. WETH on Ethereum, 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, is also not this token.

sections.heading: A local unwrap never reaches BscScan
sections.body: Burning Base WETH returns Base ETH on chain 8453. You stay on an L2, and you can spend that ETH on Base fees. This route is justified only when a BNB Chain application asked for the pegged ETH contract. If you simply wanted spendable ETH where you already are, unwrap and stop.

sections.heading: BNB was the gas order
sections.body: Orders that say get ETH for gas on BNB Chain are asking for native BNB. Orders that say get ETH on Ethereum are asking for chain 1. Orders that say USDT or USDC are asking for dollars. All three should leave this page. WBTC is not a substitute either, and WBTC is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: What to open on BscScan
sections.body: Open the pegged contract, not the account's BNB line, if you want to see the credit. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) states that fees are BNB. The debit of WETH is on Basescan. Do not resend because the hashes differ. There is no promised bridge duration on top of the 3 second blocks. Keep the quote's minimum in view before you sign.

faqs.question: Is pegged ETH the same as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH on Base is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, and that is the input you spend. WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The output here is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan, a pegged BEP-20. None of those three contracts is native BNB. If you needed the gas coin, buy BNB instead of this pegged token.

faqs.question: Will this ETH pay BNB Chain fees?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain 56 is BNB, often labeled 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in interfaces. Pegged ETH cannot be used as that fee. You need BNB in the account before the new token can be transferred. Base ETH used to approve WETH does not fill that gap. Chain 56 blocks are about 3 seconds only after that BNB is already there.

faqs.question: What if I only hold native ETH on Base?
faqs.answer: Then wrap it into 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 before this route can see a balance, or pick a route that sells native ETH directly. Native ETH is the gas coin on chain 8453 and is not an ERC-20 approval. This page assumes the wrapper is already in the wallet.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to BNB on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves, and native BNB is the coin that arrives.

The token you approve is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453, checked on Basescan. The coin you receive is native BNB on chain 56, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. BscScan shows that as the account balance, not as a token contract. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is the lookalike people open by mistake. Unwrapping WETH on Base would have returned ETH on Base instead of BNB.
description: Swap WETH from Base to BNB on BNB Chain. Base WETH leaves and native BNB arrives on chain 56. That is the gas coin, not pegged ETH and not a local unwrap.

sections.heading: Wrapped ether becomes another chain's gas
sections.body: You give up an ERC-20 claim on ETH and you receive the fee coin of BNB Chain. After it lands, transfers on chain 56 can spend it. The quote decides the amount. It is not sized as a stipend, and a small fill can still be eaten by the next few transactions. Read the minimum before you treat the result as spare gas.

sections.heading: The approval stays on Base
sections.body: Only the WETH allowance is signed on chain 8453, and it costs ETH. If you have no ETH beside the WETH, you cannot pay that approval. Native BNB does not exist on Base to help. If you decline the allowance, the router cannot pull the wrapper and the hop does not start.

sections.heading: Same placeholder, different coin
sections.body: On Base, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means ETH. On BNB Chain it means BNB. Seeing that string on both lines of the quote does not mean you are moving one coin unchanged. You are selling wrapped ETH for a different native coin. Confirm chain id 56 on the destination side before you sign.

sections.heading: Do not call this an unwrap
sections.body: An unwrap burns 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and credits ETH on Base. This page credits BNB on BscScan. Use the unwrap when a Base app needs the gas coin. Use this route when a BNB Chain app needs BNB. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing outline, not a timer. No arrival duration is stated here.

faqs.question: Does this route deliver pegged ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. This route delivers native BNB, shown on the account, and labeled 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in the quote. If a contract call needs the pegged ETH address, you are on the wrong page. BscScan will show BNB on the account line, not inside that pegged contract.

faqs.question: Is unwrapping Base WETH enough?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping returns ETH on Base, chain 8453, at the gas-coin balance. It does not create BNB on chain 56. This route spends 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and credits BNB, which you verify on BscScan. The local unwrap and this hop solve different problems. Stay with the unwrap only when the ETH must remain on Base.

faqs.question: What do I need on Base besides WETH?
faqs.answer: A little native ETH to pay for the approval and the send. WETH cannot pay Base gas until it is unwrapped, and unwrapping would take you off this route. Chain 8453 is an L2. The BNB you are buying cannot pay that Base fee because it is not on Base yet.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Tether USDT arrives on Polygon chain 137.

Send Circle USDC from 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453, an L2 with ETH gas. Read it on Basescan. It has 6 decimals. Receive Tether USDT at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon, chain 137. Read it on Polygonscan. It also has 6 decimals. Matching decimals do not make Circle and Tether the same issuer. Gas on Polygon is POL, the native coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on that chain. USDT will not pay it.
description: Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on chain 137. Both use 6 decimals. Gas after arrival is POL, not ETH.

sections.heading: Same width, different issuer
sections.body: Because both tokens use 6 decimals, a script that worked for Base USDC will not blow up on the integer size of this USDT. It can still pay the wrong company. Circle redeems USDC. Tether redeems USDT. If the invoice says Circle, the Polygon contract you want is native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, and this page does not deliver it.

sections.heading: POL is the fee you did not buy
sections.body: ETH on Base pays the send. POL on Polygon pays the next transfer. Those balances are not pooled. The old ticker MATIC is not what the chain uses as its gas symbol now. If the Polygon account has tokens and no POL, Polygonscan can show the USDT while the wallet refuses to move it.
