sections.heading: Bridged USDC.e is a third trap
sections.body: Some Polygon apps still ask for bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. That is neither this route's output nor Circle's native Polygon USDC. Arriving with Tether will not fill a USDC.e deposit. Read the contract the app displays, then decide whether any cross-chain dollar route is the right tool.

sections.heading: Explorer order
sections.body: Basescan first, for the USDC approval and debit. Polygonscan second, for USDT at the Tether contract. [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the destination note. Chain 137 is not Base and not Ethereum. There is no promised time for the bridge on top of block production. If the minimum USDT is short, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the same token as Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. You spend Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base. You receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon, which you check on Polygonscan. Both use 6 decimals. The issuers differ. Native Polygon USDC, if that was the request, is a different contract again. Match the invoice issuer, Circle or Tether, before you sign.

faqs.question: What token pays gas on Polygon?
faqs.answer: POL, the native coin on chain 137. Interfaces may show it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. USDT cannot pay those fees, and ETH on Base cannot pay them either. Put POL on the account before you rely on moving the Tether balance. Chain 137 will not accept Base ETH as a fee.

faqs.question: Does this deliver native USDC on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. Native Circle USDC on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Bridged USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route delivers Tether USDT. If the app named either USDC contract, pick a different quote. Read the address in the app and leave this page when it is not Tether's contract on Polygon.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to WETH on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Polygon WETH is what arrives on chain 137.

The USDC is Circle's Base contract 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, 6 decimals, on Basescan. Base is chain 8453 and the fee is ETH. The WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon, chain 137, on Polygonscan. That is wrapped ether, an ERC-20. It is not POL, and it is not the Base WETH predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Native gas on Polygon is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning POL. This route does not buy POL.
description: Swap USDC from Base to WETH on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves Base and wrapped ETH arrives on chain 137. That WETH cannot pay gas. POL is the fee coin, not WETH.

sections.heading: Polygon WETH is not the gas coin
sections.body: Applications on Polygon use 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 when they want ETH exposure inside a token interface. The chain itself is paid in POL. A wallet full of this WETH and empty of POL cannot approve or transfer the WETH. Plan the fee coin separately. Native ETH on Ethereum is yet another balance, on chain 1, and it is not credited here.

sections.heading: You are leaving a dollar for wrapped ether
sections.body: Circle USDC is a fiat-issued stable. WETH tracks ETH. This is not a dollar-to-dollar hop, and it is not a wrap of ETH you already hold. If you wanted Tether, the Polygon contract is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. If you wanted to keep USDC, do not sign. Price movement in ETH can dominate the result. Read the minimum WETH.

sections.heading: The Base predeploy will not satisfy Polygon
sections.body: Holding or wrapping into 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 keeps you on Base. Polygon pools will not see that contract. Canonical Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a third deployment. Match 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan or you are inspecting the wrong chain.

sections.heading: Where the hop is unnecessary
sections.body: If the Polygon position was not required, sell USDC for ETH on Base and stop. If the position was required, follow [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) and still verify both addresses yourself. USDC needs an allowance on Base. WETH on Polygon will need POL before it can move. No bridge duration is promised.

faqs.question: Can Polygon WETH pay the next fee?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is an ERC-20. Gas on chain 137 is POL, the native coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in quotes. You need POL already on the account. ETH spent on Base does not become that POL. A WETH balance on Polygonscan is not a POL balance, and the wallet will not substitute one for the other.

faqs.question: Is this the same WETH contract as on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain 8453. This route spends Circle USDC, not that WETH, and it delivers 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, which you check on Polygonscan. The tickers match. The chains and the contracts do not. Approving Base WETH would be a different route that does not start from USDC.

faqs.question: What if the app wanted POL instead of WETH?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. POL is the gas coin, not an ERC-20 you receive here. Choose the quote that delivers native POL. Staying in USDC, or switching only as far as Tether, is also a different page. Do not sign a WETH minimum if the order was a fee top-up.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to POL on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves Base, and native POL arrives on Polygon chain 137.

You spend Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, 6 decimals, on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows that contract, and the send needs an ETH fee plus an allowance. You receive native POL on Polygon. Quotes write it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which on chain 137 means the gas coin, not ETH and not an ERC-20. Polygonscan shows POL on the account. It is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and not Tether.
description: Swap USDC from Base to POL on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves Base and native POL arrives on chain 137. POL is the gas coin, not WETH and not an ERC-20 token.

sections.heading: Buying the fee coin with a dollar
sections.body: POL can pay later transactions on Polygon. The quote sets the amount. It is not a stipend sized for a week of fees. USDC could not pay those fees, which is often why this hop exists. If you only needed a dollar on Polygon, buying POL sells the stable exposure you had. Read the minimum before you treat the result as spare gas.

sections.heading: The placeholder is POL only on this chain
sections.body: The same 0xEeee string on Base means ETH, the coin that pays for your USDC approval. On Polygon it means POL. Searching that string on Polygonscan does not open a token page. If a form shows it as the output while the wallet is on chain 137, you are buying the native coin. Confirm the network before you sign.

sections.heading: Three nearby assets this page skips
sections.body: It skips Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. It skips native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. It skips WETH. It also skips a Base-only sale of USDC into ETH. Use this route when a Polygon account needs the gas coin and you are funding it from Circle dollars on Base.

sections.heading: How the two explorers differ
sections.body: Basescan records an ERC-20 debit. Polygonscan records a native credit, so you may not see a token transfer on the destination. [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the chain note. No bridge duration is stated. Keep ETH on Base for the approval. If the minimum POL is too small, do not sign.

faqs.question: Does 0xEeee on this route mean ETH or POL?
faqs.answer: On the destination it means POL, the gas coin of chain 137. On Base the same placeholder means ETH, which pays the fee. It is not a contract on Polygonscan. WETH, if that was the order, is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 instead. Match the chain id before you read the address.

faqs.question: Will I receive an ERC-20 called POL?
faqs.answer: You receive native POL on the account balance. There is no token-contract credit to hunt. If a dapp asks for an ERC-20 address rather than the gas coin, this route has not given it that address. Check Polygonscan's native line after the Base USDC debit confirms.

faqs.question: What do I need on Base besides USDC?
faqs.answer: ETH, to pay for the allowance and the send on chain 8453. Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 cannot pay gas. The POL you are buying is not on Base yet, so it cannot cover that fee. Leave the ETH in the wallet when you size the swap.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Base, and Circle's native USDC arrives on Polygon chain 137.

You sell the gas coin on Base, chain 8453, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows the account, not a token page. Leave enough ETH for the fee. There is no approval on native ETH. You receive Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygon, chain 137. Polygonscan is the explorer. That contract is native USDC, 6 decimals, not bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. Gas after arrival is POL.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Base and Circle's native USDC arrives on chain 137. It is not bridged USDC.e. Check Polygonscan.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not the bridged copy
sections.body: Polygon carried a bridged USDC for a long time, and many older pools still point at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This quote credits Circle's native contract instead. A deposit button that names USDC.e will reject the balance you just bought. Read the app's address before you treat the hop as finished. Six decimals match Circle's Base and Ethereum USDC, but those are still other chains.

sections.heading: Selling L2 gas on purpose
sections.body: ETH on Base pays fees and, here, is also the asset sold. A full-balance entry can fail before the bridge sees it. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is invisible to this page. Unwrap if that is all you hold, or switch routes. You do not arrive holding ETH on Polygon. You arrive holding a dollar token.

sections.heading: POL is the leftover problem
sections.body: USDC cannot pay Polygon fees. Base ETH does not become POL. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL only when the wallet is on chain 137. Fund that coin or the USDC sits on Polygonscan with no way to transfer. [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the note for that fee.

sections.heading: Skip the page when the dollar is wrong
sections.body: Skip it for Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Skip it for WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Skip it if you meant to keep ETH, on Base or on Ethereum. Skip it if the minimum USDC is below the floor you will accept. No bridge duration is attached to this quote.

faqs.question: Is this Polygon USDC the bridged USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. Bridged USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route delivers Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, which you check on Polygonscan. Both can be called USDC in a wallet. The app you are funding decides which address it will accept. Read that address on Polygonscan before you fund the market.

faqs.question: Do I approve the ETH I am selling?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH on Base is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is sent rather than approved. Keep a remainder on chain 8453 for the fee. If the wallet asks you to approve WETH, the input selected is the wrapper, and that is a different route.

faqs.question: What pays gas after the USDC arrives on Polygon?
faqs.answer: POL, the native coin on chain 137. USDC cannot pay it, and the ETH you sold on Base does not travel as POL. Put a little POL on the account before you try to move the dollars. Polygonscan will show the USDC even when the wallet cannot send it.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Polygon. You sell native ETH on Base and you receive Tether USDT on Polygon.

The input is Base ETH, chain 8453, placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, visible on Basescan as the account balance. Leave a fee remainder. The output is Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan. Polygon is chain 137. This is not Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and not USDC.e. It is not Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Afterward you need POL, because USDT is not gas.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on chain 137. USDT has 6 decimals and cannot pay POL gas fees now.

sections.heading: Tether on Polygon is its own deployment
sections.body: Six decimals make this USDT feel like Ethereum USDT, and the issuer is Tether in both cases. The contract addresses are not the same, and a mainnet transfer aimed at 0xdAC17 will not move a Polygon balance. Confirm 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan. Tether can still freeze listed addresses. A hop from Base does not remove that rule.

sections.heading: What you gave up
sections.body: You gave up Base ETH, which was paying fees on an L2. You did not receive POL, WETH, or USDC. If the point of holding ETH was to keep using Base, this route works against that. If the point was a Polygon venue that settles in Tether, the contract above is the one to match.

sections.heading: The fee coin changes ticker
sections.body: Base takes ETH. Polygon takes POL. People still say MATIC out of habit. The symbol in the wallet should be POL, and the native balance is not an ERC-20 you approve. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why Basescan and Polygonscan never share one hash. There is no promised wait beyond that explanation.

sections.heading: Refuse the quote for these mismatches
sections.body: Refuse it if the written asset is Circle USDC, native or bridged. Refuse it if the written asset is WETH. Refuse it if you needed ETH on Ethereum, chain 1, where blocks are about 12 seconds. Refuse it if the minimum USDT, after the ETH price, is a worse trade than you will take.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the Ethereum Tether contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route delivers 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, chain 137. Both are Tether and both use 6 decimals. A payment pointed at the Ethereum address will not spend the Polygon balance. Open Polygonscan on chain 137 and match the contract before you send.

faqs.question: Will I have POL because I sold ETH?
faqs.answer: No. You sold ETH on Base and bought USDT on Polygon. POL is a separate native coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE only while the wallet is on chain 137. USDT cannot pay fees. Bring POL before you try to transfer the Tether you just received. ETH sold on Base does not become that fee coin.

faqs.question: Does native ETH on Base need an allowance?
faqs.answer: No. The gas coin is sent, not approved. You must leave enough ETH on chain 8453 to pay the fee or the swap never broadcasts. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is a different input and a different page. This quote will not pull that wrapper. Check Basescan if you are unsure which ETH balance you hold.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to WETH on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Base, and Polygon WETH arrives, which is not a local wrap.

Sell Base ETH, the gas coin at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain 8453. Basescan shows the account. Keep a fee remainder. There is no ERC-20 approval. Receive WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon, chain 137, and read it on Polygonscan. That token is not POL. POL is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE when Polygon is selected. Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is also not the arrival.
description: Swap ETH from Base to WETH on Polygon. Base ETH leaves and Polygon WETH arrives on chain 137. Wrapping on Base would stay on Base. WETH cannot pay POL gas.

sections.heading: Not the wrap button on Base
sections.body: Wrapping on Base mints 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and leaves you on chain 8453. You can unwrap there. This page moves value to Polygon and mints nothing at the Base predeploy. Use the local wrap when a Base contract wants WETH. Use this route when a Polygon contract wants 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619.

sections.heading: WETH still cannot pay Polygon
sections.body: The arrival is an ERC-20 claim on ether, not the fee coin. A large WETH balance with an empty POL balance cannot approve a spender or transfer a token. Get POL onto chain 137 first. Native ETH on Ethereum, chain 1, is a third balance and is not what Polygonscan will show.

sections.heading: Orders this page will not fill
sections.body: It will not fill an order for POL. It will not fill an order for USDC or USDT. It will not fill an order for canonical WETH on Ethereum at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. It will not spend Base WETH, because the input is unwrapped ETH. WBTC is unrelated, and WBTC is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Checking the right row
sections.body: Look at the WETH token row on Polygonscan, not at the POL line and not at Basescan. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through the two signatures' worth of waiting without putting a clock on it. If the minimum WETH is too thin for the ETH you sell, do not sign.

faqs.question: If I wrap ETH on Base, do I get this WETH?
faqs.answer: No. A Base wrap credits 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain 8453. This route credits 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon, which you verify on Polygonscan. The word WETH is shared. The contract and the chain are not. A Polygon pool cannot see the Base predeploy. Confirm the credit on Polygonscan at the Polygon WETH contract.

faqs.question: Can the WETH that arrives pay Polygon fees?
faqs.answer: No. Fees on chain 137 are POL, the native coin. WETH is an ERC-20. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL on Polygon and ETH on Base. You need POL in the account before you can move or unwrap the WETH you receive. Base ETH will not cover that fee.

faqs.question: Is this the same as receiving native ETH on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH on Ethereum is the gas coin on chain 1, shown on Etherscan as the account balance, with blocks about every 12 seconds. This route delivers wrapped ETH on Polygon. If the order was mainnet ETH or mainnet WETH, you are on the wrong page.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to POL on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Base, and native POL is what arrives on Polygon.

Both lines can show 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On Base, chain 8453, that placeholder is ETH, an L2 gas coin, read on Basescan as the account balance. On Polygon, chain 137, it is POL, read on Polygonscan as the account balance. It is not an ERC-20. It is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Leave some ETH on Base or the send cannot pay its own fee. You are changing exposure from ether to POL.
description: Swap ETH from Base to POL on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Base and POL arrives on chain 137. POL is the gas coin. It is not WETH and not a shared 0xEeee contract.

sections.heading: The placeholder is not a portable coin
sections.body: Copying 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE between chains does not move a token. Each chain interprets it as its own gas coin. Chain id 8453 means you are selling ETH. Chain id 137 means you are buying POL. If the wallet header still says Ethereum, you are not looking at this route's destination at all.

sections.heading: POL replaced the MATIC habit
sections.body: The fee symbol on Polygon is POL. Older guides say MATIC. A wallet that still labels the native balance with the old word is talking about the same gas coin, not about an extra ERC-20 you must approve. There is no approval on the ETH you send, and there is no token contract to open for the POL you receive.

sections.heading: When ether should have stayed ether
sections.body: Stay off this page if you wanted WETH on Polygon, USDC, or USDT. Stay off it if you wanted ETH on Ethereum. Stay off it if you only needed a local wrap on Base. This route is a sale of ETH exposure into the Polygon fee coin. [Trade on Base](/chains/base) is where that ETH currently pays fees, until you sell it.

sections.heading: Confirm the account line
sections.body: Polygonscan's native balance is the arrival record. A WETH transfer means a different quote was used. Basescan's ETH debit is the source record. Do not send a second swap because the hashes differ. The bridge wait is not given as a duration. Reject the quote when the minimum POL is too small.

faqs.question: Why do ETH and POL share an address in the quote?
faqs.answer: They do not share a contract. Interfaces write 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for the native gas coin of the selected chain. On Base that is ETH. On Polygon that is POL. Basescan and Polygonscan show two account balances, not one token page. Chain ids 8453 and 137 keep them apart.

faqs.question: Is POL the same asset as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH on Polygon is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, an ERC-20 you would see on Polygonscan as a token. POL is the gas coin and can pay fees on chain 137. If a pool asked for the WETH contract, this route delivered the wrong asset. POL can pay fees, and that WETH contract cannot.

faqs.question: What happens if I spend all of my Base ETH?
faqs.answer: The transaction cannot pay the chain 8453 fee, so it should fail before a bridge message is sent. Leave a remainder. Native ETH is not approved. If your ether is wrapped at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, this native route will not see it until you unwrap. Unwrap on Base first, then sell the gas coin if POL is still the goal.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Polygon. Base WETH leaves, and Circle's native USDC arrives on Polygon chain 137.

Approve 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453, and confirm that token on Basescan. Native ETH, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, is not the input. Receive 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygon, chain 137. That is Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan. It is not USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. It is not Tether. You still need POL to move it, because USDC is not the gas coin.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Polygon. Base WETH leaves and Circle USDC arrives on chain 137. That USDC is not bridged USDC.e and it cannot pay POL gas.

sections.heading: The allowance is only the Base wrapper
sections.body: The router needs permission to take WETH. Read the spender and the cap. The signature costs ETH on chain 8453. It does not approve USDC on Polygon, and it does not move native ETH. If the wallet shows an ETH balance and an empty WETH balance, wrap first or change routes. Declining the allowance stops the trade cleanly.

sections.heading: Native USDC versus USDC.e
sections.body: Circle's current Polygon USDC is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. The older bridged token is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. Both have been displayed as USDC. A lending market still wired to the bridged address will not accept this credit. Six decimals match either token, so decimals alone will not save you. Open Polygonscan.

sections.heading: Wrong input, wrong output
sections.body: Wrong if you meant to sell native ETH rather than WETH. Wrong if the destination dollar is Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Wrong if you wanted POL so you could pay fees. Wrong if you wanted WETH to remain WETH on Polygon. Wrong if the USDC only needed to stay on Base.

sections.heading: Fee coin after a dollar credit
sections.body: [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the reminder that POL pays chain 137. WETH you sold was on Base. USDC you bought cannot substitute. Basescan shows the wrapper debit. Polygonscan shows the USDC credit. No duration is promised for the gap between those pages. If the minimum USDC is poor, leave it unsigned.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract should Polygonscan show?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is the bridged token and is not this route. Tether is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Match the address in the app to the address on the quote before you sign. USDC.e and native USDC are not interchangeable on Polygon chain 137.

faqs.question: Do I approve WETH on Base?
faqs.answer: Yes. The input is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, an ERC-20 on chain 8453. The router needs an allowance. Native ETH is the gas coin that pays for that approval, and it is not the asset being sold. Review the spender. The allowance does not extend to Polygon. A later spend of USDC on chain 137 is a new signature, paid in POL.

faqs.question: Can this USDC pay Polygon gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is POL, the native coin on chain 137, often written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. USDC is an ERC-20 from Circle with 6 decimals. ETH on Base does not pay Polygon fees. Without POL, the USDC can show on Polygonscan and still be stuck. Fund the gas coin before you try to move it.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Polygon. Wrapped ETH leaves Base, and Tether USDT arrives on Polygon chain 137.

The WETH you approve is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453, on Basescan. Gas for the approval is ETH, not the wrapper itself. The USDT you receive is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, Tether, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan, chain 137. It is not Circle USDC and not USDC.e. Native gas uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means ETH on Base and POL on Polygon. Neither native coin is the asset this quote exchanges.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Polygon. Base WETH leaves and Tether USDT arrives on chain 137. USDT is 6 decimals. You still need POL to move it later.

sections.heading: Selling wrapped ether into Tether
sections.body: This is a change of asset, not a relocation of WETH. Polygon WETH, if you had wanted it, is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. You will not see a credit there. You will see Tether, 6 decimals against WETH's 18, so the raw log integers are not comparable. Read the human amount on the quote, then the contract.

sections.heading: Circle would have been a different address
sections.body: Native USDC on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Bridged USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. A treasury that redeems at Circle cannot redeem this USDT at Circle. Tether's freeze list still applies on the destination contract. The bridge does not wash that status.

sections.heading: Two signatures people mix up
sections.body: First you may approve WETH on Base. Later a Polygon app may ask to spend USDT, and that second request is paid in POL. You do not approve USDT in order to receive it. If the wallet is on the wrong chain, the spender address in the popup belongs to a different network. Check chain id 8453 for the input.

sections.heading: Receipts on two explorers
sections.body: Basescan records WETH leaving. Polygonscan records USDT arriving. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the sequence, without a clock. Bring POL before you forward the dollars. If you hold native ETH instead of WETH, this page cannot see your balance. Decline a minimum you would not keep.

faqs.question: Is the USDT here the same as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: The issuer is Tether and the decimals are 6, but the contract is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon, chain 137. Ethereum's contract is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Check Polygonscan for the credit. A mainnet transfer will not move these tokens. The credit is on Polygonscan, chain 137, and it stays there until you use that network.

faqs.question: What if I have ETH on Base but no WETH?
faqs.answer: This route spends 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 only. Native ETH, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays gas and is not pulled as the input. Wrap on Base first, or use the route that sells native ETH for USDT. An empty WETH balance cannot be approved into a trade. Native ETH on Base can pay gas, but it is not this input.

faqs.question: Does arriving USDT include POL for fees?
faqs.answer: No. USDT cannot pay gas on chain 137. POL is the native coin. The ETH you spent to approve WETH on Base stays on Base. Put POL on the Polygon account or the Tether balance is visible on Polygonscan and still immovable. POL has to be there first.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to POL on Polygon. Base WETH leaves, and native POL arrives on Polygon chain 137 today.

You approve wrapped ETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows that ERC-20. You receive native POL on chain 137, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Polygonscan shows it on the account, not as a token contract. It is not Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Unwrapping on Base would have returned ETH on Base, which cannot pay Polygon fees. This route is how you turn the wrapper into the destination gas coin.
description: Swap WETH from Base to POL on Polygon. Base WETH leaves and native POL arrives on chain 137. POL is the gas coin. It is not Polygon WETH and not a local unwrap.

sections.heading: You are buying the fee coin
sections.body: POL can pay for later Polygon transactions. The amount is the quote, not a calculated reserve. A small fill may cover one transfer and not a second. WETH could not pay those fees even if you had bridged the wrapper unchanged. Read the minimum POL before you assume the account is funded for a session.

sections.heading: Approval still costs Base ETH
sections.body: The wrapper needs an allowance, and the allowance needs ETH on chain 8453. If ETH is zero, unwrap a slice of WETH first or add ETH. You cannot pay that Base fee with the POL you have not received. Declining the spender stops the route. The spender on Base is not a Polygon contract.

sections.heading: WETH on Polygon is the decoy
sections.body: If the app address is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, you want wrapped ether, not POL. If the app wants USDC or USDT, you want a dollar. If you only needed Base ETH, unwrap locally. WBTC is not this trade and is not native bitcoin. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the handoff you do want when POL really is the target.

sections.heading: What a successful check looks like
sections.body: Basescan: WETH balance down at the predeploy. Polygonscan: native POL up on the account. No token-transfer row is required for the arrival, because POL is not an ERC-20. Chain 137 must be the network in the wallet before that native line is the one you think it is. No fill time is promised.

faqs.question: Is the POL I receive an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: No. It is the native gas coin on chain 137. Quotes label it 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Polygonscan shows the account balance. Polygon WETH, an ERC-20, is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. If you needed that contract, this route is the wrong one. POL is only the gas coin, shown on the account in Polygonscan.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap Base WETH instead?
faqs.answer: You can, and the result is ETH on Base, chain 8453, not POL on Polygon. Unwrapping burns 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 locally. This page sends that wrapper toward chain 137 and credits POL. Use the unwrap only when you intend to stay on Base. This hop is for a POL balance on chain 137.

faqs.question: What pays for the approval?
faqs.answer: ETH on Base. WETH is the token being approved, not the coin that pays gas, until you unwrap it. The POL you are buying is not on Base and cannot cover the fee. Keep a little ETH beside the WETH or the allowance cannot be mined.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Tether USDT arrives on Arbitrum One.

Send 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, Circle's USDC on Base, chain 8453, and read it on Basescan. Receive 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, Tether's USDT, on Arbitrum One, chain 42161, and read it on Arbiscan. Both tokens use 6 decimals. The issuers differ. This is Arbitrum One, not Arbitrum Nova. Both chains use ETH for gas, and the balances are separate. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on each chain. USDT will not pay it.
description: Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. Both use 6 decimals. Gas is ETH.

sections.heading: One, not Nova
sections.body: Chain id 42161 is Arbitrum One. Nova is a different network with different contracts. A wallet pointed at Nova will not show this USDT, and a bridge aimed at One will not fill a Nova balance. Check the network badge before you decide the funds are missing. Arbiscan for this route is the One explorer.

sections.heading: Circle out, Tether in
sections.body: Native USDC on Arbitrum One is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Bridged USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. This page delivers neither. It delivers Tether. If a protocol still asks for USDC.e, or if a desk redeems at Circle, stop. Six decimals on both sides only means the integer width matches.

sections.heading: ETH on Base is not ETH on Arbitrum
sections.body: You pay ETH to approve USDC on Base. You need other ETH, already on Arbitrum One, to move USDT after it lands. The hop does not bundle that gas. [Trade on Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) covers One as the trading network. There is no promised bridge time. If the minimum USDT is short of what you will accept, do not sign.

sections.heading: When a same-chain swap is enough
sections.body: If the buyer of your dollars is on Base, crossing to Arbitrum only to come back pays two fees and two contract checks. If you need ARB, the governance token, this dollar route will not mint it. If you need WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, you are on the wrong output as well.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum USDT the same contract as Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. You spend Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base. You receive Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One, chain 42161, which you check on Arbiscan. Native USDC on One is a different address. This page is only right when Tether is the asset you meant. Circle's own USDC on Arbitrum One is a different contract.

faqs.question: Does this work on Arbitrum Nova?
faqs.answer: No. This route targets Arbitrum One, chain 42161, not Nova. USDT at the address above is the One contract. A wallet on Nova can look empty even after Arbiscan shows the credit. Switch to One before you hunt for the balance. Nova will not display this USDT credit.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay gas on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is ETH on chain 42161, just as gas is ETH on Base, chain 8453. They are separate ETH balances. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means that native coin on whichever chain is selected. USDT cannot replace it. Keep ETH on Arbitrum One if you need to move the tokens after they land.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to ETH on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base, and native ETH arrives on Arbitrum One, chain 42161.

Spend Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan is the explorer, and you should expect an approval paid in ETH. Receive native ETH on Arbitrum One. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means that gas coin, shown on Arbiscan as the account balance, not as a token. It is not WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. This is One, not Nova. Base ETH and Arbitrum ETH are separate balances.
description: Swap USDC from Base to ETH on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base and native ETH arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. That ETH is the gas coin, not WETH.

sections.heading: You are buying gas on a second rollup
sections.body: Both Base and Arbitrum One charge fees in ETH, and neither balance pays the other. This route sells a dollar on Base and credits ETH on One, so the arrival can pay later One transactions. The amount is the quote's minimum, not a reserved fee budget. WETH is a different asset if a contract wants 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1.

sections.heading: Nova will hide the result
sections.body: Chain id 42161 is Arbitrum One. Nova uses other contracts and will not display this credit. If the wallet badge says Nova, switch it before you conclude the bridge failed. Arbiscan for One is the page that matters. A Base transaction hash will not appear there as the same receipt.

sections.heading: Dollars you might have meant instead
sections.body: Tether on One is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Native USDC is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Bridged USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. ARB, the governance token, is another page entirely. If any of those was the written order, do not sign this ETH quote.

sections.heading: What to compare on the quote
sections.body: [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) separates the two receipts. You still match the USDC contract on Basescan yourself. Leave Base ETH for the approval. There is no promised duration. If the minimum ETH is less than you will accept for the dollars, leave the quote unsigned. Chain 42161 and chain 8453 both name the fee coin ETH, and those balances still do not combine.

faqs.question: Is the ETH I receive WETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Arbiscan shows it on the account. WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. A pool that accepts only that contract will ignore the native balance until you wrap it on Arbitrum One, chain 42161. Wrapping is a later step, and it is not included in this USDC sale.

faqs.question: Does Base ETH travel over as the same balance?
faqs.answer: No. You are selling USDC, not relocating your Base ETH. The ETH that arrives is a new balance on chain 42161. The ETH you already hold on Base, chain 8453, stays there and is what pays the send. Arbiscan and Basescan are different explorers for that reason.

faqs.question: Will this show up on Arbitrum Nova?
faqs.answer: No. This route credits Arbitrum One, chain 42161, not Nova. If the wallet is on Nova, the account can look empty after Arbiscan already shows the ETH. Switch networks before you send a second swap. USDC on Base is unchanged until you sign. A second click will not speed the first bridge, and no duration is promised.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to WETH on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Arbitrum WETH arrives on chain 42161.

The USDC is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453, an L2, checked on Basescan. It needs an allowance, and that allowance costs ETH. The WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, checked on Arbiscan. It is an ERC-20. It is not native ETH, so it cannot pay gas. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is a third contract and is not the arrival. This is not Nova.
description: Swap USDC from Base to WETH on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base and WETH arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. That WETH cannot pay gas until you unwrap it.

sections.heading: Why a pool asks for this contract
sections.body: Many Arbitrum markets take WETH rather than native ETH because the token interface is uniform. Depositing ETH into 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on One would wrap locally. This route buys that wrapped token from a USDC sale on Base. It does not wrap ETH you already hold on Arbitrum, and it does not leave a spendable gas balance by itself.

sections.heading: You still need ETH on One
sections.body: Unwrapping or approving WETH costs ETH on chain 42161. If the account has none, the WETH can sit on Arbiscan and not move. Base ETH paid the USDC approval and does not migrate. Get a small ETH balance onto One before you depend on the unwrap. The placeholder for that gas coin is 0xEeee, not the WETH address.

sections.heading: Wrong contract, wrong chain
sections.body: Wrong if you needed native ETH to pay fees immediately. Wrong if you needed Tether, native USDC, or USDC.e. Wrong if you needed ARB. Wrong if the wallet is on Nova. Wrong if you only wanted to wrap on Base, which stays at the 0x4200 predeploy. WBTC is not this asset and is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Read Arbiscan for the wrapper
sections.body: The credit is a token balance at the WETH contract, not a rise in the account's ETH line. [Trade on Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) is the network context, and it means One. Basescan shows the USDC debit. No clock is promised for the bridge. Decline the quote if the minimum WETH is too small.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay Arbitrum gas?
faqs.answer: Not directly. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is an ERC-20. Gas on Arbitrum One, chain 42161, is native ETH. You need some of that ETH already before you can unwrap. The 0xEeee placeholder is how quotes refer to the gas coin, and this route does not deliver it.

faqs.question: Is Base WETH the token I will receive?
faqs.answer: No. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain 8453. This route spends Circle USDC and delivers 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, which you check on Arbiscan. Holding the Base predeploy does not open an Arbitrum position. Basescan and Arbiscan are showing two different networks, and only chain 42161 receives this WETH.

faqs.question: What if the app only accepts native ETH?
faqs.answer: Then stop. This route ends at the WETH contract. Unwrapping is a separate transaction on Arbitrum One and needs ETH for gas. If native ETH was the order, choose the route that delivers the gas coin. Nova is the wrong network either way. Chain 42161 is Arbitrum One, and that is the only destination this quote credits.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to ARB on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base, and the ARB token arrives on Arbitrum One.

Send Circle USDC from 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453. Check Basescan and approve if asked. The fee is ETH. Receive ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One, chain 42161. Check Arbiscan. ARB is the governance token. It is not ETH, it is not WETH, and it does not pay gas. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on each chain, and the two ETH balances are separate. This is not Arbitrum Nova.
description: Swap USDC from Base to ARB on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC leaves Base and the ARB governance token arrives on chain 42161. ARB is not ETH and cannot pay gas.

sections.heading: Governance token, not a fee token
sections.body: ARB is used for voting and for markets that list it. Validators on Arbitrum One are paid in ETH. A wallet that holds only ARB cannot move that ARB. If you came here to fund gas, you wanted native ETH, and this page sells you a volatile token instead. Price moves in ARB can dwarf the stable value you spent. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Not Nova, and not USDC on One
sections.body: Nova will not show this contract's balance. Native USDC on One is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Bridged USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. Tether is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. None of those is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. If the order still says a dollar, leave.

sections.heading: ETH you must already have on One
sections.body: The route does not attach ETH to the ARB credit. Move ARB later only if chain 42161 already has ETH. Base ETH paid the USDC side and stays on chain 8453. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing sequence, not a timer.

sections.heading: When the hop is unnecessary
sections.body: If you can buy ARB with dollars already on Arbitrum One, you do not need to start from Base USDC. If your USDC buyer is on Base, stay there. Crossing only to swap and return pays twice. WBTC is unrelated, and it would not be native bitcoin even on a different route.

faqs.question: Does ARB pay gas on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the governance token, an ERC-20. Gas is ETH on chain 42161. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means that ETH, not ARB. You need ETH on One before the new ARB balance can be transferred. Arbiscan can show ARB while the wallet still refuses to send it.

faqs.question: Is this Arbitrum Nova?
faqs.answer: No. The destination is Arbitrum One, chain 42161. Nova is a different network. A Nova wallet will not display this ARB credit even after Arbiscan shows it. Switch to One, then look for 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. The source USDC remains on Base, chain 8453, until you sign.

faqs.question: I wanted to keep a dollar. Does ARB count?
faqs.answer: No. You spend Circle USDC and you receive a governance token whose price moves. Native USDC on Arbitrum One and Tether are different routes. If the written instruction says USDC or USDT, do not sign this page. The minimum ARB on the quote is the number that matters, and there is no promised fill time.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Arbitrum One. Native ETH leaves Base, and Circle's native USDC arrives on Arbitrum One.

You sell the gas coin on Base, chain 8453, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows the account. Leave a remainder for the fee. There is no approval on native ETH. You receive 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One, chain 42161. That is Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals, on Arbiscan. It is not bridged USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. It is not Tether. This is not Nova. You will need separate ETH on One to move the USDC.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Arbitrum One. Native ETH leaves Base and Circle's native USDC arrives on chain 42161. It is not bridged USDC.e and not Nova.

sections.heading: Native USDC versus USDC.e
sections.body: Arbitrum One still has apps pointed at bridged USDC.e, 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. This quote credits Circle's native contract instead. A deposit screen that names the bridged address will not take your balance. Six decimals will not tell the two apart. Open Arbiscan and compare. Circle's Base USDC, which you are not receiving, is a different chain entirely.

sections.heading: You sold the Base fee token
sections.body: ETH on Base both pays the send and is the asset sold. Do not enter the full balance. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is not accepted here. If that is what you hold, unwrap or switch pages. You do not arrive with ETH on Arbitrum. You arrive with a dollar that cannot pay One's fees.

sections.heading: Gas on the far side is still ETH, just not this ETH
sections.body: Chain 42161 uses ETH for gas, and that balance is empty if you never funded it. The ETH you sold lived on Base. Put a little ETH on One by some other means before you forward the USDC. [Trade on Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) assumes One, not Nova. No bridge time is promised.

sections.heading: Leave if the dollar contract is wrong
sections.body: Leave if the app wants USDC.e. Leave if it wants Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Leave if it wants ARB or WETH. Leave if you meant to keep ETH on Base for fees. Leave if the minimum USDC is below your floor.

faqs.question: Is this USDC the bridged USDC.e on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. This route delivers Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, which you check on Arbiscan. Chain 42161 is Arbitrum One, not Nova. If the app displays the bridged address, this credit will not satisfy it. Compare the address on the deposit screen with 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 before you sign.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH before selling it?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin on Base, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is sent rather than approved. Keep enough on chain 8453 to pay the fee. An approval request means the input is an ERC-20 such as WETH, which is a different route.

faqs.question: The USDC arrived. Why can't I send it?
faqs.answer: Arbitrum One charges ETH for gas, and this route did not deliver ETH. It delivered USDC. Your Base ETH was the input, so it is not sitting on chain 42161. Add ETH on One, then the USDC at the native Circle contract can move. Until then Arbiscan can show a balance the wallet will not transfer.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Arbitrum One. You sell native ETH on Base and you receive Tether USDT on Arbitrum One.

The input is Base ETH, chain 8453, placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Basescan as the account balance. Leave a fee. No approval applies to that coin. The output is Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, 6 decimals, on Arbiscan. Arbitrum One is chain 42161, not Nova. This is not Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 and not USDC.e. Ethereum mainnet Tether is a different contract again. USDT cannot pay ETH gas on One.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Arbitrum One. Native ETH leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. USDT has 6 decimals and cannot pay gas.

sections.heading: Tether's One contract
sections.body: Six decimals match Ethereum USDT, and the issuer is Tether, but 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 lives on chain 42161. A mainnet payment to 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 will not spend this balance. Confirm the row on Arbiscan. Tether's freeze rules still apply. Coming from Base does not clear an address that is already listed.

sections.heading: What the sale removes
sections.body: You remove Base ETH, the coin that was paying L2 fees. You do not receive ARB, WETH, or USDC. If Base apps still need that ETH, size the sale so a remainder remains, beyond the network fee. If an Arbitrum venue settles in Tether, this contract is the one to match.

sections.heading: Nova and the dollar lookalikes
sections.body: Nova is the wrong network. USDC.e is the wrong dollar. Native Circle USDC is the wrong dollar if the instruction says Tether, and Tether is the wrong dollar if the instruction says Circle. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the handoff. It does not name a duration. Reject a weak minimum.

sections.heading: ETH on One is a separate chore
sections.body: After USDT shows up you still cannot move it without ETH on chain 42161. The placeholder 0xEeee on One means that gas coin, which this quote did not buy. Fund it first. Basescan will not display the USDT credit. Arbiscan will.

faqs.question: Is this the Ethereum USDT contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan, chain 1, where blocks are about 12 seconds. This route delivers 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. Both use 6 decimals. Check Arbiscan. A mainnet transfer will not move the One balance. Stay on Arbiscan, chain 42161, when you confirm the credit.

faqs.question: Will Nova show this USDT?
faqs.answer: No. The destination is chain 42161, Arbitrum One, not Nova. If the wallet is on Nova, switch before you look. The source is native ETH on Base, chain 8453, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That debit appears on Basescan, not as a Nova transaction. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One before you judge the result missing.

faqs.question: Can USDT pay the next Arbitrum fee?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is ETH. USDT is Tether's ERC-20. Selling Base ETH does not leave ETH on Arbitrum One. Add ETH on chain 42161 or the USDT stays visible on Arbiscan and stuck. The two ETH balances never merge just because the ticker matches. Fund chain 42161 on purpose.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to WETH on Arbitrum One. Native ETH leaves Base, and Arbitrum WETH arrives. That is not a local wrap.

Sell Base ETH, gas coin 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain 8453. Basescan shows the account. Keep a fee remainder. Receive 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, chain 42161, on Arbiscan. That WETH cannot pay gas. Native ETH on One is the same placeholder style, a different balance. Wrapping on Base would mint 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and stay on Base. This is not Nova and not canonical Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2.
description: Swap ETH from Base to WETH on Arbitrum One. Native Base ETH leaves and WETH arrives on chain 42161. A local wrap on Base stays on Base. WETH cannot pay gas.

sections.heading: Local wrap versus this destination
sections.body: A wrap on Base takes native ETH and returns the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. You can unwrap on Base. Nothing in that pair of actions touches Arbiscan. This page is only useful when an Arbitrum One contract asked for 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If the app is on Base, stop and wrap locally.

sections.heading: Unwrap later still needs gas ETH
sections.body: WETH on One is not the fee token. To unwrap it you already need ETH on chain 42161. This route sold your Base ETH and did not deliver native ETH on One. Fund a small gas balance before you plan the unwrap. Otherwise the wrapper is visible and idle.

sections.heading: Orders that do not match
sections.body: Native ETH on One is a different route. USDC, USDT, and ARB are different routes. Ethereum mainnet WETH is a different contract on chain 1. Nova is a different network. WBTC is not ether and is not native bitcoin. If your input is already Base WETH, this page, which spends unwrapped ETH, will not see it.

sections.heading: Explorer split
sections.body: [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the sequence. Basescan should show ETH leaving the account. Arbiscan should show WETH at the One contract, not a jump in the native ETH line. Twelve second Ethereum blocks are irrelevant here. No bridge duration is promised. Do not sign a minimum you dislike.

faqs.question: Does wrapping on Base give me Arbitrum WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Wrapping on Base credits 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on chain 8453. This route credits 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, which you check on Arbiscan. The tickers match. The chains do not. A One pool cannot see the Base predeploy. If the app lives on Base, wrap locally and do not use this bridge.

faqs.question: Will the arriving WETH pay gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain 42161 is native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, not WETH. You need some native ETH on Arbitrum One before you can unwrap or approve the wrapper. ETH you kept on Base does not pay One. This route does not deliver that gas coin.

faqs.question: Is this Arbitrum Nova or Ethereum WETH?
faqs.answer: Neither. The network is Arbitrum One, chain 42161, not Nova. Canonical WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. If the order names that mainnet contract, or names Nova, leave this page. The input is native ETH on Base, not WETH. If you already hold the Base wrapper, this page will not spend it.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to ARB on Arbitrum One. Native ETH leaves Base, and the ARB governance token arrives on Arbitrum One.

You spend Base ETH, chain 8453, placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows the account balance. Leave enough to pay the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval. You receive ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on chain 42161. Arbiscan is the explorer. ARB is not ETH and cannot pay gas. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is not the output. This is Arbitrum One, not Nova. You are selling ether exposure for a governance token.
description: Swap ETH from Base to ARB on Arbitrum One. Native ETH leaves Base and ARB arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. ARB cannot pay gas. Bring ETH on One first.

sections.heading: A volatile token, not a fee top-up
sections.body: People sometimes buy ARB because they want to vote or to use a market that pairs it. The price can move while the bridge is in progress, and the minimum on the quote is your floor. If that floor is a bad trade for the ETH you give up, do not sign. Nothing here promises how long the bridge takes or what ARB will be worth when it shows on Arbiscan.

sections.heading: You still owe One some ETH
sections.body: ARB cannot pay for its own transfer. Chain 42161 wants ETH. The ETH you sold was on Base and does not reappear as gas. Fund One separately. If you cannot, the governance token will sit idle. The placeholder 0xEeee means ETH on whichever chain the wallet has selected, not ARB.

sections.heading: Wrong when you wanted ether to remain ether
sections.body: If the goal was ETH on Arbitrum One, this page sells it into ARB and you should stop. If the goal was WETH, USDC, or USDT, stop. If the goal was a Base wrap, stop. If the wallet is on Nova, you are looking at the wrong network even after a correct fill. WBTC is not a stand-in, and it is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Where the debit and the credit live
sections.body: Debit: Basescan, native ETH down, chain 8453. Credit: Arbiscan, ARB token up, chain 42161. [Trade on Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) is the destination note and it means One. Do not resubmit because the hashes differ. Keep a Base ETH remainder so the first transaction can be mined.

faqs.question: Is ARB the gas token on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is ETH. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the governance token, which you verify on Arbiscan. The native coin is written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in quotes. You need that ETH on chain 42161 before ARB can move. This route does not include it. Add ETH on One or the ARB balance cannot be sent.

faqs.question: Does this fill on Arbitrum Nova?
faqs.answer: No. The chain id is 42161, Arbitrum One, not Nova. A Nova wallet can look empty when Arbiscan already shows ARB. Switch to One. The ETH you sold is the Base gas coin, chain 8453, and that debit is on Basescan only. Nova never becomes the destination by waiting.

faqs.question: I wanted to move ETH, not sell it. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Do not sign. A route that delivers native ETH on Arbitrum One keeps the gas coin as the gas coin. This page delivers ARB instead. If you only needed ETH on Base, you do not need a bridge at all. Read the output symbol on the quote and stop when it says ARB.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves, and Circle's native USDC arrives on Arbitrum One, chain 42161.

Approve 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows that ERC-20. The approval costs ETH. Native ETH, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, is not the input. Receive 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan shows Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 and is not this credit. This is not Nova. You need ETH on One before the USDC can move.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves and Circle's native USDC arrives on chain 42161. It is not bridged USDC.e and not on Nova.

sections.heading: Allowance on the wrapper, dollars on One
sections.body: The router may take Base WETH only after you allow it. Read the spender and the cap. That signature is chain 8453. It does not approve USDC on Arbitrum, and it does not spend native ETH. If the wallet shows ETH and no WETH, wrap first or switch to the native ETH route. Declining the allowance stops the hop before any bridge message.

sections.heading: Native USDC is the contract apps are migrating toward
sections.body: Older Arbitrum pools still name USDC.e. A deposit of native USDC into a market wired to 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 will fail or sit unused. Six decimals describe both tokens, so the integer width will not warn you. Compare the address on the app with 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan.

sections.heading: Nova, Tether, and the gas gap
sections.body: Nova is a different network and will not list this balance. Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 is a different issuer. ARB is a different asset. WETH on One, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, is what you would receive if you had not sold the wrapper for dollars. ETH on Base does not become ETH on One.

sections.heading: Check, then decide
sections.body: [Trade on Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) means One, chain 42161. Basescan records the WETH debit. Arbiscan records the USDC credit. No duration is promised between them. If the minimum USDC is below your floor, do not sign. Fund One with ETH before you try to forward the dollars.

faqs.question: Which USDC should Arbiscan show?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One, chain 42161. USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is the bridged token and is not this route. Tether is a third contract. Match the app's address before you treat the balance as deposited. Arbiscan on chain 42161 is the check, and Nova will not list this USDC.

faqs.question: What if I only hold native ETH on Base?
faqs.answer: This page cannot spend it. The input is WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it pays for the approval rather than being sold. Wrap first, or choose the route that sells the gas coin directly. The wrapper and the gas coin are different balances on Base.

faqs.question: Why is the USDC stuck after it arrives?
faqs.answer: USDC cannot pay gas on chain 42161. ETH does, and the ETH on Base stayed on Base. Arbiscan can show the Circle balance while the wallet refuses to send it. Put ETH on Arbitrum One, not on Nova, and then the transfer can be signed.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves, and Tether USDT arrives on Arbitrum One, chain 42161.

The wrapper you approve is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453, on Basescan. Gas for that step is ETH. The USDT you receive is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, 6 decimals, on Arbiscan. It is Tether, not Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 and not USDC.e. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is a mainnet contract. This destination is Arbitrum One, not Nova. Native gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and you are not delivering it.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves and Tether USDT arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. USDT has 6 decimals and cannot pay ETH gas.

sections.heading: Selling the wrapper into Tether
sections.body: You exit ETH exposure. You do not relocate WETH to 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. WETH has 18 decimals and this USDT has 6, so raw log integers are not comparable. Read the human amount. Tether can freeze addresses. A bridge from Base does not remove a freeze that already applies to your address on this contract.

sections.heading: Circle would be a different fill
sections.body: If the counterparty redeems at Circle, native USDC on One is the contract to buy, and this page is wrong. If they named USDC.e, neither this USDT nor native USDC will match. If they named Ethereum USDT, chain 1, you still have another hop after this one. Chain 42161 is not chain 1, even though both use the letters ETH for gas.

sections.heading: Approval chain versus receive chain
sections.body: Approve WETH on Base only. Do not approve USDT in order to receive it. A later One app may ask to spend USDT, and that request is paid with ETH on chain 42161. If the wallet is on Nova during that second signature, you are approving a different network. Check the badge.

sections.heading: Two explorers, no shared hash
sections.body: [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why Basescan and Arbiscan do not share a transaction id. There is no promised wait. Bring ETH to One before you move USDT. If you hold native ETH instead of WETH, this route sees an empty input. Decline a minimum you will not accept.

faqs.question: Is this USDT the Ethereum Tether contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route delivers 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One, chain 42161, which you check on Arbiscan. Both use 6 decimals and both are Tether. A mainnet transfer will not move the One balance. Stay on Arbiscan and chain 42161 when you confirm Tether arrived.

faqs.question: Do I need WETH, or will native ETH work?
faqs.answer: You need WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Native ETH on Base, the 0xEeee placeholder, pays gas and is not pulled as the sold asset. Wrap on chain 8453 first if the wrapper is what you meant to sell. An empty WETH balance cannot be approved into this trade.

faqs.question: Can the USDT pay Arbitrum fees?
faqs.answer: No. Fees on chain 42161 are ETH, a separate balance from Base ETH. USDT cannot pay them. Nova will not show this credit even if you wait. Switch to Arbitrum One, fund ETH there, and only then can the Tether balance move. Base ETH never becomes that One gas balance.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to ETH on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves, and native ETH arrives on Arbitrum One, chain 42161.

This is not an unwrap on Base. Unwrapping burns 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and returns ETH on chain 8453. This route takes that wrapper, visible on Basescan after you approve it, and credits native ETH on Arbitrum One. Quotes write the arrival as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Arbiscan shows the account balance, not a token. WETH on One is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and is not the result. This is not Nova.
description: Swap WETH from Base to ETH on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves and native ETH arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. This is not an unwrap and not One's WETH.

sections.heading: Unwrap locally only if you are staying
sections.body: A local unwrap gives you Base ETH, which pays Base fees and never appears on Arbiscan. Use it when a Base app needs the gas coin. Use this page when an Arbitrum One app needs the gas coin. The approval on the wrapper still costs a little Base ETH, so do not sit at zero ETH while holding only WETH.

sections.heading: The arrival can pay One, the input could not
sections.body: Once native ETH is credited on chain 42161 it can pay later transactions there. Do not treat the quoted amount as spare gas after those transactions. WETH could not have paid One fees even if you had bridged the wrapper unchanged. If a pool wants the WETH contract, you finished on the wrong asset and would still wrap.

sections.heading: What this page will not do
sections.body: It will not deliver USDC, USDT, or ARB. It will not deliver canonical WETH on Ethereum at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. It will not spend native ETH, because the input is the wrapper. It will not credit Nova. WBTC is unrelated, and WBTC is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Reading the account, not the token
sections.body: Look at the ETH line on Arbiscan after the WETH debit on Basescan. [Trade on Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) is One, chain 42161. A token transfer of WETH means you used another route. No bridge duration is stated. Reject the quote if the minimum ETH is too small for the wrapper you give up.

faqs.question: Is receiving ETH the same as receiving WETH on One?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Arbiscan shows it on the account. WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Pools that take only the contract will ignore the native balance until you wrap on chain 42161. That wrap is not part of this route at all.

faqs.question: Can I just unwrap Base WETH?
faqs.answer: You can, and the ETH stays on Base, chain 8453. This route delivers ETH on Arbitrum One, which you check on Arbiscan, and it spends 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 only after an approval. The tickers match. The chains do not. A local unwrap never creates the One balance.

faqs.question: Does the ETH that arrives pay gas on One?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is the gas coin on chain 42161, not Nova. You still needed ETH on Base to approve the WETH and send the swap. Those are two balances. The amount that arrives is the quote, not a promise that surplus remains after the next transfer.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to ARB on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves, and the ARB governance token arrives on Arbitrum One.

Approve wrapped ETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan is where that allowance sits, and it costs ETH. Receive ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on chain 42161. Arbiscan lists it as the governance token, not as gas. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and is not the output. WETH on One at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is not the output either. This is Arbitrum One, not Nova.
description: Swap WETH from Base to ARB on Arbitrum One. Base WETH leaves and the ARB token arrives on chain 42161, not Nova. ARB cannot pay gas. Keep ETH on One to move it.

sections.heading: Wrapped ether for a governance token
sections.body: You are not moving WETH to Arbitrum. You are selling it for ARB, which trades on its own market. The minimum on the quote is the floor while that price can move. If the floor is a poor trade, do not sign. There is no promised bridge time and no promised ARB price. Read both numbers as they stand on the quote you are asked to sign.

sections.heading: ARB still needs ETH beside it
sections.body: Chain 42161 will not accept ARB as a fee. The ETH that paid the Base approval does not travel. If One has no ETH, Arbiscan can show the governance token and the wallet can still refuse the transfer. Fund ETH on One before you depend on sending ARB anywhere.

sections.heading: Simpler jobs that are not this page
sections.body: Unwrap on Base if you need Base ETH. Buy One WETH if a pool wants 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Buy native USDC or Tether if the order is a dollar. Stay off Nova. WBTC is not a substitute and is not native bitcoin. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) applies only when ARB on One really is the target.

sections.heading: What a correct pair of receipts looks like
sections.body: Basescan: WETH down at the predeploy. Arbiscan: ARB up at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. No native ETH increase is required for success, and none should be expected from this quote. Chain id 42161 must be selected or you will look on the wrong network.

faqs.question: Does ARB pay gas after this swap?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the governance token. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in quotes. You need that ETH on chain 42161, separate from Base. Until it is there, the ARB balance cannot be sent. Arbiscan can show the token while the wallet still refuses to move it.

faqs.question: Is this a way to move WETH onto Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. WETH on One is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. This route spends Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and delivers ARB. If the pool asked for the One WETH contract, leave this page. Arbiscan will not show a WETH credit from this quote. You sold the wrapper for ARB, and the two contracts are not substitutes.

faqs.question: What if my Base balance is native ETH?
faqs.answer: Then this route sees nothing to approve. Native ETH is the gas coin on chain 8453, not the input. Wrap into the predeploy first, or pick a route that sells native ETH for ARB. The wrap is a Base transaction and does not by itself create ARB.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Tether USDT arrives on Avalanche C-Chain.

Send Circle USDC from 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453, an L2 with ETH gas. Read it on Basescan. It has 6 decimals and needs an allowance. Receive Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Read that exact address on Snowtrace. It is not Circle's Avalanche USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Gas after arrival is AVAX, not ETH.
description: Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on chain 43114. C-Chain only, not the X-Chain. Gas is AVAX.

sections.heading: C-Chain only
sections.body: Avalanche has an X-Chain and a P-Chain that do not speak ERC-20 the way the C-Chain does. This route credits chain 43114. An X-Chain address will not show the USDT, and a wallet set to the wrong chain will look empty. Snowtrace is the C-Chain explorer. Confirm the network in the wallet is C-Chain before you search.

sections.heading: Tether, not the Circle dollar already on Avalanche
sections.body: If you wanted to keep Circle, the C-Chain USDC contract is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. This page delivers Tether instead. The older bridged USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is a third contract and is also not the output. Issuers do not become interchangeable because both prices sit near a dollar.

sections.heading: AVAX is the new fee
sections.body: ETH on Base pays the USDC approval. AVAX on the C-Chain pays the next transfer. USDT cannot pay it. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means AVAX only when C-Chain is selected. On Base it means ETH. Fund AVAX or the Tether balance sits on Snowtrace. Chain 43114 will not treat Base ETH as a fee, and the X-Chain will not show this token.

sections.heading: When not to cross
sections.body: Do not cross if the buyer of USDC is already on Base. Do not cross if you need native USDC on Avalanche. [Trade on Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) is the C-Chain context. No bridge duration is promised. If the minimum USDT is poor, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is this USDT Circle's USDC on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Circle's C-Chain USDC is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. This route delivers Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, which you must match on Snowtrace including that capitalization. The source is Base USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Different issuers, different chains. Snowtrace on the C-Chain, chain 43114, is where this Tether credit belongs on Snowtrace.

faqs.question: Will an X-Chain wallet show the USDT?
faqs.answer: No. This credit is on the C-Chain, chain 43114, not the X-Chain or the P-Chain. Use a C-Chain account and Snowtrace. USDT here is an ERC-20 style token on that chain. The X-Chain does not hold this contract. Switch the wallet to the C-Chain before you decide the transfer failed.

faqs.question: What pays gas after USDT arrives?
faqs.answer: AVAX, the native coin on the C-Chain. USDT cannot pay it, and ETH on Base cannot pay it. The 0xEeee placeholder means AVAX on chain 43114. Put AVAX on the account before you try to move the Tether. Snowtrace can show the token while the wallet still refuses.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base, and native AVAX arrives on the C-Chain.

Spend 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, Circle's USDC on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows it, and you pay ETH for the allowance and the send. Receive native AVAX on chain 43114. Quotes label it 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows AVAX on the account, not as a token contract. This is the C-Chain, not the X-Chain. Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is a different result. You are buying the fee coin.
description: Swap USDC from Base to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Circle USDC leaves Base and native AVAX arrives on chain 43114. AVAX is the C-Chain gas coin, not the X-Chain.

sections.heading: You are funding C-Chain gas
sections.body: AVAX pays fees on chain 43114. USDC could not. The quote decides how much AVAX you get, and that figure is not a monthly fee budget. A small fill can disappear into the next transactions. If you wanted to keep a dollar, this route sells it. Read the minimum before you call the result spare gas.

sections.heading: X-Chain AVAX is not this balance
sections.body: People move AVAX between the X-Chain and the C-Chain inside Avalanche wallets. This bridge does not drop value on the X-Chain. If your receiving wallet is showing an X-Chain address, you are looking in the wrong place. The C-Chain address is the EVM-style account Snowtrace understands. Chain id 43114 is the check.

sections.heading: The placeholder changes meaning
sections.body: On Base, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is ETH. On the C-Chain it is AVAX. It is not an ERC-20 you approve on the destination, because the destination asset is the gas coin itself. USDC on the source still needs an allowance. Do not paste the placeholder into Snowtrace and expect a token page.

sections.heading: Skip it for dollar-to-dollar
sections.body: Skip it if you need Tether or Circle USDC on the C-Chain. Skip it if you need ETH to remain ETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) describes the handoff, without a clock. Basescan records the USDC debit. Snowtrace records AVAX on the account. Decline a weak minimum.

faqs.question: Does this AVAX arrive on the X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. It arrives as native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114, shown on Snowtrace as the account balance. The quote writes it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The X-Chain and the P-Chain are different systems. An export from C-Chain to X-Chain would be another step, not this route.

faqs.question: Is AVAX an ERC-20 I must approve on arrival?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX is the gas coin. You do not approve it to hold it. You did approve Circle USDC on Base, at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, so the router could take the input. That allowance was chain 8453 and cost ETH. AVAX on the C-Chain is a separate coin and does not pay the Base fee.

faqs.question: I needed USDT, not AVAX. Is this close?
