faqs.answer: No. Tether on the C-Chain is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Circle USDC there is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. This page delivers the gas coin. If the order was a dollar, leave it. AVAX will not satisfy a stablecoin whitelist. If the invoice says USDT or USDC, pick the dollar route instead of the gas coin.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Native ETH leaves Base, and Circle USDC arrives on the C-Chain.

Sell the Base gas coin, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain 8453. Basescan shows the account. Leave a fee remainder. There is no approval on native ETH. Receive Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on chain 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. That is native USDC, not the old USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664, and not Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. You will need AVAX to move the USDC.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Native ETH leaves Base and Circle USDC arrives on chain 43114. It is not old USDC.e. Gas afterward is AVAX.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not USDC.e
sections.body: Some C-Chain pools still point at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. This quote credits 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Both have been called USDC. A deposit into the old contract will not see the new balance. Check Snowtrace before you tell a counterparty you paid them in Circle dollars. Six decimals will not distinguish the two.

sections.heading: You are spending Base gas
sections.body: ETH pays the send and is the asset sold. A max click can fail. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is invisible here. Unwrap or change routes. You do not arrive holding ETH, and you do not arrive holding AVAX. You arrive holding a dollar that cannot pay C-Chain fees.

sections.heading: AVAX is mandatory afterward
sections.body: Chain 43114 uses AVAX for gas. Base ETH does not convert into it. The placeholder 0xEeee means AVAX only on the C-Chain. If that balance is zero, Snowtrace can show USDC and the wallet can refuse to send it. [Trade on Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) is the C-Chain, not the X-Chain.

sections.heading: Wrong dollar, wrong chain
sections.body: Wrong if you need Tether. Wrong if a pool still wants USDC.e. Wrong if you need AVAX itself. Wrong if the USDC was supposed to stay on Base. Wrong if you send to an X-Chain address and wait. The C-Chain account is the only place this USDC can land. No bridge time is promised. Do not sign a minimum you dislike.

faqs.question: Is this the old Avalanche USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. This route delivers Circle's native USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Check Snowtrace. If the app still displays the older address, this credit will not match it. Compare the deposit address with the native Circle contract before you sign.

faqs.question: Do I approve the ETH I sell?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH on Base is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is sent rather than approved. Leave enough on chain 8453 for the fee. If the wallet asks you to approve WETH, you selected the wrapper, which is a different route. This page sells the gas coin only.

faqs.question: What do I need on the C-Chain besides USDC?
faqs.answer: AVAX, the native coin, to pay fees. USDC cannot pay them. The ETH you sold lived on Base and does not become AVAX. The X-Chain will not show this ERC-20. Stay on chain 43114 and fund AVAX before you move the Circle balance. Without it, Snowtrace can show USDC that the wallet will not send.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Native ETH leaves Base, and Tether USDT arrives on the C-Chain.

The ETH is the gas coin on Base, chain 8453, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows the account. Keep a remainder for the fee. No ERC-20 approval applies. The USDT is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on chain 43114. Match that address on Snowtrace, capitalization included. It is Tether, not Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. AVAX, not USDT, pays the next fee.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Native ETH leaves Base and Tether USDT arrives on chain 43114. Check Snowtrace. USDT cannot pay AVAX gas.

sections.heading: Match the address, not just the ticker
sections.body: Avalanche USDT is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Ethereum USDT is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and uses the same 6 decimals with a different deployer address. A habit of pasting the Ethereum contract into a C-Chain wallet will not find this balance. Snowtrace on chain 43114 is the check. Tether's freeze list still applies.

sections.heading: Circle is the other major dollar
sections.body: 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E is native USDC. 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is the older bridged USDC.e. Neither is what this quote buys. If a treasury rule says Circle only, stop. If it says Tether, this contract is the one to verify before you sign.

sections.heading: Selling Base ETH has a remainder rule
sections.body: The fee and the sold asset are the same coin on chain 8453. Leave some ETH. WETH will not be detected. You will not hold ETH on Avalanche afterward, and you will not hold AVAX unless you buy it separately. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the sequence, without a timer.

sections.heading: Where people look and see nothing
sections.body: They look on the X-Chain, or on Ethereum, or on Base after the debit and expect the USDT there. The credit is a C-Chain token on Snowtrace. Bring AVAX before you transfer it. If the minimum USDT is too low for the ETH you sell, do not sign. Ethereum's 12 second blocks are not a clock for this C-Chain credit. Snowtrace is the page that matters.

faqs.question: Which contract is the USDT on Snowtrace?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114. It is Tether. Circle's USDC is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Ethereum's Tether address will not locate this balance. Use Snowtrace, not an X-Chain explorer, when you confirm the credit. The C-Chain id is 43114, and the X-Chain will not list this token.

faqs.question: Does native ETH need an approval?
faqs.answer: No. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the Base gas coin, and you send it. Leave enough on chain 8453 to pay the fee. An approval popup means WETH or another ERC-20 is selected. That is not this route. Recheck the asset line. Native ETH is sent, not approved, on chain 8453.

faqs.question: Will USDT pay C-Chain fees?
faqs.answer: No. AVAX pays fees on chain 43114. USDT cannot. Base ETH does not become AVAX when you sell it for Tether. Fund AVAX on the C-Chain or the token sits on Snowtrace. The X-Chain will not display this contract either. Stay on Snowtrace and the C-Chain account.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Native ETH leaves Base, and native AVAX arrives on the C-Chain, chain 43114.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and that string is not one coin. On Base, chain 8453, it is ETH, the L2 gas coin, shown on Basescan as the account balance. On Avalanche it is AVAX, shown on Snowtrace as the C-Chain account balance. It is not an ERC-20. It is not the X-Chain and not the P-Chain. Leave some Base ETH for the fee. You are changing exposure from ether to AVAX, not wrapping ether.
description: Swap ETH from Base to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Native ETH leaves Base and native AVAX arrives on chain 43114. That is the C-Chain gas coin, not the X-Chain.

sections.heading: Two gas coins, one placeholder
sections.body: Wallets reuse the 0xEeee string for whatever pays fees on the selected chain. Chain id 8453 means you sell ETH. Chain id 43114 means you buy AVAX. Pasting the string into Snowtrace does not open a token. If the wallet header still says Base while you look for the result, you are staring at the coin you sold, not the coin you bought.

sections.heading: Do not drain Base, and do not use the X-Chain
sections.body: Selling the full ETH balance can fail before a bridge message exists, because the fee comes from that same coin. There is no approval on native ETH. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is a different input. An X-Chain receiving address will not display this C-Chain credit. The EVM account on chain 43114 is the one Snowtrace tracks.

sections.heading: AVAX is not a dollar and not WETH
sections.body: If you needed Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, or Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, this page is the wrong asset. If you needed ETH to remain ETH on Base or on Ethereum, stop. WBTC is unrelated and is not native bitcoin. The fit is a C-Chain account that needs the gas coin.

sections.heading: How to see the credit
sections.body: Basescan: ETH down. Snowtrace: AVAX up on the account, no token-transfer row required. [Trade on Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) means the C-Chain. No duration is promised for the bridge. Reject the quote if the minimum AVAX is too small for the ETH you give up.

faqs.question: Why do ETH and AVAX share an address in the quote?
faqs.answer: They do not share a contract. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means the native gas coin of the selected chain. On Base that is ETH. On the C-Chain that is AVAX. Snowtrace and Basescan show two account balances. Chain ids 8453 and 43114 keep them apart. The X-Chain does not use this placeholder the same way.

faqs.question: Does this AVAX land on the X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. The credit is native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114. An export from the C-Chain to the X-Chain is a separate Avalanche action, not this route. If your wallet is showing an X-Chain address, switch to the C-Chain account before you decide the funds are missing.

faqs.question: What if I spend my entire Base ETH balance?
faqs.answer: The chain 8453 fee cannot be paid, so the swap should fail before it is broadcast. Leave a remainder. Native ETH is sent, not approved. If your ether is WETH, unwrap it on Base first or use the WETH route. This page only sees the gas coin.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Base WETH leaves, and Circle's native USDC arrives on the C-Chain.

Approve 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows that ERC-20, and the approval costs ETH. Native ETH, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, is not the input. Receive 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. The old USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is not this credit. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. You need AVAX before the USDC can move.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Base WETH leaves and Circle USDC arrives on chain 43114. It is not old USDC.e. You need AVAX for gas.

sections.heading: The allowance never leaves Base
sections.body: You grant a router the right to take Base WETH. Read the spender and the cap. That signature is chain 8453. It does not approve USDC on Avalanche, and it does not sell native ETH. If the WETH balance is zero, wrap first or switch routes. Declining the allowance ends the attempt cleanly, with no bridge message sent.

sections.heading: Native USDC versus the older bridged token
sections.body: C-Chain apps have not all moved off 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. This quote credits 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Depositing into the old market will not see your balance. Decimals are 6 on both, so the width of the integer is not the test. Open Snowtrace and match the address the app displays.

sections.heading: AVAX, the X-Chain, and Tether
sections.body: USDT at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is a different issuer. AVAX is the fee coin this route does not buy. An X-Chain address will not hold this ERC-20. ETH spent on Base stays on Base. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the split receipts and does not give a duration.

sections.heading: A usable arrival
sections.body: Snowtrace should show USDC at the native Circle contract on chain 43114, and the account should hold AVAX or the token cannot be forwarded. Basescan should show the WETH debit. If the minimum USDC is below your floor, do not sign. Chain 43114 is the C-Chain, not the X-Chain, and the wrong chain hides this Circle balance even after Snowtrace shows it.

faqs.question: Is this Avalanche USDC the old USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. This route delivers 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Check Snowtrace. If the app still names the older contract, this credit will not satisfy that deposit. Read the address in the app and compare it on Snowtrace before you sign.

faqs.question: Can I pay with native ETH instead of WETH?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and pays the Base fee. The input is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Wrap on chain 8453 first, or choose the route that sells the gas coin. An empty WETH balance cannot be approved. The gas coin and the wrapper are different balances on Base.

faqs.question: What has to sit beside the USDC?
faqs.answer: AVAX, the C-Chain gas coin. USDC cannot pay fees, and Base ETH does not become AVAX. The X-Chain will not show this token. Fund AVAX on chain 43114 or Snowtrace can display a balance the wallet will not send. USDC never becomes the fee coin.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Wrapped ETH leaves Base, and Tether USDT arrives on the C-Chain.

Approve 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453, and confirm it on Basescan. The fee is ETH. Receive 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on chain 43114. Match that address on Snowtrace, including the lowercase hex. It is Tether, not Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and not USDC.e. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Native gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning ETH on Base and AVAX on the destination. You are buying neither.
description: Swap WETH from Base to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Base WETH leaves and Tether USDT arrives on chain 43114. Check Snowtrace now. USDT cannot pay AVAX gas.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals in, six decimals out
sections.body: WETH uses 18 decimals. This USDT uses 6. The log integers will not look like a one-for-one move, and they should not. Read the human amounts on the quote. You are selling ether exposure for Tether. A script that assumes both legs share a decimal width will mis-state the fill.

sections.heading: The address is case-sensitive in the way you compare it
sections.body: Use 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 exactly when you search Snowtrace. Ethereum's Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, is a different chain and will not locate this balance. Tether can freeze listed addresses. Bridging from Base does not clear that status.

sections.heading: Circle and the X-Chain are the usual misses
sections.body: If the rule is Circle only, buy 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E instead. If the wallet is on the X-Chain, you will not see an ERC-20 credit. If you hold native ETH rather than WETH, this page has no input. If you need AVAX for gas, this USDT will not provide it. [Trade on Base](/chains/base) is only the source network.

sections.heading: Receipts
sections.body: Basescan shows the WETH allowance and debit. Snowtrace shows USDT on the C-Chain. No shared hash, and no promised wait. Bring AVAX before you forward the dollars. Decline the quote when the minimum is worse than you will take. Ethereum's 12 second blocks are not a timer for this C-Chain credit. Snowtrace is the page that shows the Tether.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract belongs on Snowtrace?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114. It is Tether. Circle's USDC is a different contract, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Ethereum's Tether address will not find this balance. The X-Chain does not hold the contract either. Stay on Snowtrace and chain 43114 when you search for this credit before you sign.

faqs.question: Does Base WETH need an approval?
faqs.answer: Yes. 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is an ERC-20 on chain 8453. The router needs an allowance, paid in ETH. Native ETH is not the asset sold. You do not approve USDT in order to receive it. A later C-Chain spend of USDT would be a new signature, paid in AVAX.

faqs.question: Will this USDT pay C-Chain gas?
faqs.answer: No. AVAX pays fees on chain 43114. USDT cannot. The ETH used on Base stays on Base. Put AVAX on the C-Chain account or the Tether balance is visible on Snowtrace and still stuck. This route does not deliver the 0xEeee gas coin. AVAX has to be funded on its own.

intro:
Swap WETH from Base to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Base WETH leaves, and native AVAX arrives on the C-Chain, chain 43114.

You approve 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows the ERC-20. The approval costs ETH. You receive native AVAX, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows it on the C-Chain account, not as a token. Unwrapping on Base would have returned ETH on Base, which cannot pay Avalanche fees. This is not the X-Chain. Tether and Circle USDC are different outputs.
description: Swap WETH from Base to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Base WETH leaves and native AVAX arrives on chain 43114. It is C-Chain gas, not an unwrap or the X-Chain.

sections.heading: Wrapper in, fee coin out
sections.body: You give up an ERC-20 claim on ETH and receive the coin that pays C-Chain fees. The quote sets the amount. It is not sized as a reserve for later transactions. A small fill can be consumed quickly. Read the minimum before you treat the result as a funded gas tank.

sections.heading: The Base approval still needs ETH
sections.body: WETH cannot pay the allowance fee until it is unwrapped, and unwrapping would take you off this route. Keep a little ETH on chain 8453. AVAX is not on Base yet, so it cannot help. If you decline the spender, the router cannot pull the wrapper.

sections.heading: Not an unwrap, not a dollar, not the X-Chain
sections.body: A local unwrap credits ETH on Base. A dollar route credits 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E or 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. An X-Chain address will not show this native C-Chain balance. WBTC is not part of the trade and is not native bitcoin. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing path, not a timer.

sections.heading: What success looks like
sections.body: WETH down on Basescan. AVAX up on the Snowtrace account for chain 43114. No token contract page for the arrival. If you see a USDT transfer, you signed a different quote. No bridge duration is stated here. The C-Chain id is 43114, and an X-Chain balance is not a substitute for the AVAX this quote buys.

faqs.question: Is the AVAX I receive an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: No. It is the native gas coin on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Quotes label it 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Snowtrace shows the account. The X-Chain is a different system. If a dapp asked for a token contract rather than the gas coin, this route did not provide that contract.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap Base WETH instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the ETH stays on Base, chain 8453. Unwrapping burns 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 locally. This page sends that wrapper toward the C-Chain and credits AVAX. Use the unwrap only when you intend to stay on Base and pay Base fees. This hop exists only when the AVAX must sit on the C-Chain.

faqs.question: What pays for the WETH approval?
faqs.answer: ETH on Base. The wrapper is the token being approved, not the coin that pays gas. AVAX cannot cover that fee because it is not on chain 8453 yet. Keep a little ETH beside the WETH or the allowance cannot be mined. AVAX arrives later and cannot pay this Base fee.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Solana. Circle USDC leaves Base, and Tether's SPL USDT mint arrives on Solana.

Send 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, Circle's USDC on Base, chain 8453. Basescan shows that ERC-20, and you approve it with ETH as gas. Receive the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Solscan is the explorer. That mint is Tether, not Circle's Solana USDC at EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solana has no ERC-20 approval. A Phantom or similar Solana wallet must hold the destination. MetaMask on Base cannot display the SPL balance.
description: Swap USDC from Base to USDT on Solana. Circle USDC leaves Base and Tether's SPL mint arrives. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Use Phantom and Solscan.

sections.heading: The wallet has to change jobs
sections.body: Base is an EVM L2. Solana is not. The address you paste as a Solana receiver is not a 0x address. If you only have MetaMask, you do not have a place for this USDT to land. Phantom, Solflare, or another SPL wallet is the receiving side. The sending side still signs on Base, chain 8453, with ETH for gas.

sections.heading: No approval on the Solana mint
sections.body: ERC-20 approvals exist on Base for the USDC you spend. They do not exist on Solana. The destination may need an associated token account for Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, which is not the same thing as an allowance. Do not wait for a Solana approve button that will not appear. SOL, the native coin, pays Solana fees, and this route does not claim to include it.

sections.heading: Circle's mint is the wrong finish
sections.body: If the order says USDC on Solana, the mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, and this page delivers Tether instead. If both dollars already sit on Base, do not bridge. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the handoff between an EVM contract and an SPL mint. No arrival time is promised.

sections.heading: How to confirm
sections.body: Basescan: USDC debit at the Circle contract. Solscan: the Es9v mint credited to the Solana address you named. A Base hash will not open as a Solana transaction. If the minimum USDT is poor, do not sign.

faqs.question: Can MetaMask hold the USDT from this route?
faqs.answer: MetaMask can hold the Base USDC you spend, at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. It cannot hold the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Use Phantom or another Solana wallet for the credit, and check Solscan. There is no ERC-20 approval step on Solana. SOL pays Solana fees, and this route does not replace that coin.

faqs.question: Is this the same USDT as on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The issuer is Tether, but the asset is an SPL mint, Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, not the Ethereum contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Circle's Solana USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. If the order says Circle, this Tether mint is the wrong arrival. Check Solscan for the mint before you call the payment done.

faqs.question: Do I approve USDT on Solana before it arrives?
faqs.answer: No. Solana does not use ERC-20 approvals. You approve USDC on Base if the router must pull it, and that costs ETH on chain 8453. The Solana side may create a token account for the mint. SOL pays Solana fees, and this USDT route does not replace that native coin.

intro:
Swap USDC from Base to SOL on Solana. Circle USDC leaves Base, and SOL arrives through the wrapped SOL mint.

Spend Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, chain 8453. Basescan is the explorer, and ETH pays the fee. The destination mint in this quote is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. That is the wrapped SOL mint routes use to represent SOL. It is not an ERC-20 on Base. Solscan shows it. Native SOL pays Solana fees. Phantom, not MetaMask, holds the result. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana.
description: Swap USDC from Base to SOL on Solana. Circle USDC leaves Base and the wrapped SOL mint arrives. Phantom holds it. Solana has no ERC-20 approval. Check Solscan.

sections.heading: Why the mint is all ones and a two
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the canonical wrapped SOL mint. Quotes use it when the thing you buy is SOL. It is not a meme coin that happens to look repetitive, and it is not native SOL stored as an ERC-20. If you expected a 0x contract called SOL on Base, this route is the wrong shape. You are leaving the EVM.

sections.heading: Phantom, fees, and the missing approve button
sections.body: The receiving wallet must speak Solana. MetaMask on Base can sign the USDC side and then has nowhere to show the mint. SOL is the fee coin on Solana. Wrapped SOL and native SOL are closely related in wallets, and you should still confirm on Solscan that the mint is the one above. No Solana ERC-20 allowance will be requested, because that standard is not how SPL tokens move.

sections.heading: Dollars you might have meant to keep
sections.body: Tether's mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Circle's Solana USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Neither is the output here. If you needed a stable on Solana, stop. If you needed ETH on Base, stop. [Trade on Solana](/chains/solana) is the destination context. No fill time is promised.

sections.heading: Checking both sides
sections.body: Debit the Circle contract on Basescan. Credit the wrapped SOL mint on Solscan to the Solana address you supplied. Leave ETH on Base so the approval can be paid. If the minimum SOL is too small, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is So111... an ERC-20 on Base?
faqs.answer: No. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the wrapped SOL mint on Solana. The token you spend is Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base. MetaMask cannot hold the mint. Use Phantom and confirm the mint on Solscan. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana side. Native SOL is what pays Solana fees, separate from this mint.

faqs.question: Does this deliver native SOL or only the wrapped mint?
faqs.answer: The quote's destination is the wrapped SOL mint, which is how SPL routes represent SOL. Wallets often treat that balance as SOL, and native SOL is what pays fees. If you wanted an ERC-20 named SOL on Base, this page is wrong. Read Solscan before you assume a different mint arrived.

faqs.question: What pays fees on each side?
faqs.answer: ETH pays Base, chain 8453, including the USDC allowance. SOL pays Solana. USDC cannot pay either fee by itself. Keep ETH on Base for the send. Have a Solana wallet ready, because the credit will not appear inside an EVM account. Phantom or a similar wallet has to be the receiver.

intro:
Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Solana. Native ETH leaves Base, and Circle's SPL USDC mint arrives on Solana.

You sell Base ETH, the gas coin, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain 8453. Basescan shows the account. Leave a remainder for the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval on native ETH. You receive the SPL mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan is the explorer. That is Circle USDC on Solana, not Tether's Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, and not Ethereum USDC. Phantom must receive it. Solana does not use ERC-20 approvals.
description: Swap ETH from Base to USDC on Solana. Native ETH leaves Base and Circle's SPL USDC arrives. Use Phantom and Solscan. Solana has no ERC-20 approval step.

sections.heading: Selling L2 gas for an SPL dollar
sections.body: ETH on Base pays fees and, here, is also what you sell. Do not spend the full balance. WETH is not the input. The arrival is a Solana mint, so the value leaves the EVM. You will not hold ETH on Solana, and you will not hold Base ETH in place of the dollars. Size the trade so the fee still fits.

sections.heading: Phantom is not optional
sections.body: MetaMask can sign the Base transaction and cannot store EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Put a Solana address from Phantom or a similar wallet on the receiving side. Solscan is where that mint should appear. An associated token account may be created. That is not an ERC-20 approval, and you should not look for one.

sections.heading: Tether and Ethereum USDC are other contracts
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is Tether on Solana. 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is Circle on Ethereum, chain 1. Neither is this credit. If the written order names those, stop. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the wallet change. It does not promise a duration.

sections.heading: SOL still pays Solana
sections.body: The USDC mint does not pay Solana fees. Native SOL does. This route does not claim to deliver a pile of SOL for fees. Have a little SOL in the Phantom account if you must move the USDC after it lands. If the minimum USDC is too low, do not sign.

faqs.question: Which mint should Solscan show?
faqs.answer: Circle's USDC mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Tether is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. The source is native ETH on Base, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain 8453, not an ERC-20 approval. Confirm the mint on Solscan, not on Basescan. MetaMask cannot store that SPL balance, so Phantom has to be ready before you sign anything.

faqs.question: Can I receive this USDC in MetaMask?
faqs.answer: No. MetaMask holds the Base side. The credit is an SPL mint and needs Phantom or another Solana wallet. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. If you paste a 0x address as the receiver, you are not naming a Solana account. Fix the destination before you sign.

faqs.question: Is Solana USDT the Ethereum Tether contract?

faqs.question: Does the USDT include SOL for fees?

sections.heading: Phantom, not an approve popup
sections.body: MetaMask can sign the Base debit and cannot store the mint. Paste a Solana address. Do not look for an ERC-20 approval on Solscan. An associated token account is a different mechanism. sections.heading: What to refuse

faqs.question: Is So111 an ERC-20 I hold in MetaMask?

MetaMask cannot store the mint. Use Phantom and confirm it on Solscan. Solana does not use ERC-20 approvals. Native SOL pays fees and is separate from the mint.

faqs.question: Does this include extra SOL for fees?

faqs.question: I wanted USDC on Solana, not SOL. Is this it?

intro:

description: Swap WETH from Base to USDC on Solana. Base WETH leaves and Circle's SPL USDC arrives. Phantom holds it. Solscan checks the mint. No ERC-20 approval on Solana.

sections.heading: Approval stays on Base
sections.body: The router needs an allowance on Base WETH. Read the spender. That signature costs ETH on chain 8453. sections.body: MetaMask cannot display the mint. Phantom can. SOL must already be available if you need to move USDC after it lands. faqs.question: Does Solana ask me to approve USDC?

faqs.question: Do I approve anything on Solana?

faqs.question: Does the wrapped SOL mint pay Solana fees by itself?

faqs.question: What if the order was a stablecoin?

sections.heading: C-Chain source, mainnet Tether
sections.body: An X-Chain balance is not this USDC. Chain 43114 is the EVM chain Snowtrace follows. You approve the Circle contract there if the router must pull it, and AVAX pays that approval. The arrival on Ethereum is Tether, 6 decimals, with the old transfer behavior traders already know. It is not a rename of the USDC you sent.

sections.heading: Circle on Ethereum is a different contract

sections.heading: Two gas coins
sections.body: AVAX starts the send. ETH on chain 1 moves the USDT afterward. Neither dollar pays those fees, and AVAX does not become ETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why Snowtrace and Etherscan do not share a hash. Twelve second blocks are Ethereum's cadence, not a bridge promise.

sections.heading: Stay home if you can
sections.body: If the buyer of Circle dollars is already on the C-Chain, do not bridge. If you need USDC to remain USDC on Ethereum, pick that route instead. If the minimum USDT is poor, do not sign. The old Avalanche USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is not the input here.

faqs.question: Is Ethereum USDT the same token I sent?

faqs.question: Will the X-Chain show this transfer?
faqs.answer: No. The source is C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. The destination is Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. The X-Chain and the P-Chain do not hold this USDC contract. Use the C-Chain account when you approve, and use AVAX for that fee. Ethereum ETH is a second balance you need later, and it does not come from the C-Chain.

faqs.question: Can USDT pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain 1 is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds once you have it. USDT cannot pay the fee. AVAX on the C-Chain cannot pay it either. Fund Ethereum with ETH or the Tether balance sits on Etherscan and does not move.

sections.heading: Maker's dollar against Circle's
sections.body: DAI is minted through Maker's system. Circle does not redeem it. A rule that allows only fiat-issued stables should stop here even if the quote looks like a dollar trade. The contract on Etherscan is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. If the instruction said Tether, the contract is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 instead.

sections.heading: Six decimals become eighteen
sections.body: 100 USDC is a 6 decimal integer. 100 DAI is an 18 decimal integer. Wallets hide that. Event logs do not. Do not compare base units across Snowtrace and Etherscan and call the trade broken. Compare the human amounts, then the contracts. The price of one USDC is not the integer width.

sections.heading: Gas and the chains that are not involved
sections.body: AVAX on the C-Chain sends. ETH on Ethereum moves DAI later. The X-Chain will not show either leg. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the destination context, including the 12 second blocks, which are not a bridge timer. USDC.e on Avalanche is not the token you are spending.

sections.heading: Wrong job

faqs.question: Is DAI redeemable at Circle?

faqs.question: Why is the Etherscan integer so much larger?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals. The USDC you sent uses 6. A similar dollar amount produces a much wider base-unit number on the DAI transfer. Read the wallet figure, and confirm the contract on Etherscan. Chain 1 blocks are about 12 seconds. That is not the bridge wait.

faqs.question: What pays gas on each side?
faqs.answer: AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114, not the X-Chain. ETH on Ethereum after DAI arrives. DAI cannot pay Ethereum gas. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means whichever native coin the selected chain uses, and this route's assets are the two dollar contracts, not that placeholder. Fund AVAX first and ETH later, or the dollars cannot move on one of the two chains.

description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and native ETH arrives on mainnet. That ETH is the gas coin, not WETH.

sections.heading: The arrival can pay mainnet fees
sections.body: Unlike a USDT or DAI finish, the asset you buy is the fee coin on chain 1. Later transactions can spend it. The amount is still the quote, not a calculated gas stipend. WETH is what you would hold if a contract required 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and this route has not wrapped anything for you.

sections.heading: AVAX does not travel as ETH
sections.body: You need AVAX on the C-Chain to start, because USDC cannot pay that fee. You are not relocating AVAX. You are selling Circle dollars for ether on Ethereum. If the C-Chain account must keep USDC, this page works against that. The X-Chain is the wrong place to look for either balance.

sections.heading: Placeholder versus contract
sections.body: Do not paste 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE into Etherscan's token search and expect an ERC-20. On this destination it means native ETH. On the C-Chain the same string would mean AVAX, which is not the output. The input you do approve, if asked, is the USDC contract on Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Refuse the obvious mismatches
sections.body: [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) separates the two explorers. Refuse the quote for Tether, DAI, or Ethereum USDC. Refuse it for WETH. Refuse it if the minimum ETH is too small. Twelve second blocks are not a delivery promise. AVAX on the C-Chain starts the send, and ETH on Ethereum is a separate balance you still need if you wrap later.

faqs.question: Does this ETH count as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin on Ethereum, chain 1, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Etherscan shows the account balance. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. A pool that accepts only WETH will not see this balance until you wrap it. That wrap is a separate step. This route stops at native ETH on the account in Etherscan.

faqs.question: Where does the USDC leave from?
faqs.answer: Circle's contract 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114, which you check on Snowtrace. Not the X-Chain, and not USDC.e. AVAX pays the C-Chain fee. The ETH credit is on Etherscan and will not appear in the Snowtrace USDC balance. Chain 1 is Ethereum, and the X-Chain is neither side of this hop.

faqs.question: Is the 12 second block the arrival time?
faqs.answer: No. About 12 seconds is how often Ethereum produces a block. The bridge wait sits on top of that and is not stated here. If the quote expires, request another. AVAX on the C-Chain and ETH on Ethereum remain separate gas coins throughout. Fund both if you need to send on each chain.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and canonical WETH arrives on Ethereum.

Send 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E from Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer, and AVAX is the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. That is canonical WETH, an ERC-20. It is not native ETH, so it cannot pay gas. Native ETH is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Blocks are about 12 seconds. You need some ETH on Ethereum already if you want to unwrap.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and canonical WETH arrives on mainnet. WETH cannot pay gas until unwrapped.

sections.heading: Why the canonical contract matters
sections.body: Ethereum applications that cannot hold native ETH inside a token call use 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Depositing ETH there mints WETH. This route buys that WETH with C-Chain USDC. It does not wrap AVAX, and it does not leave you with spendable mainnet gas. If the pool gave you this address, you are on the right output. If it gave you the 0xEeee placeholder, you are not.

sections.heading: USDC.e and Tether are not substitutes
sections.body: The input must be native Circle USDC, not 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. The output is not Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and not DAI. Selling dollars for WETH also takes ETH price risk. Read the minimum WETH. A dollar-looking quote that delivers WETH is a different position than the USDC you hold now.

sections.heading: ETH you still have to own
sections.body: Unwrap or a later approval of WETH costs ETH on chain 1. AVAX will not pay it. Base and other L2 WETH contracts, including 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, are not this arrival. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that canonical WETH lives. No bridge duration is promised.

sections.heading: C-Chain discipline
sections.body: Approve on chain 43114, with AVAX in the account. Look for the result on Etherscan, not on the X-Chain and not in the native ETH line. If the minimum is worse than you will accept, do not sign. Chain 1 blocks run about every 12 seconds and do not time the bridge.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. Gas is native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, on chain 1. You need some ETH before you can unwrap. AVAX on the C-Chain does not cover that fee. Blocks are about 12 seconds only after the transaction is paid for.

faqs.question: Is the USDC I send the old USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. The input is Circle's native USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on the C-Chain, chain 43114, checked on Snowtrace. USDC.e is 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. The X-Chain does not hold this contract. AVAX pays the send on the C-Chain, and it does not arrive on Ethereum as gas for you.

faqs.question: What if the app wants native ETH, not WETH?
faqs.answer: Choose the route that delivers the gas coin. This page stops at canonical WETH. Unwrapping is extra, and it needs ETH you did not receive here. If you only wanted to keep a dollar, Tether and Ethereum USDC are different pages. Do not sign a WETH minimum for a fee top-up.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum mainnet.

Send 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 from Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Match that address on Snowtrace. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Receive Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. Both dollars use 6 decimals. The issuers differ. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the arrival. Blocks are about 12 seconds. ETH, not USDC, pays mainnet gas. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native gas, not either token.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Ethereum. Tether leaves the C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on mainnet. Not the X-Chain. USDC cannot pay ETH gas.

sections.heading: Tether out, Circle in
sections.body: You are changing issuer, not just chain. A whitelist that names Tether on Ethereum will reject this credit. A whitelist that names Circle will accept 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and will ignore the Avalanche USDT you started with. Six decimals on both sides only means the integer width matches. It does not mean the companies match. Read Etherscan before you tell a desk the dollars arrived.

sections.heading: C-Chain is the only Avalanche side
sections.body: The X-Chain and the P-Chain do not hold this USDT contract. Approve, if the wallet asks, on chain 43114, and pay AVAX. USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is not the input. Circle's C-Chain USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E is also not the input. If you are holding that USDC, you are on a different page.

sections.heading: Mainnet gas is a second coin
sections.body: USDC cannot pay Ethereum fees. AVAX cannot pay them either. Put ETH on chain 1 before you plan to forward the Circle balance. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why Snowtrace and Etherscan do not share a hash. The 12 second block time is not a bridge promise. Decline a minimum you will not accept.

sections.heading: When to keep the ticker
sections.body: If the counterparty asked for Tether on Ethereum, stop and use the route that delivers 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. If they asked for DAI, stop. If the USDT buyer is already on the C-Chain, do not bridge. This page fits only when Circle's mainnet contract is the balance you meant to hold.

faqs.question: Is this Circle USDC the same asset as the USDT I sent?
faqs.answer: No. You send Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain. You receive Circle at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, checked on Etherscan. Both use 6 decimals. Ethereum's own Tether contract is different again. Match the issuer the other side named before you sign. Etherscan is the page that proves which dollar arrived.

faqs.question: Does the X-Chain participate?
faqs.answer: No. The source is C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. The destination is Ethereum, chain 1. The X-Chain and the P-Chain do not hold this USDT. AVAX pays the C-Chain fee. ETH pays anything you do with the USDC after it shows on Etherscan. AVAX cannot take that role.

faqs.question: Will the USDC pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain 1 is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds once that ETH is available. USDC cannot pay the fee. AVAX on Avalanche does not become that ETH. Fund mainnet separately or the Circle balance sits visible and stuck. Twelve second blocks start only after that ETH is in the account.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to DAI on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum.

The USDT is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on chain 43114. Snowtrace must show that address. AVAX pays the send. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. The DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. DAI is Maker's token and uses 18 decimals. USDT uses 6. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI is not Circle and not Tether. Native gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and neither dollar is that gas coin.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to DAI on Ethereum. Tether leaves the C-Chain and Maker DAI arrives on mainnet. DAI has 18 decimals. It is not Circle USDC.

sections.heading: From a fiat-issued token to Maker
sections.body: Tether and Circle are companies that issue dollars. DAI is created in Maker's system. If your policy allows only fiat-issued stables, DAI fails the policy even when the screen shows a price near one dollar. The contract check is Etherscan for 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Anything else, including Ethereum USDT, is a different trade.

sections.heading: The integer will look inflated
sections.body: A transfer of DAI uses 18 decimals, so the base-unit number on Etherscan is vastly wider than the 6 decimal USDT you sent from Snowtrace. The wallet amount is the one to trust. Do not file a missing-funds note because the raw integers disagree. Then confirm you are on chain 1, not still refreshing the C-Chain.

sections.heading: Fees on both ends
sections.body: AVAX moves the USDT off chain 43114. ETH moves the DAI once it exists on Ethereum. DAI cannot pay that second fee. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the destination note. Twelve second blocks describe Ethereum, not the bridge wait. The old USDC.e contract is irrelevant to this input.

sections.heading: Stop if the dollar name was loose
sections.body: Stop if the written asset is USDC, on Avalanche or on Ethereum. Stop if it is Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Stop if you need native ETH or WETH. Stop if the minimum DAI is a worse price than you will take. No arrival time is stated.

faqs.question: Is DAI the same kind of dollar as USDT?
faqs.answer: No. USDT at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is Tether and uses 6 decimals. DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is Maker and uses 18 decimals. Circle is a third issuer. A Tether or Circle redemption desk will not take this DAI. Check Etherscan before you treat the invoice as settled. Maker will not pass a Tether or Circle redemption desk.

faqs.question: Why does the raw DAI amount look enormous?
faqs.answer: Eighteen decimals make the base units large. The USDT you sent uses 6. Compare human amounts in the wallet, not the event-log integers across Snowtrace and Etherscan. Chain 1 blocks are about 12 seconds. That figure is not how long the bridge takes. Request a new quote if the old one expires.

faqs.question: What token pays each fee?
faqs.answer: AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114, not the X-Chain. ETH on Ethereum after the DAI arrives. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means the native coin of the chain you have selected. Neither USDT nor DAI can substitute for it. Keep AVAX for the send and ETH for the arrival.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and native ETH arrives on Ethereum.

Spend 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Tether. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Receive native ETH on Ethereum, chain 1. Quotes write it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Etherscan shows the account balance, not a token page. Blocks are about 12 seconds. That ETH is the gas coin. It is not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and it is not Circle USDC.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Ethereum. Tether leaves the C-Chain and native ETH arrives on mainnet. That ETH is the gas coin, not WETH now.

sections.heading: You are buying the fee coin
sections.body: USDT on the way out cannot pay Ethereum gas. ETH on the way in can, once it is credited. The quote's minimum is the amount, not a reserve sized for later transactions. If a contract wants WETH, you still have to wrap. If a contract wants a dollar, you have sold the dollar and this page was the wrong finish.

sections.heading: AVAX starts it, ETH finishes as the asset
sections.body: The C-Chain fee is AVAX. You are not moving AVAX to Ethereum. You are selling Tether for ether. Keep enough AVAX to broadcast. The X-Chain will not display the USDT debit or the ETH credit. Chain id 43114 and chain id 1 are the pair to watch.

sections.heading: Do not search the placeholder as a token
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native ETH on this destination and would mean AVAX if the selected chain were the C-Chain. It is not an ERC-20 page on Etherscan. The token you may approve is the USDT contract on Snowtrace. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the two receipts without putting a clock on them.

sections.heading: Other outputs that belong on other pages
sections.body: Circle USDC, Maker DAI, and Ethereum Tether are different arrivals. Canonical WETH is a different arrival. Staying in USDT on the C-Chain is a different job entirely. If the minimum ETH is too small for the Tether you give up, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is the ETH I receive WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Etherscan shows it on the account. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Pools that take only that contract ignore the native balance until you wrap. Wrapping is not included in this route. Chain 1 blocks are about 12 seconds.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract leaves Avalanche?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114, checked on Snowtrace. It is Tether. The X-Chain does not hold it. AVAX pays the send. The ETH you receive will not show up inside that USDT contract. Look at the account on Etherscan instead. Chain 1 is where that ETH balance lives.

faqs.question: Does selling USDT give me Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: It gives you native ETH on Ethereum, which is the gas coin, in the amount the quote delivers. It does not give you AVAX, and it does not leave your C-Chain USDT in place. Keep AVAX for the send itself. The bridge wait is not the 12 second block time.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and canonical WETH arrives on Ethereum.

Send 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 from chain 43114. Snowtrace is the check, and AVAX is the fee. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. That WETH is an ERC-20 claim on ETH. It is not the gas coin. The gas coin is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Blocks are about 12 seconds. You need some native ETH already on Ethereum if you intend to unwrap or to move the WETH.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Ethereum. Tether leaves the C-Chain and canonical WETH arrives on mainnet. WETH cannot pay gas. You still need ETH.

sections.heading: Canonical WETH is a specific contract
sections.body: Mainnet pools that want wrapped ether want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, not a WETH deployment from Base or Arbitrum, and not native ETH. This route buys that contract with C-Chain Tether. It does not wrap a coin you already hold on Ethereum. If the app address is the 0xEeee placeholder, you wanted the gas coin and should leave this page.

sections.heading: Tether is not Circle and not DAI
sections.body: If the source of funds was supposed to stay a dollar, WETH is the wrong exit because you take ETH price exposure. If the dollar that arrives was supposed to be Circle, the contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. If it was supposed to remain Tether, the contract is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Read the minimum WETH before you accept the price risk.

sections.heading: Gas you do not receive
sections.body: AVAX pays chain 43114. ETH pays chain 1, and this WETH will not substitute until it is unwrapped, which itself costs ETH. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where canonical WETH is used. Twelve second blocks are not a promise for the bridge. The X-Chain will not show either leg.

sections.heading: Input hygiene
sections.body: The USDT address includes the lowercase form 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Do not substitute Circle's C-Chain USDC. Do not substitute USDC.e. If the wallet has no AVAX, the approval or the send cannot be broadcast. Decline a quote whose minimum you would not keep.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay Ethereum fees?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. Gas is native ETH on chain 1, the 0xEeee placeholder. You need some of that ETH before you unwrap. AVAX on the C-Chain does not cover it. Blocks are about 12 seconds only after the fee is paid.

faqs.question: Which token am I spending on Snowtrace?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Not Circle USDC, and not the X-Chain. AVAX pays the send. The WETH credit appears on Etherscan at the canonical contract, not as native ETH on the account, and you still need ETH before that WETH can move.

faqs.question: What if I wanted native ETH instead?
faqs.answer: Use the route that delivers the gas coin. This page stops at WETH. Unwrapping is extra and needs ETH you did not buy here. If you wanted to remain in Tether or move to Circle, those are dollar routes. Do not sign a WETH quote as a fee top-up.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum.

You sell the C-Chain gas coin, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain 43114. Snowtrace shows the account, not a token. Leave enough AVAX for the fee. There is no ERC-20 approval on native AVAX. This is not the X-Chain. You receive Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. It uses 6 decimals. It is not Tether and not DAI. Blocks are about 12 seconds. USDC cannot pay Ethereum gas.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and Circle USDC arrives on mainnet. USDC cannot pay ETH gas on Etherscan.

sections.heading: Spending the fee coin on purpose
sections.body: AVAX pays C-Chain fees and, here, is also the asset sold. A max click can fail before any bridge message. If your AVAX is on the X-Chain, this EVM route cannot see it. Move to the C-Chain first, outside this page, or you will be signing against an empty balance. You do not arrive holding AVAX on Ethereum.

sections.heading: Circle, specifically, on mainnet
sections.body: 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is the long-standing Circle contract. Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 will not satisfy a Circle whitelist. DAI will not either. C-Chain USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E is a different chain's Circle token and is not what you receive. Six decimals describe the arrival, not the AVAX you sold.

sections.heading: ETH afterward
sections.body: The USDC cannot move on chain 1 without ETH. The AVAX you sold does not become that ETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) separates Snowtrace from Etherscan. Twelve second blocks are Ethereum's cadence. They are not a promised delivery time. If the minimum USDC is poor, do not sign.

sections.heading: Wrong when you wanted to keep AVAX exposure
sections.body: Wrong if the goal was ETH the gas coin, or WETH. Wrong if the goal was Tether. Wrong if you only needed USDC already listed on the C-Chain. Wrong if the wallet network is still Avalanche while you search Etherscan and conclude the funds vanished.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX before this swap?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is sent rather than approved. Leave enough on the C-Chain, chain 43114, to pay the fee. The X-Chain is not this balance. An approval popup means a token such as USDT is selected, which is a different route.

faqs.question: Which USDC arrives on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Circle's Ethereum USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. It is not Tether and not Maker DAI. The source is native AVAX on Snowtrace, chain 43114, not an ERC-20. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds once a transaction is broadcast, which is not the bridge wait. USDC still needs ETH before it can move.

faqs.question: Will I have ETH for gas on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Not from this route. You sold AVAX and bought USDC. USDC does not pay gas on chain 1. Bring ETH to Ethereum before you try to transfer the dollars. AVAX left behind on the C-Chain, if any, cannot pay that mainnet fee. Fund Ethereum ETH on purpose.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and Tether USDT arrives on Ethereum.

Sell C-Chain AVAX, chain 43114, placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Keep a fee remainder. No approval applies to native AVAX. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Receive Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. It uses 6 decimals. It is not Circle USDC. Blocks are about 12 seconds. USDT cannot pay Ethereum gas, so you need ETH on mainnet from somewhere else. C-Chain Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is not the output.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on mainnet. USDT cannot pay ETH gas on Etherscan.

sections.heading: Tether on mainnet, not the C-Chain copy
sections.body: People who already hold 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 sometimes think this route moves that token. It does not. It sells AVAX and buys Ethereum Tether. The contracts differ. Tether can freeze addresses on the destination contract. Selling AVAX does not change a freeze that already applies to you.

sections.heading: Leave AVAX for the broadcast
sections.body: The coin you sell is the coin that pays the C-Chain fee. Drain it and the transaction never starts. There is no ERC-20 approval. If the balance is on the X-Chain, switch to the C-Chain before you look at this quote. You will not hold AVAX on Ethereum when the trade completes.

sections.heading: Mainnet still wants ETH
sections.body: USDT is an old ERC-20 and cannot pay gas. Blocks on chain 1 are about 12 seconds when you do have ETH. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is that fee environment. Snowtrace will show AVAX leaving. Etherscan will show USDT arriving. No shared hash, and no promised wait.

sections.heading: Dollar choice
sections.body: Circle's contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. DAI is Maker's. If either of those was named, leave. If you wanted WETH or native ETH, leave. If the minimum USDT is a bad sale of AVAX, leave the quote unsigned. Chain 1 blocks take about 12 seconds and do not time this bridge.

faqs.question: Is this the USDT I already hold on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Avalanche Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. This route sells native AVAX and delivers Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, which you check on Etherscan. The source network is the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace, not the X-Chain. The two Tether contracts are not interchangeable, even when the ticker matches.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX?
faqs.answer: No. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the gas coin, and you send it. Leave enough AVAX on chain 43114 for the fee. An approval request means a token is selected. Recheck the asset. This page does not pull USDT or USDC as the input. Native AVAX is not an ERC-20.

faqs.question: Can the USDT I receive pay mainnet fees?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum gas is ETH. USDT cannot pay it, and the AVAX you sold does not reappear as ETH. Blocks are about 12 seconds only after you have ETH to spend. Fund that ETH or the Tether balance on Etherscan cannot be moved. AVAX on the C-Chain is a separate coin.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to DAI on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum.

You spend AVAX, the gas coin on chain 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Leave a remainder for the fee. There is no token approval. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. You receive DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. DAI is Maker's token and uses 18 decimals. It is not Circle and not Tether. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI cannot pay Ethereum gas.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to DAI on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and Maker DAI arrives on mainnet. DAI has 18 decimals, not 6, on Etherscan.

sections.heading: A gas coin for Maker's dollar
sections.body: You give up AVAX exposure and receive a token that holds a dollar peg through Maker, not through Circle or Tether. If a treasury rule names those companies, DAI will not pass. The contract on Etherscan is the test. Eighteen decimals mean the raw transfer integer looks large next to 6 decimal stables you may be used to. Read the human amount.

sections.heading: Do not empty the C-Chain account
sections.body: The fee comes from the AVAX you are also trying to sell. Keep a remainder. The X-Chain balance is invisible to this route. You will not receive AVAX on Ethereum, and you will not receive ETH unless you pick a different output. This page's output is only DAI.

sections.heading: ETH for the second hop of ownership
sections.body: Once DAI is on chain 1, moving it costs ETH. AVAX cannot pay that. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the split between Snowtrace and Etherscan. Twelve second blocks are not the bridge's duration. WBTC is unrelated, and it is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: Refuse the nearby dollars
sections.body: Refuse Circle USDC. Refuse Ethereum Tether. Refuse native ETH and canonical WETH. Refuse a minimum DAI that prices your AVAX worse than you accept. No fill time is offered on this page. Snowtrace shows the AVAX debit, and Etherscan shows the DAI credit, with no shared hash.

faqs.question: Is DAI redeemable at Circle or Tether?
faqs.answer: No. DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is Maker's token, 18 decimals, on Etherscan. Circle redeems USDC. Tether redeems USDT. The asset you sell is native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. If the policy names Circle or Tether, do not sign. DAI is Maker's instrument, checked on Etherscan.

faqs.question: Why is the DAI figure so large on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals. A modest dollar amount becomes a very wide integer in the log. AVAX also uses 18 decimals, and the prices are still unrelated. One AVAX is not one DAI. Read the quote in human units, then confirm the Maker contract on Etherscan before you sign.

faqs.question: What must I leave on the C-Chain?
faqs.answer: Enough AVAX to pay the fee on chain 43114. The X-Chain does not count. Native AVAX is sent, not approved. After arrival you need ETH on Ethereum, because DAI is not gas. Blocks there are about 12 seconds, which does not time the bridge. Bring ETH before you try to send the DAI.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and native ETH arrives on Ethereum.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and they are not the same coin. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114, the placeholder is AVAX, shown on Snowtrace as the account balance. On Ethereum, chain 1, it is ETH, shown on Etherscan as the account balance. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. This is not the X-Chain. It is not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Leave some AVAX for the C-Chain fee. You are changing exposure from AVAX to ether.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and native ETH arrives on mainnet. Each 0xEeee coin differs by chain.

sections.heading: One label, two gas coins
sections.body: Chain id 43114 sells AVAX. Chain id 1 buys ETH. Pasting the placeholder into either explorer does not open a token contract. If the wallet is still on Avalanche while you look for the result, you are watching the coin you sold. Switch to Ethereum before you decide the credit failed. The X-Chain is a third place, and it is the wrong one.

sections.heading: Keep a C-Chain remainder
sections.body: There is no approval on native AVAX. There is a requirement not to spend the entire balance, because the fee is paid in AVAX. WETH is not an input you can substitute. You do not receive WETH. You receive ETH that can pay later mainnet fees, in the amount the quote states, not as a stipend.

sections.heading: Dollars are a different intent
sections.body: USDC, USDT, and DAI are other routes. If the order was any of those, stop. If the order was canonical WETH, stop and wrap after a native ETH delivery, or pick the WETH route instead. [Trade on Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the chain you are buying into. No bridge duration is promised.

sections.heading: How the receipts differ
sections.body: Snowtrace: AVAX down on the C-Chain account. Etherscan: ETH up on the Ethereum account. No token-transfer row is required on either side, because both assets are native. If you see a DAI or USDT transfer, you signed something else. Reject a minimum you dislike.

faqs.question: Why do AVAX and ETH show the same address?
faqs.answer: Interfaces use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for the native gas coin of the selected chain. On the C-Chain that is AVAX. On Ethereum that is ETH. Snowtrace and Etherscan show two account balances. Chain 43114 is not chain 1, and the X-Chain is neither of them. Confirm the wallet network before you search.

faqs.question: Will the ETH I receive pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is the gas coin on chain 1. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The amount is the quote, not a guaranteed surplus after the next transfer. You still had to keep AVAX on the C-Chain to pay for the send. That remainder does not migrate to Ethereum.

faqs.question: Is this the same as receiving WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, an ERC-20. This route delivers native ETH on the account. A pool that accepts only the WETH contract will not see the balance until you wrap it on Ethereum. That wrap is separate and costs a little of the ETH you just received.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and canonical WETH arrives on Ethereum.

Sell AVAX on chain 43114, the gas coin marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Leave a fee. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. There is no ERC-20 approval on AVAX. Receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum, chain 1, on Etherscan. That is canonical WETH. It is not native ETH, so it cannot pay gas. Blocks are about 12 seconds. You need ETH on Ethereum already if you want to unwrap the WETH or send it.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Ethereum. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and canonical WETH arrives on mainnet. WETH cannot pay gas here too.

sections.heading: AVAX in, wrapped ether out
sections.body: You are not bridging AVAX as a token on Ethereum. You are selling it for canonical WETH. Mainnet apps that call 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 will see the credit. Apps that want native ETH will not, until you unwrap. Unwrapping needs ETH, and this route did not deliver the gas coin. Fund a little ETH on chain 1 before you depend on that step.

sections.heading: The C-Chain fee still comes first
sections.body: If you type the entire AVAX balance, the send cannot pay itself. The X-Chain balance does not count. There is nothing to approve, because AVAX is native. If the wallet asks for a token allowance, you are not on this route. Recheck the asset line before you sign.

sections.heading: Dollars and the other WETH deployments
sections.body: USDC, USDT, and DAI are different finishes. WETH on Base at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is a different contract on a different chain. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the handoff from Snowtrace to Etherscan. Twelve second blocks are not a bridge timer. WBTC is not this asset and is not native bitcoin.

sections.heading: A correct look at the result
sections.body: Etherscan should show WETH at the canonical contract, not a rise in the native ETH line. Snowtrace should show AVAX down on chain 43114. If the minimum WETH is too small, do not sign. No duration is promised between those two pages.

faqs.question: Will this WETH pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Canonical WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. Gas is native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain 1. You need some ETH before you can unwrap. AVAX from the C-Chain does not fill that gap. Blocks are about 12 seconds after the fee is paid, and that is not the bridge wait.

faqs.question: Is the source the X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. You sell native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114, which Snowtrace shows as the account balance. The X-Chain and the P-Chain are different. There is no token approval on AVAX. Leave enough for the fee or the transaction cannot be broadcast. Snowtrace, not the X-Chain, is where that AVAX sits.

faqs.question: I wanted native ETH, not the wrapper. What now?
faqs.answer: Do not sign this page. The route that delivers native ETH keeps the gas coin as the gas coin. This one delivers WETH. If you already need WETH for a mainnet pool, the contract above is the right arrival, and you still must bring ETH separately to move it.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and 18 decimal USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

Send 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals, on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows it. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain and not USDC.e. Receive 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, chain 56. BscScan should show 18 decimals. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. That token is not Ethereum's 6 decimal Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Gas after arrival is BNB. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native gas, not this USDT.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and 18 decimal USDT arrives on chain 56. It is not 6 decimal Tether.

sections.heading: Six decimals in, eighteen out
sections.body: A script that divides Avalanche USDC by 1,000,000 will be right for the source and wildly wrong for the destination. BscScan's decimals field on 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 should read 18. The wallet may still show a similar dollar amount. Trust the human figure, then the contract, not a copied Ethereum decoder. The ticker USDT is shared with a different deployment on chain 1.

sections.heading: BNB is not included
sections.body: USDT cannot pay chain 56 fees. AVAX cannot pay them either. The 3 second block time is the chain, not the bridge. Put BNB on the account or the dollars sit on BscScan. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is that fee note. The C-Chain send still needs its own AVAX.

sections.heading: Wrong dollar, wrong chain
sections.body: Wrong if you need Ethereum Tether. Wrong if you need to keep Circle USDC, on Avalanche or as a 6 decimal mainnet token. Wrong if you need BNB itself or pegged ETH. Wrong if you are looking on the X-Chain. The old USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is not the input.

sections.heading: What a clean check is
sections.body: Snowtrace: USDC down at the Circle contract on chain 43114. BscScan: USDT up at the 18 decimal contract. No shared hash. No promised wait. If the minimum is poor, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is this the 6 decimal USDT from Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and uses 6 decimals. This route delivers 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, chain 56, with 18 decimals. Check BscScan. The source is Circle USDC on the C-Chain, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, not the X-Chain. BscScan, not Etherscan, is where this 18 decimal credit belongs.

faqs.question: What pays fees after the USDT arrives?
faqs.answer: BNB, the gas coin on chain 56. USDT cannot. AVAX on chain 43114 cannot. Blocks are about 3 seconds when BNB is available, and that is not a bridge promise. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means BNB only while BNB Chain is selected. AVAX cannot pay those fees.

faqs.question: Should I approve the USDC on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the wallet asks. Circle USDC is an ERC-20 on the C-Chain, so the router needs an allowance paid in AVAX. That signature does not approve anything on BNB Chain. Review the spender and the cap. USDC.e is not this input contract. Match Circle's C-Chain address before you allow the spender.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and pegged ETH arrives as a BEP-20.

Spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Circle's USDC. AVAX pays the send. This is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain, chain 56. BscScan lists it as pegged ETH. It is not native ETH, not WETH, and not gas. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Gas is BNB. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE would mean BNB on this destination, and this route does not deliver it.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and pegged ETH arrives as a BEP-20. It cannot pay gas. BNB is the fee coin.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH cannot run a transaction
sections.body: On Ethereum, ETH pays gas. On BNB Chain, the token at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a peg. You can hold it and trade it. You cannot pay a validator with it. WETH on Ethereum at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a third contract. If someone said get ETH for gas, they meant BNB, and this page will not solve that.

sections.heading: The C-Chain dollar you are selling
sections.body: Native Circle USDC is the input, not USDC.e and not Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Expect an allowance if the router must pull the token, paid in AVAX. An X-Chain wallet will not show this debit. Chain id 43114 has to be selected on the way out.

sections.heading: Where this route is the wrong job
sections.body: Wrong if you wanted native ETH on Ethereum, chain 1, where blocks are about 12 seconds. Wrong if you wanted BNB. Wrong if you wanted USDT. Wrong if you wanted to keep USDC. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers the two explorers. Three second blocks are not a delivery promise. Bring BNB or the pegged token cannot move.

sections.heading: Reading BscScan
sections.body: Open the pegged contract, not the account's BNB line. Snowtrace shows the USDC debit. If the minimum pegged ETH is too small, do not sign. No bridge duration is stated. Chain 56 cannot move the pegged token until BNB is already in the account.

faqs.question: Can I pay BNB Chain fees with this ETH?
faqs.answer: No. 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is pegged ETH, a BEP-20, on BscScan. Gas on chain 56 is BNB. The 0xEeee placeholder means BNB on that chain, and this route does not buy it. You need BNB separately. Blocks are about 3 seconds only after that BNB is available.

faqs.question: Is this the ETH I would get on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum ETH is the gas coin on chain 1, shown on Etherscan as an account balance, with blocks about every 12 seconds. This arrival is a token on BNB Chain. It is also not WETH. If the order says mainnet ETH, leave this page.

faqs.question: Which USDC am I sending?
faqs.answer: Circle's C-Chain USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, on Snowtrace, chain 43114. Not the X-Chain and not USDC.e. AVAX pays the fee. The destination check is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. That token is pegged ETH, not BNB, so the account still needs the gas coin before the token can move.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and native BNB arrives on chain 56.

You spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows that Circle contract. AVAX pays the allowance and the send. This is not the X-Chain. You receive native BNB. Quotes write it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On chain 56 that string means BNB, shown on BscScan as the account balance, not as a token. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is not the result.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and native BNB arrives on chain 56. BNB is the gas coin, not pegged ETH.

sections.heading: You are buying the destination fee coin
sections.body: BNB can pay later transfers on chain 56. The quote sets the amount. It is not a fee budget for a long session. USDC could not pay those fees, which is a common reason to take this hop. If you needed to keep a dollar, you are selling it. Read the minimum before you call the result spare gas.

sections.heading: The placeholder changes with the chain id
sections.body: On the C-Chain, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means AVAX, the coin that pays your send. On BNB Chain it means BNB.
