Searching that string does not open a token page on BscScan. Confirm chain id 56 on the destination before you sign, or you will misread which gas coin you are buying.

sections.heading: Skip it when the order disagrees
sections.body: Skip it for pegged ETH. Skip it for USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Skip it if you need Circle USDC to remain USDC. Skip it if you are on the X-Chain. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing path, not a timer.

sections.heading: Account line, not a token row
sections.body: BscScan's native balance is the arrival. A token transfer of pegged ETH means another route. Snowtrace's USDC debit is the source. Three second blocks are not a bridge promise. Keep AVAX on the C-Chain so the first transaction can be paid. BNB cannot cover that Avalanche fee.

faqs.question: Does 0xEeee here mean AVAX or BNB?
faqs.answer: On the destination it means BNB, the gas coin of chain 56. On the C-Chain the same placeholder means AVAX, which pays the USDC send. It is not a contract on BscScan. Pegged ETH, if that was the order, is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 instead. Chain ids 43114 and 56 keep the coins apart.

faqs.question: Will I receive a BEP-20 called BNB?
faqs.answer: You receive native BNB on the account. BscScan shows that balance, not a token contract. You do not receive pegged ETH, and you do not receive USDT. If a dapp asks for a token address rather than the gas coin, this route has not given it that address.

faqs.question: What do I need on the C-Chain besides USDC?
faqs.answer: AVAX, to pay for the allowance and the send on chain 43114. Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E cannot pay gas. The X-Chain will not show this contract. The BNB you are buying is not on Avalanche yet, so it cannot cover the fee. Fund AVAX on chain 43114 first.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

Send 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, Tether on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Match it on Snowtrace. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BNB Chain, chain 56. That is Binance-pegged USDC with 18 decimals, not Circle's 6 decimal USDC. BscScan is the explorer. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Circle on Avalanche is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and is not what you are sending. BNB is required after arrival. Native gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning AVAX on the source and BNB on the destination.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on BNB Chain. Tether leaves the C-Chain and 18 decimal pegged USDC arrives on chain 56. It is not 6 decimal USDC.

sections.heading: Pegged USDC will miss a Circle whitelist
sections.body: Ethereum and Avalanche Circle contracts use 6 decimals. This BNB Chain token uses 18 and a Binance peg. A treasury file copied from 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 or from 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E will not recognize 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Check decimals on BscScan before you book the credit. The word USDC is not a promise of Circle redemption.

sections.heading: You started in Tether
sections.body: The input is not Circle's C-Chain USDC. If you hold that USDC, this page cannot spend it. Tether's freeze list can still apply to the source token. Bridging does not clear it. An allowance, if requested, is on chain 43114 and costs AVAX.

sections.heading: BNB after the dollars
sections.body: Pegged USDC cannot pay chain 56 fees. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the reminder. Three second blocks are not a bridge clock. Snowtrace records the USDT debit. BscScan records the USDC credit. If the minimum is poor, do not sign. BNB has to sit on chain 56 before those dollars can move.

sections.heading: Other finishes
sections.body: USDT on BNB Chain, native BNB, and pegged ETH are different quotes. Ethereum USDC is a different chain. The X-Chain is the wrong Avalanche network. Stay on this page only when the 18 decimal peg is the contract a BNB Chain app asked for.

faqs.question: Is this the same USDC Circle issues on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Circle on the C-Chain is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and uses 6 decimals. This route spends Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 and delivers 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, an 18 decimal peg, on BscScan. A Circle whitelist will miss it. The peg uses 18 decimals, and Circle's own contracts use 6. Read BscScan before you book the credit.

faqs.question: What pays gas on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: BNB. Pegged USDC cannot. Chain 56 blocks are about 3 seconds when BNB is present. AVAX paid the C-Chain send and does not convert into BNB. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means BNB only on the destination chain. Fund it before you move the dollars. Three second blocks are not a bridge promise.

faqs.question: Does the X-Chain hold this USDT?
faqs.answer: No. The source is C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. The X-Chain and the P-Chain do not hold 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Approve there if asked, and pay AVAX. The credit is on BscScan, chain 56, at the pegged USDC contract. Do not look for it on the X-Chain.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain.

Spend 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on chain 43114. Snowtrace shows that Tether contract. AVAX pays the fee. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain 56. BscScan shows pegged ETH, a BEP-20. It is not native ETH, not WETH, and not BNB. Blocks are about 3 seconds. The gas coin is BNB, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE only when BNB Chain is selected. This route does not deliver that coin.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on BNB Chain. Tether leaves the C-Chain and pegged ETH arrives on chain 56. It cannot pay gas. BNB is the fee coin.

sections.heading: A dollar becomes a peg, not gas
sections.body: You leave Tether and receive a token named ETH that cannot pay BNB Chain fees. If the goal was BNB, stop. If the goal was Ethereum's gas coin, stop. That coin lives on chain 1, with blocks about every 12 seconds, and Etherscan would show it on the account. BscScan will show a token balance instead.

sections.heading: Match Tether before you approve
sections.body: The source address is lowercase-sensitive in the sense that you should paste 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 and not Circle's contract. An allowance costs AVAX. The X-Chain will not list this token. If the wallet is on the wrong Avalanche chain, the balance looks empty and the route is not the problem.

sections.heading: BNB still has to be there
sections.body: Pegged ETH cannot be transferred without BNB. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) does not attach BNB to the credit. Three second blocks are the chain cadence. No bridge duration is promised. If the minimum pegged ETH is weak, do not sign. Pegged ETH is not the gas coin on Ethereum, and chain 1 is a different network.

sections.heading: Nearby contracts that are not this output
sections.body: WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. USDT on BNB Chain is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Native BNB is the account balance. None of those is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Open that address on BscScan or you are inspecting the wrong asset.

faqs.question: Will this ETH pay BNB Chain gas?
faqs.answer: No. The token at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is pegged ETH. Gas is BNB on chain 56, often labeled 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You need that BNB in the account. This route sells C-Chain Tether and does not include the gas coin. Blocks are about 3 seconds after BNB is available.

faqs.question: Is the source Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. The source is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. Circle's USDC is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. The X-Chain does not hold the Tether contract. AVAX pays the send. The pegged ETH you receive still cannot pay BNB Chain fees. Fund BNB on chain 56.

faqs.question: Does this arrive as Ethereum ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum ETH is native on chain 1 and shows on Etherscan as the account balance. This credit is a BEP-20 on BscScan. It is not WETH. If the order named mainnet ETH or BNB, you are on the wrong page. Pegged ETH and native BNB solve different problems.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to BNB on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and native BNB is what arrives.

Sell 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace is the explorer. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Buy native BNB on chain 56, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. BscScan shows the account balance. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a different asset. You are leaving a dollar for the destination gas coin.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to BNB on BNB Chain. Tether leaves the C-Chain and native BNB arrives on chain 56. BNB is the gas coin, not pegged ETH.

sections.heading: Funding chain 56 from Tether
sections.body: BNB pays fees after it arrives. The amount is the quote, not a calculated reserve. A small fill can cover one transfer and not the next. If you needed USDT to remain USDT, this page sells it. Read the minimum BNB against the Tether you give up before you sign.

sections.heading: Two meanings of the same string
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is AVAX on the C-Chain and BNB on BNB Chain. You are not moving one native coin unchanged. You are selling an ERC-20-style dollar for a different chain's gas coin. Confirm chain id 56 in the wallet when you read the output.

sections.heading: Not pegged ETH, not Circle
sections.body: If the app wants 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, switch routes. If you hold Circle USDC rather than this Tether, switch routes. If you are on the X-Chain, switch networks. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the destination. Three second blocks are not a promise.

sections.heading: Receipts
sections.body: Snowtrace shows USDT leaving. BscScan shows BNB on the account, with no token-contract credit required. No shared transaction hash. No stated bridge time. Keep AVAX for the C-Chain fee. Snowtrace records only the C-Chain, BscScan records only BNB, and three second blocks do not say when the bridge finishes. The X-Chain shows neither side. Phantom is irrelevant here. This hop stays on EVM accounts, and BNB is the coin that must arrive before chain 56 will move anything else.

faqs.question: Is the BNB a BEP-20?
faqs.answer: No. It is the native gas coin on chain 56. BscScan shows the account. The quote labels it 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and is not this result. If a contract needs that token address, leave this page. BscScan should show BNB on the account, not inside a token contract.

faqs.question: Which USDT do I spend?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. It is Tether. The X-Chain does not hold it. AVAX pays the send. Circle's USDC on Avalanche is a different contract and will not be pulled by this quote. Confirm the Tether address on Snowtrace before you sign.

faqs.question: Do I still need AVAX if I am buying BNB?
faqs.answer: Yes. BNB is not on Avalanche, so it cannot pay the C-Chain fee. Keep AVAX beside the USDT. Chain 43114 is the source. Blocks on chain 56 are about 3 seconds after the BNB arrives, and that cadence is not the bridge wait. Keep AVAX on the C-Chain until the send is paid.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

You sell the gas coin on chain 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Leave a remainder for the fee. There is no approval on native AVAX. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. You receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, 18 decimal pegged USDC, on BscScan, chain 56. It is not Circle's 6 decimal USDC. Blocks are about 3 seconds. BNB is required to move it. Circle on Avalanche, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, is not the output.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and 18 decimal pegged USDC arrives on chain 56. It is not 6 decimal USDC.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimal peg, not Circle
sections.body: Accounting that assumes 6 decimals will misread this balance. BscScan shows the width. A whitelist built for Circle on Ethereum or on the C-Chain will not match 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. You also sold AVAX, so this is not a dollar-to-dollar hop. You changed exposure from the C-Chain gas coin into a pegged dollar.

sections.heading: Do not drain AVAX
sections.body: The fee and the sold asset are the same coin. Keep a remainder. The X-Chain balance is invisible here. You will not receive AVAX on BNB Chain. You will not receive BNB unless you pick that output instead. This output is only the pegged USDC.

sections.heading: BNB is the next problem
sections.body: The USDC cannot pay chain 56 fees. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) does not deliver BNB alongside it. Three second blocks are not a bridge timer. Snowtrace shows AVAX down. BscScan shows the pegged token up. Decline a weak minimum. Eighteen decimals on this peg will surprise a script written for Circle's 6 decimal USDC, so read BscScan before you book the credit.

sections.heading: Wrong ticker matches
sections.body: Wrong if you need Tether at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Wrong if you need pegged ETH. Wrong if you need native BNB for gas and thought USDC would cover it. Wrong if you meant to keep AVAX.

faqs.question: Is this Circle's USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Circle on the C-Chain is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and uses 6 decimals. This route delivers 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, an 18 decimal peg on BscScan. The source is native AVAX on chain 43114, not that Circle contract. A Circle whitelist will not see the credit. Read the 18 decimal field on BscScan before you report the balance.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX is the gas coin, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and you send it. Leave enough on the C-Chain for the fee. The X-Chain is not this balance. If the wallet asks for a token approval, the selected input is not AVAX. This page sends the gas coin and does not approve it.

faqs.question: Can this USDC pay BNB Chain gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is BNB on chain 56. Pegged USDC cannot pay it. Blocks are about 3 seconds when BNB is in the account. The AVAX you sold does not become BNB. Fund BNB or the dollars sit on BscScan and do not move. Bring BNB before you try again.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and 18 decimal USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

Sell AVAX on chain 43114, placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Keep a fee remainder. No approval on the gas coin. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain 56. BscScan should show 18 decimals. That is not Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, which uses 6. Blocks are about 3 seconds. BNB, not USDT, pays the next fee. C-Chain Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is not the output, because you are selling AVAX, not that token.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and 18 decimal USDT arrives on chain 56. It is not 6 decimal Tether.

sections.heading: The decimal trap, again, from a gas coin
sections.body: You are not moving C-Chain USDT. You are selling AVAX into an 18 decimal dollar on BNB Chain. A decoder built for 6 decimal Tether will mis-state the credit by a huge factor. Read BscScan's decimals field. The human amount on the quote is the figure to accept or reject. AVAX price, not a one-dollar identity, drives the size.

sections.heading: Remainder on the C-Chain
sections.body: Leave AVAX for the fee. The X-Chain does not count. There is nothing to approve. You will not hold AVAX on BNB Chain afterward. If the wallet shows an approval for a token, you selected USDT or USDC by mistake and should back out.

sections.heading: BNB, then the dollars can move
sections.body: USDT cannot pay chain 56. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) states that BNB is mandatory. Three second blocks are not the bridge wait. Snowtrace and BscScan will not share a hash. If the minimum USDT is a poor sale of AVAX, do not sign. The 18 decimal width is the detail a 6 decimal habit will miss on BscScan.

sections.heading: Contracts people paste by habit
sections.body: Ethereum USDT, C-Chain USDT, and this 18 decimal token are three addresses. Pegged USDC is a fourth. Pegged ETH is a fifth. Only 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is the arrival. Open that one on BscScan.

faqs.question: Is this the USDT already on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Avalanche Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. This route sells native AVAX and delivers 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, 18 decimals, on BscScan. Ethereum Tether uses 6 decimals and a different address. The source chain is 43114, the C-Chain, not the X-Chain. Eighteen decimals separate this credit from Ethereum Tether.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX before selling it?
faqs.answer: No. The gas coin is sent, not approved. The placeholder is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Leave enough AVAX on chain 43114 to pay the fee. An approval popup means another asset is selected. This page will not pull a USDT balance as the input. Only native AVAX is sold here.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay fees on arrival?
faqs.answer: No. BNB pays chain 56. USDT cannot. Blocks are about 3 seconds when that BNB is present. AVAX does not convert into BNB. Fund the gas coin or the 18 decimal balance is visible on BscScan and stuck. BNB has to be added before the token can transfer.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain.

Sell AVAX, chain 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Leave a fee. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. There is no token approval. Receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain 56. BscScan shows pegged ETH. It is not native ETH, not WETH, and not BNB. Blocks are about 3 seconds. BNB is the gas coin and is not what this quote buys. Ethereum's gas coin, on chain 1, is also not this token.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to ETH on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and pegged ETH arrives on chain 56. It cannot pay BNB Chain fees.

sections.heading: You did not buy gas on either chain
sections.body: AVAX was the fee coin you sold. Pegged ETH cannot become the fee coin on BNB Chain. BNB can, and you did not buy it. Ethereum ETH can, on chain 1, and you did not buy that either. If the reason for the trade was to pay fees, this page is the wrong output. If a BNB Chain app asked for 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, it is the right one.

sections.heading: Keep AVAX back for the send
sections.body: A full-balance entry fails. The X-Chain balance is not spendable here. No approval is required for native AVAX. If you see an approval, the asset line is wrong. You are changing AVAX exposure into a pegged token, so read the minimum as a price, not as a fee calculation.

sections.heading: WETH is still another contract
sections.body: Canonical WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum. It will not appear on BscScan from this route. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the explorer split. Three second blocks are not a promised arrival. Bring BNB before you try to move the peg.

sections.heading: Dollar routes exist if you wanted them
sections.body: USDT and pegged USDC are different pages. Native BNB is a different page. Staying in AVAX is not a bridge at all. Leave this quote unsigned when the minimum pegged ETH is worse than you accept.

faqs.question: Can pegged ETH pay BNB Chain fees?
faqs.answer: No. 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a BEP-20. Gas is BNB, the native coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain 56. You sold AVAX, which was the C-Chain gas coin, and did not receive BNB. Fund BNB or the pegged token cannot move. Blocks are about 3 seconds after that.

faqs.question: Is this Ethereum ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum ETH is native on chain 1 and shows on Etherscan as the account balance. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. This credit is pegged ETH on BscScan. It is not WETH. The source is AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace, not the X-Chain.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX is sent. Leave a remainder on chain 43114 for the fee. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means AVAX on the source and would mean BNB if you had chosen BNB as the output. This output is the pegged token instead. BNB would have been a different quote.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to BNB on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and native BNB arrives on chain 56.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114, that is AVAX, shown on Snowtrace as the account balance. On BNB Chain, chain 56, that is BNB, shown on BscScan as the account balance. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. This is not the X-Chain. It is not pegged ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Leave some AVAX for the fee. You are swapping one gas coin for another, not moving a single coin unchanged.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to BNB on BNB Chain. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and native BNB arrives on chain 56. Each 0xEeee coin differs by chain.

sections.heading: Chain id is the whole distinction
sections.body: 43114 sells AVAX. 56 buys BNB. The placeholder string is not a contract on either explorer. If the wallet header still says Avalanche, you are looking at the coin you sold. Switch to BNB Chain before you call the credit missing. The X-Chain is a third system and will not show this EVM balance.

sections.heading: Do not spend the last AVAX
sections.body: There is no approval. There is a fee. A max send can fail before a bridge message exists. You do not receive AVAX on BNB Chain. You receive BNB that can pay later fees, in the amount the quote states, not as a long reserve. Read the minimum.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH is the lookalike
sections.body: Orders that say ETH on BNB Chain often mean 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, which cannot pay gas. Orders that say ETH on Ethereum mean chain 1. Orders that say USDT or USDC mean a dollar. [Trade on BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the right note only when BNB itself is the target. Three second blocks are not a bridge promise.

sections.heading: Two account lines
sections.body: Snowtrace: AVAX down. BscScan: BNB up. No token-transfer row is required. If you see a pegged ETH transfer, you used another route. No duration is stated. Reject a quote you would not keep.

faqs.question: Why do AVAX and BNB share an address in the quote?
faqs.answer: They do not share a contract. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means the native gas coin of the selected chain. On the C-Chain that is AVAX. On BNB Chain that is BNB. Snowtrace and BscScan show two account balances. Chain 43114 is not chain 56, and the X-Chain is neither.

faqs.question: Does the BNB I receive pay fees?
faqs.answer: Yes. BNB is the gas coin on chain 56, and blocks are about 3 seconds. The amount is whatever the quote delivers. You still needed leftover AVAX on the C-Chain to pay for the send. That remainder stays on Avalanche. It does not migrate with the trade.

faqs.question: I wanted pegged ETH, not BNB. Is this the page?
faqs.answer: No. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. It cannot pay gas. This page delivers native BNB. If a dapp asked for the pegged contract, switch routes before you sign. The source remains AVAX on the C-Chain, not the X-Chain. Switch routes if the dapp named the pegged ETH contract.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and Tether USDT arrives on Polygon chain 137.

Send 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals, on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows it. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain and not USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. Receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, also 6 decimals, on Polygon. Polygonscan is the explorer. Gas there is POL, not AVAX and not ETH. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL on chain 137. USDT cannot pay it. Native Polygon USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 is not this arrival.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on chain 137. Gas after that is POL on Polygonscan.

sections.heading: Same width, different issuer
sections.body: Six decimals on both legs mean a script will not explode when it changes chains, and the companies are still different. Circle redeems the token you send. Tether redeems the token you receive. If the invoice says Circle on Polygon, the contract is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, and this page will not credit it. Bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is a third miss. Read the address the app displays.

sections.heading: POL is the fee you did not buy
sections.body: AVAX starts the transfer on chain 43114. POL moves USDT on chain 137. Neither dollar pays those fees, and AVAX does not become POL. The old word MATIC is a habit, not a second coin you must approve. If the Polygon account has USDT and no POL, Polygonscan can show the token while the wallet refuses to send it. Fund POL before you depend on a forward transfer.

sections.heading: C-Chain only on the way out
sections.body: The X-Chain and the P-Chain do not hold this USDC. Approve on chain 43114 if the wallet asks, and pay AVAX. [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the destination note. There is no promised bridge time. If the minimum USDT is poor, do not sign. A C-Chain buyer of Circle dollars is a reason to stay home.

sections.heading: Two explorers
sections.body: Snowtrace records the Circle debit. Polygonscan records the Tether credit at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Those hashes are not one transaction. Do not resend because the second page is quiet while the first debit is already final.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the same token as the USDC I sent?
faqs.answer: No. You send Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on the C-Chain, chain 43114. You receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon, which you check on Polygonscan. Both use 6 decimals. Native Polygon USDC is a different contract. Match the issuer before you sign. Polygonscan has to show Tether, not Circle.

faqs.question: What pays gas on Polygon?
faqs.answer: POL, the native coin on chain 137. Quotes may write it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. USDT cannot pay those fees, and AVAX on the C-Chain cannot pay them either. Put POL on the account or the Tether balance sits on Polygonscan and does not move. The X-Chain is not involved.

faqs.question: Does this deliver USDC.e or native USDC?
faqs.answer: Neither. Bridged USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. Native Circle USDC on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. This route delivers Tether. If the app named either USDC contract, pick a different quote and do not sign this one. Tether will not satisfy a USDC deposit screen on Polygon chain 137.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and Polygon WETH arrives on chain 137.

Spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Circle's USDC. AVAX pays the send. This is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon. Polygonscan shows wrapped ether, an ERC-20. It is not POL. POL is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain 137. This route does not buy POL. It is not Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. You need POL already if you want to move the WETH after it lands.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and wrapped ETH arrives on chain 137. WETH cannot pay POL gas there.

sections.heading: Wrapped ether is not the fee coin
sections.body: Polygon apps use 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 when they want ETH exposure inside a token interface. The chain itself is paid in POL. A wallet full of this WETH and empty of POL cannot approve or transfer it. Plan the fee coin separately. Native ETH on Ethereum is a third balance and is not credited here. You also sold a dollar, so ETH price now sits in the result.

sections.heading: Circle in, not Tether, not USDC.e
sections.body: The input is native C-Chain USDC, not 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 and not Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. If you needed to stay in a dollar, Tether on Polygon is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F and native USDC is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. This page leaves the dollar. Read the minimum WETH.

sections.heading: Where the hop is unnecessary
sections.body: If you did not need a Polygon position, do not bridge. If you did, [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the handoff, and you still match both contracts. Snowtrace will not show the WETH. Polygonscan will. No duration is promised. The X-Chain will not show the USDC debit.

sections.heading: POL before the wrapper can move
sections.body: Arriving WETH does not include POL. AVAX used on the C-Chain stays there. Without POL, the credit is visible and idle. If the minimum WETH is too thin for the USDC you sell, do not sign.

faqs.question: Can Polygon WETH pay the next fee?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is an ERC-20. Gas on chain 137 is POL, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in quotes. You need POL already on the account. AVAX spent on the C-Chain does not become that POL. Polygonscan can show WETH the wallet still cannot send. Bring POL before you try.

faqs.question: Is this Ethereum's canonical WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Canonical WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum, chain 1, where blocks are about 12 seconds. This route delivers 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon, which you check on Polygonscan. The source is Circle USDC on the C-Chain, not the X-Chain. AVAX pays that send, and POL pays Polygon.

faqs.question: What if the app wanted POL?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. POL is the gas coin, not the ERC-20 you receive here. Choose the quote that delivers native POL. Staying in USDC, or switching only as far as Tether, is also a different page. Do not sign a WETH minimum if the order was a fee top-up.

intro:
Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to POL on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain, and native POL arrives on Polygon chain 137.

You spend 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Circle's USDC. AVAX pays the allowance and the send. This is not the X-Chain. You receive native POL. Quotes write it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On chain 137 that string means POL, shown on Polygonscan as the account balance, not as a token. It is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and not Tether. You are buying the fee coin.
description: Swap USDC from Avalanche C-Chain to POL on Polygon. Circle USDC leaves the C-Chain and native POL arrives on chain 137. POL is the gas coin, not WETH.

sections.heading: Buying the fee coin with a dollar
sections.body: POL can pay later transactions on Polygon. The quote sets the amount. It is not a stipend for a week of fees. USDC could not pay those fees, which is often why this hop exists. If you only needed a dollar on Polygon, buying POL sells the stable exposure you had. Read the minimum before you treat the result as spare gas. A small fill can disappear into the next few transactions.

sections.heading: The placeholder is POL only on this chain
sections.body: The same 0xEeee string on the C-Chain means AVAX. On Polygon it means POL. Searching it on Polygonscan does not open a token page. If a form shows it as the output while the wallet is on chain 137, you are buying the native coin. Confirm the network before you sign. People still say MATIC. The gas symbol now is POL, and it is the same native balance, not an extra token to approve.

sections.heading: Three assets this page skips
sections.body: It skips Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. It skips native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. It skips WETH. It also skips an X-Chain balance, which cannot fund this route. Use this page when a Polygon account needs the gas coin and you are paying from Circle dollars on the C-Chain.

sections.heading: How the explorers differ
sections.body: Snowtrace records an ERC-20 debit. Polygonscan records a native credit, so you may not see a token transfer on the destination. [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the chain note. No bridge duration is stated. Keep AVAX on the C-Chain for the approval. If the minimum POL is too small, do not sign.

faqs.question: Does 0xEeee on this route mean AVAX or POL?
faqs.answer: On the destination it means POL, the gas coin of chain 137. On the C-Chain the same placeholder means AVAX, which pays the USDC fee. It is not a contract on Polygonscan. WETH, if that was the order, is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Match the chain id before you read the address. The X-Chain is not either side.

faqs.question: Will I receive an ERC-20 called POL?
faqs.answer: You receive native POL on the account balance. There is no token-contract credit to hunt. If a dapp asks for an ERC-20 address rather than the gas coin, this route has not given it that address. Check Polygonscan's native line after the C-Chain USDC debit confirms on Snowtrace.

faqs.question: What do I need beside USDC on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: AVAX, to pay for the allowance and the send on chain 43114. Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E cannot pay gas. The X-Chain will not show this contract. The POL you are buying is not on Avalanche, so it cannot cover that fee. Leave the AVAX in the wallet when you size the swap.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Polygon. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and Circle's native USDC arrives on Polygon.

Send 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, Tether on the C-Chain, chain 43114. Match that address on Snowtrace. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, Circle's native USDC on Polygon, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan. It is not bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. It is not the Tether you sent. Gas on Polygon is POL. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL on chain 137 and AVAX on the C-Chain. USDC cannot pay POL.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Polygon. Tether leaves the C-Chain and native USDC arrives on chain 137. It is not bridged USDC.e. See Polygonscan.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not the bridged copy
sections.body: Polygon still has apps pointed at USDC.e. This quote credits Circle's native contract instead. A deposit button that names 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 will not take the balance. Six decimals will not tell the two apart. Open Polygonscan and compare. You also changed issuer: Tether on the way out, Circle on the way in. A Tether-only rule should stop here.

sections.heading: C-Chain Tether is a specific address
sections.body: Paste 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Circle's C-Chain USDC is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E and will not be pulled. The X-Chain does not hold the Tether contract. An allowance, if the wallet asks, costs AVAX on chain 43114. Tether can freeze listed addresses. The bridge does not clear that status.

sections.heading: POL after the Circle credit
sections.body: USDC cannot pay chain 137 fees. AVAX cannot pay them either. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) separates Snowtrace from Polygonscan and does not name a duration. If the minimum USDC is poor, do not sign. Fund POL or the dollars sit idle.

sections.heading: When the ticker should have stayed
sections.body: If the counterparty asked for Tether on Polygon, the contract is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, and this page is wrong. If they asked for WETH or POL, this page is wrong. If they asked for USDC.e, this page is wrong. It fits when native Circle USDC on Polygon is the balance you meant.

faqs.question: Is this Polygon USDC the bridged USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route delivers Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, which you check on Polygonscan. The source is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, not the X-Chain. If the app displays the bridged address, this credit will not satisfy it. Compare the address on the deposit screen before you sign.

faqs.question: What pays gas after USDC arrives?
faqs.answer: POL on chain 137. USDC cannot pay it. AVAX on chain 43114 cannot pay it. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL while Polygon is selected. Put POL on the account before you try to move the Circle balance. Polygonscan can show the token while the wallet still refuses.

faqs.question: Do I approve USDT on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the wallet asks. Tether on the C-Chain is a token, so the router needs an allowance paid in AVAX. That signature is chain 43114 and does not approve USDC on Polygon. Review the spender. Circle's C-Chain USDC is a different contract and is not the input.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Polygon. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and Polygon WETH arrives on chain 137.

Spend 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Tether. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Receive 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon. Polygonscan shows wrapped ether. It is not POL, and POL is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain 137. It is not Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. You are leaving a dollar for ETH exposure. You still need POL to move the wrapper.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to WETH on Polygon. Tether leaves the C-Chain and Polygon WETH arrives on chain 137. WETH cannot pay POL gas on Polygon.

sections.heading: A dollar sold for wrapped ether
sections.body: Tether uses 6 decimals. WETH uses 18. The log integers will not look like a one-for-one move. Read the human amount. You take ETH price risk. If the order was to remain in a dollar, native USDC on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and this page is the wrong exit. If the order was POL for gas, this page is also wrong.

sections.heading: Which Tether, which chain
sections.body: The source address must be the C-Chain contract, not Ethereum Tether and not Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. The X-Chain will not list it. An allowance costs AVAX. Tether's freeze list can still apply. Bridging from Avalanche does not wash a blocked address on the destination, because the destination is not even Tether.

sections.heading: POL is separate
sections.body: WETH cannot pay chain 137. [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the fee context. No bridge clock is stated. Snowtrace shows USDT down. Polygonscan shows WETH up at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. If the minimum WETH is a bad sale of Tether, do not sign. POL still has to be funded on chain 137 or the wrapper cannot move, and AVAX will not cover that fee.

sections.heading: Canonical mainnet WETH is not hiding here
sections.body: Chain 1 WETH will not increase. Ethereum blocks of about 12 seconds are irrelevant to this credit. If a mainnet pool gave you 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, you are on the wrong route. Polygon's wrapper is a different deployment.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay Polygon fees?
faqs.answer: No. The contract 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is an ERC-20. Gas is POL on chain 137, the 0xEeee placeholder when Polygon is selected. AVAX does not become POL. Fund POL or the WETH sits on Polygonscan. This route spent Tether and did not buy the gas coin. POL has to be funded on its own.

faqs.question: Which USDT leaves Avalanche?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. Not the X-Chain, and not Circle's USDC. AVAX pays the send. The WETH credit is on Polygonscan, not inside the USDT contract you started with. Snowtrace and Polygonscan are separate pages, and the X-Chain is neither of them.

faqs.question: Is this the same WETH as on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. This arrival is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on chain 137. If the app lives on Ethereum, this Polygon wrapper will not satisfy it. Check Polygonscan before you sign. Mainnet WETH will not appear from this hop.

intro:
Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to POL on Polygon. Tether USDT leaves the C-Chain, and native POL arrives on Polygon chain 137.

Sell 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain, chain 43114. Snowtrace shows Tether. AVAX pays the fee. This is not the X-Chain. Buy native POL on Polygon, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Polygonscan shows the account balance, not a token contract. It is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. You are leaving a dollar for the destination gas coin. Circle's Polygon USDC is a different route.
description: Swap USDT from Avalanche C-Chain to POL on Polygon. Tether leaves the C-Chain and native POL arrives on chain 137. POL is the gas coin, not WETH, on Polygon.

sections.heading: Funding Polygon from Tether
sections.body: POL pays fees after it arrives. The amount is the quote, not a calculated reserve. A small fill can cover one transfer and not the next. If you needed USDT to remain USDT, this page sells it. Read the minimum POL against the Tether you give up. The C-Chain fee is still AVAX, which you must keep aside, because POL is not on Avalanche yet.

sections.heading: Two meanings of one string
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is AVAX on the C-Chain and POL on Polygon. You are not moving one native coin unchanged. You are selling Tether for a different chain's gas coin. Confirm chain id 137 when you read the output. The old MATIC label, if the wallet still shows it, is this same native balance.

sections.heading: Not WETH, not Circle
sections.body: If the app wants 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, switch routes. If you hold Circle USDC rather than this Tether, switch routes. If you are on the X-Chain, switch networks. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the sequence. No duration is promised.

sections.heading: Receipts
sections.body: Snowtrace shows USDT leaving. Polygonscan shows POL on the account. No token-contract credit is required for the arrival. No shared hash. Keep AVAX for the C-Chain fee. Decline a minimum you will not accept. Chain 137 will not treat AVAX as gas, so POL is a separate balance.

faqs.question: Is POL an ERC-20 I must approve on arrival?
faqs.answer: No. It is the native gas coin on chain 137. Polygonscan shows the account. The quote labels it 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and is not this result. If a contract needs that token address, leave this page and pick the WETH route. Native POL is only the gas coin.

faqs.question: Which USDT do I spend?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace. It is Tether. The X-Chain does not hold it. AVAX pays the send. Circle's USDC on Avalanche is a different contract and will not be pulled by this quote. Confirm the address before you allow a spender.

faqs.question: Do I still need AVAX if I am buying POL?
faqs.answer: Yes. POL is not on Avalanche, so it cannot pay the C-Chain fee. Keep AVAX beside the USDT. Chain 43114 is the source. Polygon chain 137 is the destination. There is no promised time between the Snowtrace debit and the Polygonscan credit. AVAX still pays the first fee.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Polygon. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and Circle's native USDC arrives on Polygon.

You sell the gas coin on chain 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Leave a remainder for the fee. There is no approval on native AVAX. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. You receive 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan. It is not USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. It is not Tether. POL is required to move it. You do not arrive holding AVAX.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDC on Polygon. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and native USDC arrives on chain 137. It is not bridged USDC.e on Polygon.

sections.heading: Native USDC from a gas-coin sale
sections.body: This is not a dollar-to-dollar hop. You sell AVAX exposure and buy Circle's Polygon USDC. Older apps still want USDC.e. Depositing this credit there will fail. Six decimals describe both USDC contracts, so the integer width will not warn you. Open Polygonscan and match 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 before you tell anyone you paid them in USDC.

sections.heading: Do not empty the C-Chain
sections.body: The fee comes from the AVAX you are selling. Keep a remainder. The X-Chain balance is invisible to this route. You will not receive AVAX on Polygon. You will not receive POL unless you pick that output. This output is only the native USDC, and it cannot pay Polygon fees by itself.

sections.heading: POL is the leftover chore
sections.body: [Trade on Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the reminder that chain 137 uses POL. AVAX does not convert into it. No bridge duration is promised. Snowtrace shows AVAX down. Polygonscan shows USDC up. If the minimum USDC is a poor sale of AVAX, do not sign. POL is still required on Polygon, and the X-Chain will not show this native USDC credit.

sections.heading: Tether would have been another address
sections.body: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F is Polygon Tether. If that was named, leave. WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is another leave. C-Chain USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E is what you are not receiving, because you are not spending USDC.

faqs.question: Is this USDC the bridged USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route delivers 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. The source is native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, not an ERC-20. If the app names the bridged contract, this credit will not match it. Read the deposit address against Polygonscan before you sign.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX?
faqs.answer: No. Native AVAX is sent, not approved. Leave enough on chain 43114 for the fee. The X-Chain does not count. If the wallet asks for a token allowance, you selected USDT or USDC by mistake. This page sells the gas coin only. Snowtrace shows that balance on the account.

faqs.question: What has to sit beside the USDC?
faqs.answer: POL, the gas coin on chain 137. USDC cannot pay fees, and the AVAX you sold does not become POL. Fund POL or Polygonscan shows a Circle balance the wallet will not send. There is no promised time for that credit to appear. POL still has to be added before it can move.

intro:
Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Polygon. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain, and Tether USDT arrives on Polygon chain 137.

Sell AVAX, the gas coin on chain 43114, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows the account. Keep a fee remainder. No approval applies. The C-Chain is not the X-Chain. Receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan. It is not Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and not USDC.e. POL, not USDT, pays the next fee. C-Chain Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is not the output, because you are selling AVAX.
description: Swap AVAX from Avalanche C-Chain to USDT on Polygon. Native AVAX leaves the C-Chain and Tether USDT arrives on chain 137. USDT cannot pay POL gas there.

sections.heading: Selling AVAX into Tether
sections.body: You are not moving the C-Chain USDT contract. You are selling the gas coin for Polygon Tether. The price of AVAX, not a one-for-one dollar identity, sets the size. Tether can freeze addresses on the destination contract. This hop does not clear a freeze. Read the minimum USDT before you accept the trade. Six decimals are the width on Polygonscan, which you should confirm rather than assume from another chain's Tether.

sections.heading: Leave AVAX, ignore the X-Chain
sections.body: A full-balance click can fail because the fee is AVAX. The X-Chain balance will not be spent and will not display the result. There is no ERC-20 approval on native AVAX. If you see an approval, the asset line is a token and this is the wrong page. You will not hold AVAX on Polygon when the swap completes.

sections.heading: POL, or the dollars stay put
sections.body: [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) does not attach POL to the USDT credit. Chain 137 needs that native coin. Snowtrace shows AVAX leaving. Polygonscan shows Tether arriving at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. No shared hash and no promised wait. Decline a minimum you dislike.

sections.heading: Other dollars and other wrappers
sections.body: Native USDC and USDC.e are different arrivals. WETH is a different arrival. POL itself is a different arrival, and it is the one that pays fees. Only this Tether contract is the finish on this page. Open it on Polygonscan before you sign.

faqs.question: Is this the USDT I already hold on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: No. Avalanche Tether is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. This route sells native AVAX and delivers Polygon Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, which you check on Polygonscan. The source is the C-Chain, chain 43114, on Snowtrace, not the X-Chain. The two Tether contracts are not interchangeable. Confirm the Polygon mint address on Polygonscan.

faqs.question: Do I approve AVAX before this swap?
faqs.answer: No. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the C-Chain gas coin, and you send it. Leave enough AVAX on chain 43114 for the fee. An approval request means a token is selected. This page does not pull USDT or USDC as the input. Recheck the asset line before you sign.

faqs.question: Can the USDT pay Polygon fees?
faqs.answer: No. POL pays chain 137. USDT cannot. The AVAX you sold does not reappear as POL. Put POL on the Polygon account or the Tether balance is visible on Polygonscan and stuck. There is no promised time between the two explorers. POL has to be on chain 137 before the USDT can move.
